text: vātasañcayaḥ (वातसञ्चयः; NAMASTE code AAA-1, ICD-11 TM2 SR11): Accumulation of Vata pattern. Category: morbid state of dōṣa (dōṣāvasthā (vāta)). It is characterized by impaired movements of vāta, fullness of abdomen and aversion to factors causing of increase of vāta such as cold. This may be explained by accumulation of vatadosha at the designated site to a moderate level resulting in accumulation. Classical references: Su.Su.21/18.
title: vātasañcayaḥ Accumulation of Vata pattern

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes
text: vātavṛddhiḥ (वातवृद्धिः; NAMASTE code AAA-2, ICD-11 TM2 SR12): Aggravation of vata pattern. Category: morbid state of dōṣa (dōṣāvasthā (vāta)). It is characterized by roughness or hoarseness of voice, emaciation, blackish discoloration of body, twitching in various parts of body, desire for warmth, insomnia, reduced physical strength, hard stools. This may be explained by marked increase of vatadosha functions and consequent physiological and pathological ramifications. Classical references: Su.Su.15/13; Ah.Su.11/6.
title: vātavṛddhiḥ Aggravation of vata pattern

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes
text: vātaprakopaḥ (वातप्रकोपः; NAMASTE code AAA-2.1, ICD-11 TM2 SR10): Vitiation of vāta pattern. Category: Aggravation of vata pattern (vātavṛddhiḥ). It is characterized by abdominal pain and increased gaseous movements in abdomen. This may be explained by aggravation of vatadosha at its designated site and preparing to cause certain morbidity. Classical references: Su.Su.21/20; Ca.Su.20/12; As.Su.19/3.
title: vātaprakopaḥ Vitiation of vāta pattern

text: āvaraṇa (आवृत-वातः/आवरणवात; NAMASTE code AAD, ICD-11 TM2 SR20): Pattern of occlusion. It is characterised by hampering of the normal functioning of the dosha leading to local or systemic symptoms. This may be explained the occlusion of the free flowing and all-pervading Vata dosha or subtype of it by one another or by Pitta, Kapha, tissues, food and excreta.

It is characterized by yellowish discoloration of the body, increased body heat, desire for cold, reduced sleep, loss of consciousness, weakness of body and sense organs, yellowish discoloration of stool, urine and eyes. This may be explained by marked increase of pittadosha functions and consequent physiological and pathological ramifications. Classical references: Su.Su.15/13; As.Su.19/6; Ah.Su.11/7.
title: pittavṛddhiḥ Aggravation of pitta pattern

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes
text: pittaprakopaḥ (पित्तप्रकोपः; NAMASTE code ABA-2.1, ICD-11 TM2 SR15): Vitiation of pitta pattern. Category: Aggravation of pitta pattern (pittavṛddhiḥ). It is characterized by sour eructation, excessive thirst and burning sensation. This may be explained by aggravation of pittadosha at its designated site and preparing to cause certain morbidity. Classical references: Ca.Su.20/15; Su.Su.21/27; As.Su.19/6; Ah.Su.12/52.
title: pittaprakopaḥ Vitiation of pitta pattern

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes
text: pittaprasaraḥ (पित्तप्रसरः; NAMASTE code ABA-3, ICD-11 TM2 SR18): Spreading of pitta pattern. Category: morbid state of dōṣa (dōṣāvasthā (pitta)). It is characterized by localised or whole body burning sensation, feeling of smoky eructation. This may be explained by spreading of pittadosha from place of accumulation to other parts or entire body. Classical references: Su.Su.21/32.
title: pittaprasaraḥ Spreading of pitta pattern

Classical references: Su.Ni.12/9; Ah.U.33/5-6; Ma.Ni.47/2; Sha.Pu.kha.7/82; Bp.Ma.50/2.
title: vātaja-upadaṁśaḥ upadaṁśa due to vāta

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes
text: pittaja-upadaṁśaḥ (पित्तज-उपदंशः; NAMASTE code EI-5.2): upadaṁśa due to pitta. Category: Gonorrhoea disorder (upadaṃśaḥ). The disorder is characterized by jvaraḥ [fever], pakvōḍumbarasaṅkāśa śvayathuḥ/pakvōdumbarasaṅkāśa śvayathuḥ [swelling resemble ripe udumbara/fig fruit], tīvradāhaḥ [severe burning sensation], kṣiprapākaḥ [quick suppuration], pittavēdanā [pain of pitta type - ōśa, cōṣa etc.], bahuklēdaḥ [excessive moistness/soddening], sadāhaḥ [associated with burning sensation]. Classical references: Su.Ni.12/9; Ah.U.33/6; Ma.Ni.47/2; Sha.Pu.kha.7/82; Bp.Ma.50/2.
title: pittaja-upadaṁśaḥ upadaṁśa due to pitta

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes
text: kaphaja-upadaṁśaḥ (कफज-उपदंशः; NAMASTE code EI-5.3): upadaṁśa due to kapha. Category: Gonorrhoea disorder (upadaṃśaḥ). title: kaphaja-upadaṁśaḥ upadaṁśa due to kapha

title: pradeśaḥ

title: prayojanam

title: prasaṅgaḥ

title: yogaḥ

title: vikalpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: vidhānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viparyayaḥ (विपर्ययः; SAT SAT-A.57): antonym. Consideration of the opposite of what is expressed. Category: criteria for critical evaluation of technical texts (tantrayuktiḥ).
title: viparyayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: vyākhyānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśayaḥ (संशयः; SAT SAT-A.59): inconclusive statements. Indefinite statements which leave doubt as to the final and correct opinion. Category: criteria for critical evaluation of technical texts (tantrayuktiḥ).
title: saṁśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samuccayaḥ (समुच्चयः; SAT SAT-A.60): group statement. Words, sentence or paragraphs where in a multitude of things possessing some common property are grouped together and enumerated. Category: criteria for critical evaluation of technical texts (tantrayuktiḥ).
title: samuccayaḥ

title: sambhavaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svasañjñā (स्वसञ्ज्ञा; SAT SAT-A.62): technical terminology. The meaning of certain words which are peculiar to any science wherein they are used in a different sense other than their usual popular meaning. Category: criteria for critical evaluation of technical texts (tantrayuktiḥ).
title: svasañjñā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetvarthaḥ (हेत्वर्थः; SAT SAT-A.63): extension of reasoning from elsewhere. Application of knowledge of one phenomenon happening elsewhere or the extension of a principle enunciated at one place to many other places. Category: criteria for critical evaluation of technical texts (tantrayuktiḥ).
title: hetvarthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vādamārgaḥ (वादमार्गः; SAT SAT-A.64): rules for debate. Technical rules for argument or debate. Category: branch of knowledge (śāstram).
title: vādamārgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: atītakālam (अतीतकालम्; SAT SAT-A.65): failure to make a submission at appropriate moment. When the matter which actually to be said earlier but is said later, and because of delayed presentation become unacceptable. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: atītakālam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ananuyojyam (अननुयोज्यम्; SAT SAT-A.66): unquestionable statement. The statement which does not leave any scope for further questioning. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: ananuyojyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anuyogaḥ (अनुयोगः; SAT SAT-A.67): asking for reason. Enquire something relating to a scripture or a part, a question or a part with a view to testing the knowledge, power of comprehension and expression and capacity to reply to the later. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: anuyogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anuyojyam (अनुयोज्यम्; SAT SAT-A.68): defective statement requiring questioning. The statement which is beset with defects of speech and which requires clarification. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: anuyojyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abhyanujñā (अभ्यनुज्ञा; SAT SAT-A.69): acceptance of situation as it is. Accepting of desired as well as undesired situations. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: abhyanujñā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: arthaprāptiḥ (अर्थप्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-A.70): implied meaning. Unsaid idea conveyed by the said one. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: arthaprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: arthāntaram (अर्थान्तरम्; SAT SAT-A.71): irrelevant statement. Statement which is not relevant to the context. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: arthāntaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uttaram (उत्तरम्; SAT SAT-A.72): rejoinder. Reply. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: uttaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upanayaḥ (उपनयः; SAT SAT-A.73): confirmation of the fact by logical statement which brings the conclusion. Step of discussion and interpretation of hypothesis which bring the argument nearer to the truth which is one of the five steps of establishing statement. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: upanayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upālambhaḥ (उपालम्भः; SAT SAT-A.74): condemnation of reasoning. Censure or reproach; the loop-holing of another's reasons with regard to fallacies and invalid reasoning. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: upālambhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: chalaḥ (छलः; SAT SAT-A.75): deceit. Fraudulent or delusive statements and unmeaning verbosity. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: chalaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jalpaḥ (जल्पः; SAT SAT-A.76): positive discourse, relevant talk, argument. To argue and defend one's own view in a debate. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: jalpaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jijñāsā (जिज्ञासा; SAT SAT-A.77): inquisitiveness. Inquiry or investigation to explore something. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: jijñāsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tadvidyasambhāṣā (तद्विद्यसम्भाषा; SAT SAT-A.78): scientific discussion. Discussion with learned person. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: tadvidyasambhāṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nigamanam (निगमनम्; SAT SAT-A.79): deduction. Deduction or conclusive statement; step of inference for re-establishment of truth. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: nigamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nigrahasthānam (निग्रहस्थानम्; SAT SAT-A.80): stage of defeat. Loopholes of a competitor by which opponent can be defeated in a discussion. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: nigrahasthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parihāraḥ (परिहारः; SAT SAT-A.81): refutation; giving up, abstinence, avoidance. Correcting the defects pointed out in respect of a previous statement. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: parihāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratijñā (प्रतिज्ञा; SAT SAT-A.82): proposition. The statement that has to be proved; the first step of inference and establishment of truth. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: pratijñā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratijñāhāniḥ (प्रतिज्ञाहानिः; SAT SAT-A.83): giving up a proposition or argument. Shift from the original stand; contradiction of one’s own statement being attacked by opponent. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: pratijñāhāniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratiṣṭhāpanā (प्रतिष्ठापना; SAT SAT-A.84): establishing own hypothesis by logically refuting the hypothetical statement of the opponent. Giving a contrary meaning to a given proposition. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: pratiṣṭhāpanā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratyanuyogaḥ (प्रत्यनुयोगः; SAT SAT-A.85): interrogation. Question upon question; cross-examination; leading question(s). Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: pratyanuyogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vākyadoṣaḥ (वाक्यदोषः; SAT SAT-A.86): syntactical defects. A statement with deficiency in any of the five constituents of a sentence and does not convey the proper and complete meaning. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: vākyadoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vākyapraśaṁsā (वाक्यप्रशंसा; SAT SAT-A.87): syntactical excellence. The statement is free from any syntactical impurity and express the exact meaning of the sentence. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: vākyapraśaṁsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vitaṇḍā (वितण्डा; SAT SAT-A.88): hostile debate. Vehemently refuting other's views without considering them. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: vitaṇḍā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyavasāyaḥ (व्यवसायः; SAT SAT-A.89): methodology for assertion. The process by which ascertainment is made. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: vyavasāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthāpanā (स्थापना; SAT SAT-A.90): proving the hypothesis. Justifying a proposition on the basis of reasons, instance, and conclusion. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: sthāpanā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetvantaram (हेत्वन्तरम्; SAT SAT-A.91): irrelevant reasoning. Fallacy of reason: Giving of an irrelevant reasoning instead of relevant reasoning. Category: rules for debate (vādamārgaḥ).
title: hetvantaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: siddhāntaḥ (सिद्धान्तः; SAT SAT-A.92): principle, fundamental truth, scientific theorem. A demonstrated truth established after repeated examinations and reasoning by scientists. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: siddhāntaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmānya-viśeṣa-siddhāntaḥ (सामान्य-विशेष-सिद्धान्तः; SAT SAT-A.93): theory of increase by similar and decrease by dissimilar. An applied principle of āyurveda which is used for maintaining the equilibrium of the body constituent which states that similarity causes increase and dissimilarity causes decrease. Category: principle, fundamental truth, scientific theorem (siddhāntaḥ).
title: sāmānya-viśeṣa-siddhāntaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sarvatantrasiddhāntaḥ (सर्वतन्त्रसिद्धान्तः; SAT SAT-A.94): common theory for all school of thought/scripture/ branches of science. Common theory accepted by school of thought or branches of science. Category: principle, fundamental truth, scientific theorem (siddhāntaḥ).
title: sarvatantrasiddhāntaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratitantrasiddhāntaḥ (प्रतितन्त्रसिद्धान्तः; SAT SAT-A.95): theory particular to a specific school of thought/scripture/ branch of science. The particular doctrine made by some school of thought or science and not accepted by other science. Category: principle, fundamental truth, scientific theorem (siddhāntaḥ).
title: pratitantrasiddhāntaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣaḍ-darśanam (षड्-दर्शनम्; SAT SAT-A.96): six primary schools of philosophy. Six primary schools of philosophy which serve as the theoretical basis of āyurveda viz., saṅkhya, nyāya, vaiṣeṣika, pūrvamīmāṁsa, uttaramīmāṁsa. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: ṣaḍ-darśanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāṁkhyaḥ (सांख्यः; SAT SAT-A.97): philosophy of numerical counting. The philosophy promulgated by maharṣi Kapila, dealing enumeration of basic constituents of the universe; a philosophy to declare the truth properly. Category: six primary schools of philosophy (ṣaḍ-darśanam).
title: sāṁkhyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nyāyaḥ (न्यायः; SAT SAT-A.98): philosophy of epistemology. The branch of philosophy promulgated by maharṣi Goutama dealing with epistemology. Category: six primary schools of philosophy (ṣaḍ-darśanam).
title: nyāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yogaḥ (योगः; SAT SAT-A.99): philosophy deals with union of the soul and the supreme. The branch of philosophy promulgated by maharṣi Pataṅjali dealing with union of the soul and the supreme. Category: six primary schools of philosophy (ṣaḍ-darśanam).
title: yogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vaiśeṣikaḥ (वैशेषिकः; SAT SAT-A.100): philosophy for knowledge of specific features. The branch of philosophy promulgated by maharṣi Kaṇāda dealing with the study of objects of knowledge. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: vaiśeṣikaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pūrvamīmāṁsā (पूर्वमीमांसा; SAT SAT-A.101): philosophy for performance of vedic rituals. The branch of philosophy promulgated by maharṣi Jaimini dealing with performance of vedic rituals. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: pūrvamīmāṁsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uttaramīmāṁsā (उत्तरमीमांसा; SAT SAT-A.102): philosophy for knowledge part of Veda which are known as Upanishad. The branch of philosophy promulgated by maharṣi Vedavyāsa dealing with knowledge part of Veda known as Upanishad. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: uttaramīmāṁsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vādaḥ (वादः; SAT SAT-A.103): doctrine. Thesis, proposition, argument, doctrine. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: vādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: satkāryavādaḥ (सत्कार्यवादः; SAT SAT-A.104): the doctrine which states that the effect is existent in its cause before production. The doctrine which proposes that, the effect is always resides in cause even before its manifestation. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: satkāryavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asatkāryavādaḥ (असत्कार्यवादः; SAT SAT-A.105): the doctrine which states that the effect is non-existent in its cause before production. The doctrine which proposes that, the effect is not present in the cause. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: asatkāryavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anekāntavādaḥ (अनेकान्तवादः; SAT SAT-A.106): theory of uncertainty. Concepts in which invariable causes are given for one effect. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: anekāntavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ārambhavādaḥ (आरम्भवादः; SAT SAT-A.107): theory of spontaneous/ unprompted origin of the universe. The doctrine which proposes that, effect is produced sequentially after the sequential destruction of the cause. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: ārambhavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣaṇabhaṅguravādaḥ (क्षणभङ्गुरवादः; SAT SAT-A.108): theory of continuous decaying. The doctrine which proposes that, nothing is stable or permanent and everything’s undergoes through continuous process of decaying. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: kṣaṇabhaṅguravādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vivartavādaḥ (विवर्तवादः; SAT SAT-A.109): theory of ‘Brahman’ as the only truth. The doctrine of the Vedānta philosophy which proposes that, ‘Brahman’ is the only truth and the rest is illusion. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: vivartavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svabhāvoparamavādaḥ (स्वभावोपरमवादः; SAT SAT-A.110): theory of inevitable natural destruction. The doctrine of the buddhism which believes that natural destruction is inevitable to everything. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: svabhāvoparamavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pariṇāmavādaḥ (परिणामवादः; SAT SAT-A.111): theory of transformation. Doctrine of transformation which states that all the substances get changes continuously. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: pariṇāmavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: piṭharapākavādaḥ (पिठरपाकवादः; SAT SAT-A.112): concept of physical changes. The doctrine which explains about the transformation at physical plane. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: piṭharapākavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pīlupākavādaḥ (पीलुपाकवादः; SAT SAT-A.113): concept of molecular changes. The doctrine which explains about the transformation at molecular level. Category: doctrine (vādaḥ).
title: pīlupākavādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prameyaḥ (प्रमेयः; SAT SAT-A.114): object of knowledge. Object of perceptible knowledge. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: prameyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: padārthaḥ (पदार्थः; SAT SAT-A.115): knowable objects. Entities which exists (astitvam), are knowable (jñeyatvaṁ), and are denoted with a name (abhidheya); the meaning of a word or group of word. Category: object of knowledge (prameyaḥ).
title: padārthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣaṭ-padārthāḥ (षट्-पदार्थाः; SAT SAT-A.116): the six knowable objects. The six knowable objects which are 1. Sāmānya 2. Viśeṣa 3. Guṇa 4. Dravya 5. Karma and 6. Samavāya. Category: knowable objects (padārthaḥ).
title: ṣaṭ-padārthāḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmānya (सामान्य/तुल्यार्थता; SAT SAT-A.117): similarity/generality. Also called tulyārthatā. 1. the attribute which always adds-up/ increases 2. that is which establishes unity 3. an attribute that is having a similar motive (tulyārthata); 4. one that is eternal, one in number and resides in various places. Category: the six knowable objects (ṣaṭ-padārthāḥ).
title: sāmānya tulyārthatā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dravya-sāmānyam (द्रव्य-सामान्यम्; SAT SAT-A.118): similarity at the level of substance. Similar substances e.g. human flesh having similarities with animal flesh, and which can nourish muscle tissue. Category: similarity/generality (sāmānya).
title: dravya-sāmānyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guṇa-sāmānyam (गुण-सामान्यम्; SAT SAT-A.119): similarity at the level of qualities. Similarity between qualities e.g. seminal tissue (śukra) and milk have similar qualities. Category: similarity/generality (sāmānya).
title: guṇa-sāmānyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karma-sāmānyam (कर्म-सामान्यम्; SAT SAT-A.120): similarity at the level of action. Action adding up to increase of certain entity e.g., sleep increasing kaphadoṣa. Category: similarity/generality (sāmānya).
title: karma-sāmānyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viśeṣaḥ (विशेषः; SAT SAT-A.121): dissimilarity; particularity. Attribute that causes depletion/decrease (hrāsahetu); that causes diversity (pṛthaktva) opposite to that of similarity (sāmānya); the one, which resides in eternal draya and differentiates one from the other. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: viśeṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dravya-viśeṣaḥ (द्रव्य-विशेषः; SAT SAT-A.122): dissimilarity at the level of substance. A substance which on consumption/ usage can deplete particular substance. Category: dissimilarity; particularity (viśeṣaḥ).
title: dravya-viśeṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guṇa-viśeṣaḥ (गुण-विशेषः; SAT SAT-A.123): dissimilarity at the level of qualities. Qualities acting opposite to each other resulting in depletion of one of them e.g., vāta getting pacified with usage of sesame oil by virtue of its opposite qualities. Category: dissimilarity; particularity (viśeṣaḥ).
title: guṇa-viśeṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karma-viśeṣaḥ (कर्म-विशेषः; SAT SAT-A.124): dissimilarity at the level of action. An activity which causes depletion/ reduction e.g. physical exercise reducing kaphadoṣa, which otherwise is increased with inactivity. Category: dissimilarity; particularity (viśeṣaḥ).
title: karma-viśeṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guṇaḥ (गुणः; SAT SAT-A.125): attribute/ property. Quality of a substance; it is an inseparable entity with substance (dravya); guṇa is devoid of any action on its own, however guṇa is responsible for action through dravya. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: guṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: triguṇāḥ (त्रिगुणाः/महागुणः; SAT SAT-A.126): three primary attributes. Also called mahāguṇaḥ. Three chief principle attributes; indicative of three mental attributes (sattva, rajas and tamas). Category: attribute/ property (guṇaḥ).
title: triguṇāḥ mahāguṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sattvam (सत्त्वम्; SAT SAT-A.127): purity or goodness. One among the three qualities (sattva, rajas and tamas) which is characterized by lightness, knowledge and enlightenment. Category: three primary attributes (triguṇāḥ).
title: sattvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rajaḥ (रजः; SAT SAT-A.128): passion. One among the three qualities (sattva, rajas and tamas) which is characterized by activity, initiation, action and attachment. Category: three primary attributes (triguṇāḥ).
title: rajaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tamaḥ (तमः; SAT SAT-A.129): delusion, ignorance. One among the three qualities (sattva, rajas and tamas) which is characterized by darkness and ignorance. Category: three primary attributes (triguṇāḥ).
title: tamaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sārthaguṇaḥ (सार्थगुणः/वैशेषिक-गुणः; SAT SAT-A.130): objects of cognition. Also called vaiśeṣika-guṇaḥ. Objects of sensory perception. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: sārthaguṇaḥ vaiśeṣika-guṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gandhaḥ (गन्धः; SAT SAT-A.131): smell. Elemental character responsible for smell of a substance; trait of pṛthvimahābhūta. Category: objects of cognition (sārthaguṇaḥ).
title: gandhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasaḥ (रसः; SAT SAT-A.132): taste. Elemental character responsible for taste of a substance; trait of jalamahābhūta. Category: objects of cognition (sārthaguṇaḥ).
title: rasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rūpaḥ (रूपः; SAT SAT-A.133): appearance/ visual form. Elemental character responsible for perceivable form by sight; trait of agnimahābhūta. Category: objects of cognition (sārthaguṇaḥ).
title: rūpaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: varṇaḥ (वर्णः; SAT SAT-A.134): colour. 1. colour 2. complexion; trait of agniamahābhūta. Category: objects of cognition (sārthaguṇaḥ).
title: varṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sparśaḥ (स्पर्शः; SAT SAT-A.135): touch. Elemental character responsible for touch an substance; trait of vayumahābhūta. Category: objects of cognition (sārthaguṇaḥ).
title: sparśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śabdaḥ (शब्दः; SAT SAT-A.136): sound. Elemental character responsible for sound, word; trait of ākāśamahābhūta; also denotes authoritative text (āgama). Category: objects of cognition (sārthaguṇaḥ).
title: śabdaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śārīra-guṇāḥ (शारीर-गुणाः/गुर्वादि-गुणाः; SAT SAT-A.137): physical attributes. Also called gurvādi-guṇāḥ. Properties of substances that relates with the body; extensively used for the selection/ preparing formulae and employing successfully. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: śārīra-guṇāḥ gurvādi-guṇāḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guruḥ (गुरुः; SAT SAT-A.138): heaviness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for nourishment (bṛṁhaṇa) e.g. black gram (māṣa). Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: guruḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: laghuḥ (लघुः; SAT SAT-A.139): lightness. The quality of a substance which promotes lightness and decreases the bulk of the body e.g., green gram (mudga). Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: laghuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mandaḥ (मन्दः; SAT SAT-A.140): mildness/slowness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for the slow activity or delayed response e.g. guḍūci, āmalaki. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: mandaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tīkṣṇaḥ (तीक्ष्णः; SAT SAT-A.141): sharpness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for quick activity e.g. bhallātaka, marica, dantī. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: tīkṣṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śītaḥ (शीतः; SAT SAT-A.142): coldness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for promoting coldness, promotes stiffness (staṁbhana) and acts as styptic or astringent e.g., uśīra, candana. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: śītaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uṣṇaḥ (उष्णः; SAT SAT-A.143): hotness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for promoting sweating, softening/ ripening (pāka) e.g. citraka, cavya. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: uṣṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: snigdhaḥ (स्निग्धः; SAT SAT-A.144): sliminess/unctuousness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for imparting smoothness, moisture and oily nature to the body e.g. ghṛta. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: snigdhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rūkṣaḥ (रूक्षः; SAT SAT-A.145): dryness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for dryness or which results in absorption of moisture. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: rūkṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ślakṣṇaḥ (श्लक्ष्णः; SAT SAT-A.146): slippery/ smoothness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for wound healing e.g. haridrā, abhraka. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: ślakṣṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kharaḥ (खरः; SAT SAT-A.147): roughness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for reducing corpulence e.g. vacā, śilajatu. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: kharaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāndraḥ (सान्द्रः; SAT SAT-A.148): thickness/ density/ viscidity. The quality of a substance which is responsible for gratifying/ satisfying effect. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: sāndraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dravaḥ (द्रवः; SAT SAT-A.149): fluidity. The quality of a substance which is responsible for stirring up/ churning (viloḍana) and moistening. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: dravaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mṛduḥ (मृदुः; SAT SAT-A.150): softness/ mildness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for bringing about softness or fragility e.g. godhuma, eraṇdataila, yaṣṭhimadhu. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: mṛduḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṭhinaḥ (कठिनः; SAT SAT-A.151): hardness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for firmness/ hardness e.g. aśvagandha, śatāvarī, pravāla. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: kaṭhinaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sūkṣmaḥ (सूक्ष्मः; SAT SAT-A.152): minuteness/penetrating. The quality of a substance which is responsible for spreading out/ penetration e.g. madhu, saindhava etc. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: sūkṣmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthūlaḥ (स्थूलः; SAT SAT-A.153): grossness/bulkiness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for closure/ concealment, bulkiness e.g. curd (dadhi). Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: sthūlaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthiraḥ (स्थिरः; SAT SAT-A.154): stability/immobility. The quality of a substance which is responsible for concentration/ immobility/ strength to the body and especially to hair, moustache, bones, nails, teeth etc. e.g. balā, atibalā, godhūma. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: sthiraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saraḥ (सरः/ चलः; SAT SAT-A.155): instability/mobility. Also called calaḥ. The quality of a substance which is responsible for movement/ stimulation (preraṇa), normal movements such as peristalis. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: saraḥ calaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viśadaḥ (विशदः; SAT SAT-A.156): conspicuousness. The quality of a substance which is responsible for cleaning and help tissues free from vitiated substances e.g. niṁba, māṁsarohiṇi. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: viśadaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: picchilaḥ (पिच्छिलः; SAT SAT-A.157): sliminess. The quality of a substance which is responsible for coating effect over the tissues eg. kumārī, mocarasa. Category: physical attributes (śārīra-guṇāḥ).
title: picchilaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ātmaguṇaḥ (आत्मगुणः; SAT SAT-A.158): attributes/ property of atma. Attributes of soul (ātma) viz., buddhi (intelligence), sukha (pleasure), duḥkha (sorrow), icchā (desire, dveṣa (aversion) and prayatna (initiation). Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: ātmaguṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: buddhiḥ (बुद्धिः; SAT SAT-A.159): intelligence. The power of forming and retaining conceptions and general notions, intelligence, reason, intellect, discernment, judgment. Category: attributes/ property of atma (ātmaguṇaḥ).
title: buddhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sukham (सुखम्; SAT SAT-A.160): pleasure. Favourable perception including happiness, delight, joy, pleasure. Category: attributes/ property of atma (ātmaguṇaḥ).
title: sukham

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: duḥkham (दुःखम्; SAT SAT-A.161): sorrow. Unfavourable perception including unhappiness, sorrow, grief. Category: attributes/ property of atma (ātmaguṇaḥ).
title: duḥkham

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: icchā (इच्छा; SAT SAT-A.162): desire. Desired attributes produced from seeking of pleasure. Category: attributes/ property of atma (ātmaguṇaḥ).
title: icchā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dveṣaḥ (द्वेषः; SAT SAT-A.163): aversion. Aversion - one among the suppressible urges. Category: attributes/ property of atma (ātmaguṇaḥ).
title: dveṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prayatnaḥ (प्रयत्नः; SAT SAT-A.164): initiation. The quality through which stimulus for useful activity is obtained. Category: attributes/ property of atma (ātmaguṇaḥ).
title: prayatnaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parādiguṇaḥ (परादिगुणः; SAT SAT-A.165): qualities beginning with paratva. Group of ten properties commencing with paratva; often used in for analytical purposes and decision making. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: parādiguṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: paratvam (परत्वम्; SAT SAT-A.166): relatively superior. Priority or superiority of a substance over the other innumerable substances. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: paratvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aparatvam (अपरत्वम्; SAT SAT-A.167): relatively inferior. Inferiority of substance over the other innumerable substances. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: aparatvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁkhyā (संख्या; SAT SAT-A.168): number/enumeration/count. The quality which enables us to quantify/ calculate. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: saṁkhyā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁyogaḥ (संयोगः; SAT SAT-A.169): combination. Combination of two or more than two substances. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: saṁyogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vibhāgaḥ (विभागः; SAT SAT-A.170): division. Division of a particular substance. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: vibhāgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pṛthaktvam (पृथक्त्वम्; SAT SAT-A.171): separation or exclusion; particularity. The quality by which one substance is differentiated or separated from the other. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: pṛthaktvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parimāṇaḥ (परिमाणः; SAT SAT-A.172): quantity/ measurement. The quality by which measurement of various substances is possible. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: parimāṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yuktiḥ (युक्तिः; SAT SAT-A.173): logical management. An activity as per plan/ scheme by logic i.e. rational plan. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: yuktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁskāraḥ (संस्कारः; SAT SAT-A.174): alter/transform. The process through which some change/ transformation is brought to the original properties of any substance. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abhyāsaḥ (अभ्यासः; SAT SAT-A.175): practice. Getting used to/ repetitive action leading to development of a habit. Category: qualities beginning with paratva (parādiguṇaḥ).
title: abhyāsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dravyam (द्रव्यम्; SAT SAT-A.176): substance. An entity encompassing the attributes of quality and action. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: dravyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāraṇadravyam (कारणद्रव्यम्; SAT SAT-A.177): causative substances. Elementary substances that are said to be the cause of manifestation of all other substances; nine in number. Category: substance (dravyam).
title: kāraṇadravyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ (मूर्तद्रव्य-परमाणुः; SAT SAT-A.178): substances having form. Perceptible substances; tangible source substances; also denoted by: settled into any fixed shape, formed, substantial, material, embodied, incarnate. Category: causative substances (kāraṇadravyam).
title: mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pṛthvī (पृथ्वी; SAT SAT-A.179): earth element. An entity which is responsible for hardness. Category: substances having form (mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ).
title: pṛthvī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jalam (जलम्; SAT SAT-A.180): water element. An entity which is responsible for fluidity. Category: substances having form (mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ).
title: jalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tejaḥ (तेजः; SAT SAT-A.181): fire element. An entity which is responsible for heat. Category: substances having form (mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ).
title: tejaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāyuḥ (वायुः; SAT SAT-A.182): air element. An entity which is responsible for movement. Category: substances having form (mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ).
title: vāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: manaḥ (मनः; SAT SAT-A.183): mind, psyche. The faculty through which indriya (cognitive organs) connect with the ātman (soul). Category: substances having form (mūrtadravya-paramāṇuḥ).
title: manaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antaḥkaraṇam (अन्तःकरणम्; SAT SAT-A.184): internal sense faculties. Internal system of perception and cognition; it is inclusive of manas (mind); buddhi (intelligence); indriya (cognitive organs); ahaṁkāra (ego). Category: mind, psyche (manaḥ).
title: antaḥkaraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cetaḥ (चेतः; SAT SAT-A.185): consciousness. Synonym of mind, denotes consciousness. Category: mind, psyche (manaḥ).
title: cetaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mano guṇaḥ (मनो गुणः/स्वरूपम्; SAT SAT-A.186): features of mind. Also called svarūpam. The features of manas (mind) viz., aṇutva: (minuteness); ekatva (oneness). Category: mind, psyche (manaḥ).
title: mano guṇaḥ svarūpam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṇutva (अणुत्व; SAT SAT-A.187): minuteness. Having dimension of a paramāṇu i.e. minute entity. Category: features of mind (mano guṇaḥ).
title: aṇutva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ekatva (एकत्व; SAT SAT-A.188): oneness. Being only one in number i.e. there is no possibility of any other entity which functions like manas in the body. Category: features of mind (mano guṇaḥ).
title: ekatva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mano-arthaḥ (मनोऽर्थः; SAT SAT-A.189): activities of mind. The functions of mind viz., thought, analysis, contemplation, mediation and volition. Category: mind, psyche (manaḥ).
title: mano-arthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cintyaḥ (चिन्त्यः; SAT SAT-A.190): that which is thought upon. It is the consideration about worth doing or otherwise. Category: activities of mind (mano-arthaḥ).
title: cintyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vicāryaḥ (विचार्यः; SAT SAT-A.191): that which is analyzed. It is a critical analysis with reasoning about happening or non-happening. Category: activities of mind (mano-arthaḥ).
title: vicāryaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūhyaḥ (ऊह्यः; SAT SAT-A.192): that which is contemplated upon. It is a process of proposing possible deduction after analysis. Category: activities of mind (mano-arthaḥ).
title: ūhyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhyeyaḥ (ध्येयः; SAT SAT-A.193): that which is meditated/pondered upon. An objective to be pondered over. Category: activities of mind (mano-arthaḥ).
title: dhyeyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṅkalpaḥ (सङ्कल्पः; SAT SAT-A.194): to intend/ volition. Developing a dogmatic attitude; a goal determined with its merits and demerits. Category: activities of mind (mano-arthaḥ).
title: saṅkalpaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mānasika-bhāvaḥ (मानसिक-भावः; SAT SAT-A.195): psychological/mental attributes. Category: mind, psyche (manaḥ).
title: mānasika-bhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhīḥ (धीः; SAT SAT-A.196): understanding. Denotes understanding; intelligence; wisdom. Category: psychological/mental attributes (mānasika-bhāvaḥ).
title: dhīḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhṛtiḥ (धृतिः; SAT SAT-A.197): retaining power of mind. Power of retention/ resolution; stable, controlling intellect. Category: psychological/mental attributes (mānasika-bhāvaḥ).
title: dhṛtiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: smṛtiḥ (स्मृतिः; SAT SAT-A.198): memory/ reminiscence/ recollection. Rembrance of the things directly perceived, heard (scriptures) or explained earlier. It is the result from a particular conjunction between the soul and mind and also from impression. Category: psychological/mental attributes (mānasika-bhāvaḥ).
title: smṛtiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣaḍripuḥ (षड्रिपुः; SAT SAT-A.199): six inner foes or faults. Six mental attributes that lead to bondage of the soul viz., desire, anger, greed, delusion arrogance and jealousy. Category: psychological/mental attributes (mānasika-bhāvaḥ).
title: ṣaḍripuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāmaḥ (कामः; SAT SAT-A.200): desire. Desire or of love or of pleasure; also one among the four puruṣārtha (goals of life). Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: kāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: krodhaḥ (क्रोधः; SAT SAT-A.201): anger. Also denoted by wrath, passion. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: krodhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lobhaḥ (लोभः; SAT SAT-A.202): greed. Insatiable desire for having something; excessive desire to acquire more than need. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: lobhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mohaḥ (मोहः; SAT SAT-A.203): delusion. Confused state of mind that doesn’t lead to correct perception. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: mohaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: madaḥ (मदः; SAT SAT-A.204): arrogance. State of being emotionally aroused and worked up. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: madaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mātsaryam (मात्सर्यम्; SAT SAT-A.205): jealousy. Intolerance to the good of others/negative competitiveness. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: mātsaryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ahaṅkāraḥ (अहङ्कारः; SAT SAT-A.206): pride, haughtiness; self-consciousness. Denotes the negative roll of pride, haughtiness; also one of the principles of the evolution in the sense of conception of one's individuality, self-consciousness. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: ahaṅkāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: damaḥ (दमः; SAT SAT-A.207): self restraint. Also denoted by: self-command, self-control. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: damaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhaktiḥ (भक्तिः; SAT SAT-A.208): devotion; natural inclination. A natural inclination or fondness for something; that which belongs to or is contained in anything else, an attribute. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: bhaktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lajjā (लज्जा; SAT SAT-A.209): shame. Also denoted by: modesty, bashfulness, embarrassment. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: lajjā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vinayaḥ (विनयः; SAT SAT-A.210): humility. Also denoted by: propriety of conduct, decency, modesty, mildness. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: vinayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vivekaḥ (विवेकः; SAT SAT-A.211): discriminatory wisdom. The faculty of distinguishing and classifying things according to their absolute properties. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: vivekaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śokaḥ (शोकः; SAT SAT-A.212): grief/sorrow/misery. A state of ill-being due to loss of children or affliction or misfortune. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: śokaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sammohaḥ (सम्मोहः; SAT SAT-A.213): illusion. Also denoted by: deluding, infatuating, leading astray. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: sammohaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: alobhaḥ (अलोभः; SAT SAT-A.214): freedom from infatuation. Also denoted by: freedom from perplexity, confusion. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: alobhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: darpaḥ (दर्पः; SAT SAT-A.215): pride. Also denoted by: arrogance, haughtiness, insolence, conceit. Category: six inner foes or faults (ṣaḍripuḥ).
title: darpaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: amūrtadravyam (अमूर्तद्रव्यम्; SAT SAT-A.216): not having form/all pervading. Not settled into any fixed shape, form, substance or material. Category: causative substances (kāraṇadravyam).
title: amūrtadravyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ākāśaḥ (आकाशः; SAT SAT-A.217): ether/space element. An attribute of a substance characterised by non-obstruction. Category: not having form/all pervading (amūrtadravyam).
title: ākāśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ātmā (आत्मा; SAT SAT-A.218): soul. Soul or spirit: principle of life and sensation, the individual self; the only conscious element in the human body. Category: not having form/all pervading (amūrtadravyam).
title: ātmā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhūtātmā (भूतात्मा; SAT SAT-A.219): individual soul. The soul in association with the living body. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: bhūtātmā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jīvaḥ (जीवः; SAT SAT-A.220): living being/soul. Living being. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: jīvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jñaḥ (ज्ञः; SAT SAT-A.221): perceiver of knowledge. Perceiver of knowledge: soul. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: jñaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kartā (कर्ता; SAT SAT-A.222): subject, person. In this context it denotes soul. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: kartā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sākṣī (साक्षी; SAT SAT-A.223): witness to all actions. Ātma does not actively participate in any action, it merely performs the duty of a witness. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: sākṣī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ādhyātmika (आध्यात्मिक; SAT SAT-A.224): relating to self. Relating to self or to the soul. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: ādhyātmika

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ativāhika-śarīram (अतिवाहिक-शरीरम्/ सूक्ष्म-शरीरम्/ लिङ्ग-शरीरम्; SAT SAT-A.225): subtle body. Also called sūkṣma-śarīram and liṅga-śarīram. The subtle body which consist of manas: mind, indriya: organs and atma: soul, devoid of gross body; causal body; subtle body. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: ativāhika-śarīram sūkṣma-śarīram liṅga-śarīram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: puruṣaḥ (पुरुषः; SAT SAT-A.226): person/ living being. The personal and animating principle in men and other beings, the soul or spirit. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: puruṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avyaktam (अव्यक्तम्; SAT SAT-A.227): un-manifested state. Unmanifestated state, unapparent, indistinct, invisible, imperceptible. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: avyaktam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vaśī (वशी; SAT SAT-A.228): controller. Absolutely autonomous; having no control by others. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: vaśī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cikitsya-puruṣaḥ (चिकित्स्य-पुरुषः; SAT SAT-A.229): person as the object of treatment. Person as the object of treatment, consisting of five mahābhūta and ātma. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: cikitsya-puruṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: caturviṁśati-puruṣaḥ (चतुर्विंशति-पुरुषः; SAT SAT-A.230): conglomerate of24 elements. Body composed of 24 elements viz., five mahābhūta, the five organs of sense, five organs of action, five tanmātra, avyakta, buddhi, ahaṁkāra and manas. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: caturviṁśati-puruṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adṛṣṭam (अदृष्टम्; SAT SAT-A.231): invisible, unforeseen. Also denoted by: not experienced, unobserved, unknown, unsanctioned; the invisible result of works done in former states of embodied existence; unseen consequences of an act. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: adṛṣṭam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: indriyāntara-sañcāraḥ (इन्द्रियान्तर-सञ्चारः; SAT SAT-A.232): trans-sense migration. Rapid conjugation of mind with sensory or motor organs. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: indriyāntara-sañcāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: niṣkriyaḥ (निष्क्रियः; SAT SAT-A.233): inactive. Inactiveness of ātma, indicating its principle quality of staying as a mere witness to what is happening. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: niṣkriyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vibhu (विभु; SAT SAT-A.234): omnipresent. Being everywhere, all pervading, an attribute of ātma. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: vibhu

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anādi (अनादि; SAT SAT-A.235): having no beginning. A process or state whose beginning cannot be ascertained. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: anādi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anityam (अनित्यम्; SAT SAT-A.236): non- eternal or transient. Not everlasting, transient, occasional, incidental. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: anityam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cetanā (चेतना/ चैतन्यम्; SAT SAT-A.237): consciousness. Also called caitanyam. Awareness. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: cetanā caitanyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nityam (नित्यम्; SAT SAT-A.238): eternal. Everlasting, all time existence; innate, native. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: nityam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirvikāram (निर्विकारम्; SAT SAT-A.239): formless. The quality of soul which is devoid of all bodily and psychological ailments. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: nirvikāram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prākāmyam (प्राकाम्यम्; SAT SAT-A.240): irresistible will. The power of having an irresistible will, one of the supra normal psychic power derivable from the practice of yoga. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: prākāmyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avyayaḥ (अव्ययः; SAT SAT-A.241): not liable to change. Imperishable. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: avyayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: draṣṭā (द्रष्टा; SAT SAT-A.242): observer of all actions. Synonym of ātmā. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: draṣṭā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svatantra (स्वतन्त्र; SAT SAT-A.243): independent. Autonomous; an attribute of ātmā. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: svatantra

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antaścetana (अन्तश्चेतन; SAT SAT-A.244): internally conscious. Living beings having internal consciousness i.e. their consciousness is not externally manifested; e.g. plants. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: antaścetana

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mokṣaḥ (मोक्षः; SAT SAT-A.245): salvation. Liberation, cessation from worldly existence or transmigration, the fourth puruṣārtha (goal of life). Category: soul (ātmā).
title: mokṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: satyabuddhiḥ (सत्यबुद्धिः; SAT SAT-A.246): true knowledge. State of self-realization of ultimate reality. It eliminates all miseries and leads to liberation. It results in the emergence of true knowledge by which the soul transcends the ego and all worldly miseries come to an end. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: satyabuddhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jīvanamuktiḥ (जीवनमुक्तिः; SAT SAT-A.247): attaining eternal salvation. Attaining salvation while one is alive or in the exiting birth itself. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: jīvanamuktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: puṣpitaḥ (पुष्पितः; SAT SAT-A.248): signs of approaching death. Person having fatal prognostic symptoms. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: puṣpitaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pretya (प्रेत्य; SAT SAT-A.249): after death. Abode of soul after death. Category: soul (ātmā).
title: pretya

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālaḥ (कालः; SAT SAT-A.250): time. One among the nine kāraṇa dravya. Category: not having form/all pervading (amūrtadravyam).
title: kālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: diśaḥ (दिशः; SAT SAT-A.251): direction. Arbitrary divisions of space. Category: not having form/all pervading (amūrtadravyam).
title: diśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāryadravyam (कार्यद्रव्यम्; SAT SAT-A.252): effectual substances. Effectual substances that are manifestations of the nine causal substances. Category: substance (dravyam).
title: kāryadravyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cetana-dravyam (चेतन-द्रव्यम्/ सेन्द्रियः; SAT SAT-A.253): sentient. Also called sendriyaḥ. Animate substances; substances having consciousness like plants, animals. Category: effectual substances (kāryadravyam).
title: cetana-dravyam sendriyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthāvaraḥ (स्थावरः/ अन्तश्चेतनः; SAT SAT-A.254): intra-sentient. Also called antaścetanaḥ. Animate substances which can feel from within but cannot not express outside e.g. plants. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: sthāvaraḥ antaścetanaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vanaspatiḥ (वनस्पतिः; SAT SAT-A.255): plant bearing fruits only. Plant which does not bear visible flowers also called as apuṣpa (flowerless) such as uduṁbara (Ficus glomerata), vaṭa (Ficus benghalensis). Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: vanaspatiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vānaspatya (वानस्पत्य; SAT SAT-A.256): plant bearing fruits as well as flowers. Plant which bears visible flowers and fruits such as āmra (Mangifera indica), jambū (Syzyigium cumini). Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: vānaspatya

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vṛkṣaḥ (वृक्षः; SAT SAT-A.257): tree. Plant which bears visible flowers and fruits such as āmra (Mangifera indica), jambū (Syzyigium cumini). Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: vṛkṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vīrudh (वीरुध्; SAT SAT-A.258): small plant. Twinner, plant which crawl or small non climbing plant; these are of two types - latā (climber) and gulma (shrub). Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: vīrudh

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: latā (लता; SAT SAT-A.259): climber. Twinner/climber e.g. vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa), kapikacchu (Mucuna prurita). Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: latā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gulma (गुल्म; SAT SAT-A.260): shrubs. Small non climbing/ calling plants e.g. atibala (Abutilon indicum), śāliparṇi (Desmodium gangeticum). Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: gulma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: oṣadhī (ओषधी; SAT SAT-A.261): plants which die after bearing fruits. Plans which perish after bearing fruits or after harvest; usually annual herbs like paddy, pulses, wheat, maize. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: oṣadhī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jaṅgamaḥ (जङ्गमः/बहिरन्तश्चेतनः; SAT SAT-A.262): extra-sentient. Also called bahirantaścetanaḥ. Living being belonging to animals kingdom which tangibly react to the external stimuli. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: jaṅgamaḥ bahirantaścetanaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jarāyujaḥ (जरायुजः; SAT SAT-A.263): born of womb. Animals which have placental birth e.g., man, lion, tiger, cow, goat. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: jarāyujaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṇḍajaḥ (अण्डजः; SAT SAT-A.264): born of eggs. Oviparous animals e.g. reptiles, birds, fish. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: aṇḍajaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svedajaḥ (स्वेदजः; SAT SAT-A.265): born of heat and moisture akin to sweat. Creatures which flourish in humid environment e.g. flies, mosquitos, ants, worms. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: svedajaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udbhijaḥ (उद्भिजः; SAT SAT-A.266): born of earth. Smaller creatures which dwell underneath mud e.g. frogs. Category: sentient (cetana-dravyam).
title: udbhijaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: acetana-dravyam (अचेतन-द्रव्यम्/ निरिन्द्रियः; SAT SAT-A.267): insentient. Also called nirindriyaḥ. Non-living; inanimate substances lacking consciousness, e.g. minerals. Category: substance (dravyam).
title: acetana-dravyam nirindriyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: khanijaḥ (खनिजः; SAT SAT-A.268): minerals. Naturally occurring minerals. Category: insentient (acetana-dravyam).
title: khanijaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṛtrimam (कृत्रिमम्; SAT SAT-A.269): synthetic substances. Artificially synthesized substances. Category: insentient (acetana-dravyam).
title: kṛtrimam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tanmātrā (तन्मात्रा; SAT SAT-A.270): subtle state of mahābhūta. Subtle and rudimentary state of mahābhūta. Category: substance (dravyam).
title: tanmātrā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samavāyaḥ (समवायः/ अपृथक्-भावः; SAT SAT-A.271): coexistence/ concomitant relation. Also called apṛthak-bhāvaḥ. The eternal and inseparable relationship i.e. relationship between mahābhūta and their qualities. Category: subtle state of mahābhūta (tanmātrā).
title: samavāyaḥ apṛthak-bhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abhāvaḥ (अभावः; SAT SAT-A.272): non-existence. Non existence. Category: coexistence/ concomitant relation (samavāyaḥ).
title: abhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāgabhāvaḥ (प्रागभावः; SAT SAT-A.273): non-existence before manifestation. Non existence of a substance before its manifestation. Category: coexistence/ concomitant relation (samavāyaḥ).
title: prāgabhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pradhvaṁsābhāvaḥ (प्रध्वंसाभावः; SAT SAT-A.274): non-existence following destruction. Non existence of a subject after its destruction. Category: coexistence/ concomitant relation (samavāyaḥ).
title: pradhvaṁsābhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: atyantābhāvaḥ (अत्यन्ताभावः; SAT SAT-A.275): absolute non-existence. Absolute non-existence in past, present or future. Category: coexistence/ concomitant relation (samavāyaḥ).
title: atyantābhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anyonyābhāvaḥ (अन्योन्याभावः; SAT SAT-A.276): mutual non-existence. Non-existence of a substance in another substance. Category: coexistence/ concomitant relation (samavāyaḥ).
title: anyonyābhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pramāṇam (प्रमाणम्; SAT SAT-A.277): means of acquiring knowledge. Modes of examining and acquiring knowledge; measure. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: pramāṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parīkṣā (परीक्षा; SAT SAT-A.278): examination. Investigation or examinations which leads to correct knowledge. Category: means of acquiring knowledge (pramāṇam).
title: parīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pramā (प्रमा; SAT SAT-A.279): true knowledge. True, valid knowledge. Category: means of acquiring knowledge (pramāṇam).
title: pramā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratyakṣam (प्रत्यक्षम्; SAT SAT-A.280): direct perception. The cognition arising at the instant of the conjugation of the soul, mind, senses, and object. Category: means of acquiring knowledge (pramāṇam).
title: pratyakṣam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sannikarṣaḥ (सन्निकर्षः; SAT SAT-A.281): union, contact. Process of sequential contact of indriyārtha (object of cognitive organs), indriya (cognitive organ), manas (mind), and ātmā (soul) to obtain the direct perception. Category: direct perception (pratyakṣam).
title: sannikarṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirvikalpakam (निर्विकल्पकम्; SAT SAT-A.282): un-differentiated knowledge. Without specific details. Category: direct perception (pratyakṣam).
title: nirvikalpakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: savikalpakam (सविकल्पकम्; SAT SAT-A.283): differentiated knowledge. With specific details. Category: direct perception (pratyakṣam).
title: savikalpakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anumānam (अनुमानम्; SAT SAT-A.284): inferential reasoning. The process through which the knowledge of the unseen facts is inferred on the basis of direct observation. Category: direct perception (pratyakṣam).
title: anumānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anumitiḥ (अनुमितिः; SAT SAT-A.285): inferential conclusion. Conclusion from given premises. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: anumitiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ahetuḥ (अहेतुः; SAT SAT-A.286): fallacy of reasoning. Fallacious resemblance of an argument. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: ahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aupādhika (औपाधिक; SAT SAT-A.287): related to specific suppositions. Relating to or depending on special qualities, limited by particular conditions, valid only under particular suppositions. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: aupādhika

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kevalavyatireki-anumānam (केवलव्यतिरेकि-अनुमानम्; SAT SAT-A.288): purely negative concomitance. Type of inference in which perception is got by negative concomitance. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: kevalavyatireki-anumānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kevalānvayi-anumānam (केवलान्वयि-अनुमानम्; SAT SAT-A.289): purely positive concomitance. Type of inference in which perception is got by positive concomitance. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: kevalānvayi-anumānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tarkaḥ (तर्कः; SAT SAT-A.290): speculation and logic; argument. Tool for inference. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: tarkaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parārthānumānam (स्वार्थानुमानम्; SAT SAT-A.291): inference obtained for self knowledge. Type of inference by which perception is obtained for self knowledge. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: parārthānumānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parārthānumānam (परार्थानुमानम्; SAT SAT-A.292): inference obtained for others. Type of inference by which perception is obtained for others. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: parārthānumānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakaraṇasamaḥ (प्रकरणसमः; SAT SAT-A.293): improper reason appearing identical to the subject. Improper reasoning while deducing an inference in a particular context; a kind of fallacy of inference; one of the ahetu. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: prakaraṇasamaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parāmarśaḥ (परामर्शः; SAT SAT-A.294): inference based on analogy. A process of drawing inference based on analogy. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: parāmarśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pakṣaḥ (पक्षः; SAT SAT-A.295): party of discussion. One aspect or party of discussion; a specific assumption; fortnight; wing. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: pakṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāptiḥ (व्याप्तिः; SAT SAT-A.296): co-existing state. Inherent and inseparable adherence between the two things. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: vyāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyatirekavyāptiḥ (व्यतिरेकव्याप्तिः; SAT SAT-A.297): negative invariable concomitance. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: vyatirekavyāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
