text: pañcāvayava-vākyam (पञ्चावयव-वाक्यम्; SAT SAT-A.298): five steps to derive a conclusion through inference. A collective term used for deriving intended inference based on five steps viz., pratijñā, hetu, udāharaṇa, upanaya, nigamana. Category: inferential reasoning (anumānam).
title: pañcāvayava-vākyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udāharaṇam (उदाहरणम्; SAT SAT-A.299): categorical examples. Categorical examples which can be equally understood by both wise and lay person. Category: five steps to derive a conclusion through inference (pañcāvayava-vākyam).
title: udāharaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: arthāśrayaḥ (अर्थाश्रयः; SAT SAT-A.300): source of meaning. The word or the part of sentence where the actual meaning is lying. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: arthāśrayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tācchilyam (ताच्छिल्यम्; SAT SAT-A.301): inclinations. An affix used to denote a particular inclination, tendency or habit; seventeen types of tācchilya are described. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: tācchilyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāraṇam (कारणम्; SAT SAT-A.302): cause of action. The one which initiates action independently; also denoted by hetu: cause, karma: doer; it is of three types viz., samavayīkāraṇa, asamavāyi-kāraṇa, nimitta-kāraṇa. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: kāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samāvayikāraṇam (समवायिकारणम्; SAT SAT-A.303): inherent cause. Intimate or primary cause e.g. a cloth is vowed by threads. in this case threads are the primary cause for making of the cloth. Category: cause of action (kāraṇam).
title: samāvayikāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asamavāyi-kāraṇam (असमवायि-कारणम्; SAT SAT-A.304): separable, dissociable cause. Secondary or non inherent cause e.g. in case of the making of the cloth, threads are primary cause and colour/dye etc., are secondary cause. Category: cause of action (kāraṇam).
title: asamavāyi-kāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nimitta-kāraṇam (निमित्त-कारणम्; SAT SAT-A.305): generative cause. Associate cause; instrumental cause; efficient cause e.g. in case of making of the cloth, looms, the weaver etc., are generative cause. Category: cause of action (kāraṇam).
title: nimitta-kāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ (दशविधपरीक्ष्यभावः; SAT SAT-A.306): ten important aspects for examination. Ten important aspects for examination viz., kāraṇa (cause); karaṇa (instrument); kāryayoni (source of action); kārya (action itself); kāryaphala (fruits of action); anubandha (subsequent manifes. Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāraṇaṁ (कारणम्; SAT SAT-A.307): cause. In the context of cikitsāśāstra (medicine), the kāraṇa (cause) is considered as physician, as he/she is the causative factor for the achievement of the object i.e. the maintenance of the equilibrium of dhātu. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: kāraṇaṁ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karaṇam (करणम्; SAT SAT-A.308): tool/ instrument. The tool for treatment i.e. medicine/procedure. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: karaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāryayoniḥ (कार्ययोनिः; SAT SAT-A.309): source of action. Intimate cause of illness e.g. disturbance of the equilibrium of dhātu. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: kāryayoniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāryaḥ (कार्यः; SAT SAT-A.310): action itself. The process undertaken for the attainment of dhātusāmya (health). i.e. the process of treatment. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: kāryaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāryaphalam (कार्यफलम्; SAT SAT-A.311): result of the activity. The outcome of intervention in the form of healthy state; result of the act is attainment of happiness. It is known by satisfaction of mind intellect, sense organs and the body. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: kāryaphalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anubandhaḥ (अनुबन्धः; SAT SAT-A.312): subsequent manifestation. The long term consequences/ result; in this context it is achievement of healthy longevity. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: anubandhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratipattiḥ (प्रतिपत्तिः; SAT SAT-A.313): prompt, appropriate action. Ability to take quick and proper decision as per time and need. Category: subsequent manifestation (anubandhaḥ).
title: pratipattiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: deśaḥ (देशः; SAT SAT-A.314): habitat. Both the land as well as the patient constitute deśa (habitat). Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: deśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālaḥ (कालः; SAT SAT-A.315): time. Both the year consisting of seasons and the state of disease. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: kālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pravṛttiḥ (प्रवृत्तिः; SAT SAT-A.316): initiation. Beginning the treatment or therapeutic action. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: pravṛttiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upāyaḥ (उपायः; SAT SAT-A.317): means of action. Excellence of the physician and the correctness of the therapy constitute upāya or means of action. Category: ten important aspects for examination (daśavidhaparīkṣyabhāvaḥ).
title: upāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vaidyaḥ (वैद्यः; SAT SAT-A.318): physician. The physician is a person who is a dakṣa (expert in medicine); tīrthāttaśāstrārtha (academically qualified); dṛṣṭakarmā (experienced) and śuci (purity). Category: science of life (āyurvedaḥ).
title: vaidyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śārīraḥ (शारीरः; SAT SAT-B): related to body. The study of structure and function of the body.
title: śārīraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śarīraḥ (शरीरः; SAT SAT-B.1): body. Indicative of the continuous process of decay of the bodily tissues.
title: śarīraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dehaḥ (देहः; SAT SAT-B.2): body. Indicative of growth in the bodily tissues. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: dehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sarvāṅgaḥ (सर्वाङ्गः; SAT SAT-B.3): whole body. Whole body comprising limbs, trunk, head and neck. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: sarvāṅgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śarīra-vṛddhikara-bhāvaḥ (शरीर-वृद्धिकर-भावः; SAT SAT-B.4): factors responsible for the growth of the body. There are four factors for growth of body:- kālayoga (appropriate time), svabhāvasaṁsiddhi (innate nature), āhārasauṣṭhvam (proper nutrition), avighāta (absence of impairing factors). Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: śarīra-vṛddhikara-bhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śarīra-sampat (शरीर-सम्पत्; SAT SAT-B.5): normal composition of body. A state of all the dhātūs of the body being in normal state. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: śarīra-sampat

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śarīropakāraka (शरीरोपकारक; SAT SAT-B.6): factors which are beneficial to the body. Factors which posess properties similar to the body tissues or those which enhance the body tissues when administered within the body. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: śarīropakāraka

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣaḍaṅgam (षडङ्गम्; SAT SAT-B.7): six divisions of the body. Four limbs, trunk and the head and neck. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: ṣaḍaṅgam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṅga-pradeśaḥ (अङ्ग-प्रदेशः; SAT SAT-B.8): body regions. Division of the body in to various regions for descriptive purposes. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: aṅga-pradeśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gātrapañcakam (गात्रपञ्चकम्; SAT SAT-B.9): five prominences of developing foetus. Five prominences in the developing foetus corresponding to the four limbs and head. Category: body regions (aṅga-pradeśaḥ).
title: gātrapañcakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adhaḥkāyaḥ (अधःकायः; SAT SAT-B.10): part of body below the waist. Lower half of the body. Category: body regions (aṅga-pradeśaḥ).
title: adhaḥkāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrdhvakāyaḥ (ऊर्ध्वकायः; SAT SAT-B.11): part of body above the waist. Upper half of the body. Category: body regions (aṅga-pradeśaḥ).
title: ūrdhvakāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrdhvajatru (ऊर्ध्वजत्रु; SAT SAT-B.12): part of body above the clavicle. Head and neck. Category: body regions (aṅga-pradeśaḥ).
title: ūrdhvajatru

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrdhvāṅgam (ऊर्ध्वाङ्गम्; SAT SAT-B.13): head and neck. Generally used as a synonym of head. Category: body regions (aṅga-pradeśaḥ).
title: ūrdhvāṅgam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śiraḥ (शिरः/ उत्तमाङ्गम्; SAT SAT-B.14): head. Also called uttamāṅgam. Site where prāṇa and indriya are situated, the uppermost and chief part of the body. Category: six divisions of the body (ṣaḍaṅgam).
title: śiraḥ uttamāṅgam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kapālaḥ (कपालः; SAT SAT-B.15): skull/cranium. Bones forming the skull. Category: head (śiraḥ).
title: kapālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śaṅkhaḥ (शङ्खः; SAT SAT-B.16): temple. Area on the sides of the forehead. Category: head (śiraḥ).
title: śaṅkhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lalāṭam (ललाटम्/अलिकम्; SAT SAT-B.17): fore-head. Also called alikam. The anterior part of the head below the hairline and above the eyes. Category: head (śiraḥ).
title: lalāṭam alikam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: akṣi (अक्षि; SAT SAT-B.18): eye. The organ of vision. Category: head (śiraḥ).
title: akṣi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dṛṣṭi-golakaḥ (दृष्टि-गोलकः/ नयन-बुद्बुदः/ अक्षि-गोलकम्; SAT SAT-B.19): eyeball. Also called nayana-budbudaḥ and akṣi-golakam. The globe of the eye. Category: eye (akṣi).
title: dṛṣṭi-golakaḥ nayana-budbudaḥ akṣi-golakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: akṣikūṭaḥ (अक्षिकूटः; SAT SAT-B.20): orbit. The bony pyramid-shaped cavity of the skull that contains and protects the eyeball. Category: eye (akṣi).
title: akṣikūṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: netrakośaḥ (नेत्रकोशः/ अक्षिकोषः/ नेत्र-छादनम् /अक्षिपुटम्/ वर्त्म /अक्षिवर्त्म/ अक्षिवर्त्मकोषः; SAT SAT-B.21): eyelid. Also called akṣikoṣaḥ, netra-chādanam, akṣipuṭam, vartma, akṣivartma and akṣivartmakoṣaḥ. Thin fold of skin that covers and protects the human eye. Category: eye (akṣi).
title: netrakośaḥ akṣikoṣaḥ netra-chādanam akṣipuṭam vartma akṣivartma akṣivartmakoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: netrasandhiḥ (नेत्रसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.22): junctions of the eye. The junction points in the eye such as sclero-corneal junction, the medial and lateral canthi, the junction between eye lashes and eyelids, pupilary margins etc. Category: eye (akṣi).
title: netrasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kanīnikā (कनीनिका/ अक्षिकनीनिका; SAT SAT-B.23): inner canthus. Also called akṣikanīnikā. Medial angle of eye; the angle at medial side of the slit between the eyelids. Category: eye (akṣi).

text: jihvā-prabandhaḥ (जिह्वा-प्रबन्धः/ जिह्वा-मूलम्; SAT SAT-B.94): root of tongue. Also called jihvā-mūlam. Posterior part of the tongue which attaches to the bone. Category: tongue (jihvā).
title: jihvā-prabandhaḥ jihvā-mūlam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: jihvā-sevanī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tālu (तालु/तालुप्रदेशः (मूर्धगः); SAT SAT-B.96): palate /anterior fontanelle. Also called tālupradeśaḥ (mūrdhagaḥ). The roof of the oral cavity which is divided into the bony (hard) and muscular (soft) parts. Category: tongue (jihvā).
title: tālu tālupradeśaḥ (mūrdhagaḥ)

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tālumāṁsam (तालुमांसम्; SAT SAT-B.97): soft palate. The posterior portion of the roof of the mouth. Category: tongue (jihvā).
title: tālumāṁsam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upajihvikā (उपजिह्विका; SAT SAT-B.98): palatine tonsils. Mass of lymphatic tissue that lies in tonsillar fossa on each side of oropharynx between palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches. Category: tongue (jihvā).
title: upajihvikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adhijihvikā (अधिजिह्विका; SAT SAT-B.99): epiglottis or adenoids. 1. a thin leaf shaped structure located immediately posterior to root of the tongue. 2. a mass of lymphatic tissue located in depressions of mucous membranes of pharynx. Category: tongue (jihvā).
title: adhijihvikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṇṭhaḥ (कण्ठः; SAT SAT-B.100): larynx/front of the neck/throat. The anterior part of the neck enclosing the pharynx and larynx which has the functions of swallowing and speech/the passage from the mouth to the pharynx. Category: head (śiraḥ).
title: kaṇṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kākalam (काकलम् / काकलकम्/ गलमणिः/गलशुण्डिका/ घण्टिका; SAT SAT-B.101): uvula. Also called kākalakam, galamaṇiḥ, galaśuṇḍikā and ghaṇṭikā. Small soft structure hanging from free edge of soft palate in the midline above the root of the tounge. Category: larynx/front of the neck/throat (kaṇṭhaḥ).
title: kākalam kākalakam galamaṇiḥ galaśuṇḍikā ghaṇṭikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: galamārgaḥ (गलमार्गः; SAT SAT-B.102): throat-passage. The passage for food bolus through the neck from the mouth to the oesophagus. Category: larynx/front of the neck/throat (kaṇṭhaḥ).
title: galamārgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: galasandhiḥ (गलसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.103): isthmus of fauces. The constricted opening leading from the mouth and the oral pharynx. Category: larynx/front of the neck/throat (kaṇṭhaḥ).
title: galasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: galaḥ (गलः; SAT SAT-B.104): oropharynx/throat. Central portion of the pharynx lying between soft palate and upper portion of epiglottis. Category: larynx/front of the neck/throat (kaṇṭhaḥ).
title: galaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: galanalakam (गलनलकम्; SAT SAT-B.105): trachea. The enlarged upper end of trachea below the root of trunk. Category: larynx/front of the neck/throat (kaṇṭhaḥ).
title: galanalakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: grīvā (ग्रीवा; SAT SAT-B.106): neck. The structure which joins the head with the trunk. Category: larynx/front of the neck/throat (kaṇṭhaḥ).
title: grīvā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: grīvāmūlam (ग्रीवामूलम्/ जत्रुमूलम्; SAT SAT-B.107): suprasternal notch. Also called jatrumūlam. Notch above the sternum. Category: head (śiraḥ).
title: grīvāmūlam jatrumūlam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: manyā (मन्या; SAT SAT-B.108): carotid area of the neck. The lateral parts of the front of neck through which the carotid vessels pass. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: manyā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antarādhiḥ (अन्तराधिः; SAT SAT-B.109): trunk. The body exclusive of head, neck and limbs. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: antarādhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsaḥ (अंसः; SAT SAT-B.110): shoulder. The area above the upper border of scapula and overlying the trapezius muscle which is the area used for weight bearing. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: aṁsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsapīṭham (अंसपीठम्; SAT SAT-B.111): glenoid cavity. The pear shaped cavity on the scapula where the rounded head of humerus attaches. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).
title: aṁsapīṭham

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsakūṭaḥ (अंसकूटः; SAT SAT-B.112): acromion. The lateral triangular projection of the spine of the scapula. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).
title: aṁsakūṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsapiṇḍaḥ (अंसपिण्डः/ अंसपिण्डिका; SAT SAT-B.113): deltoid prominence. Also called aṁsapiṇḍikā. The rounded prominance around the soulder due to underlying deltoid muscle. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).
title: aṁsapiṇḍaḥ aṁsapiṇḍikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsabandhanam (अंसबन्धनम्; SAT SAT-B.114): ligaments and muscles of the shoulder. The supporting structures of the shoulder joint. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).
title: aṁsabandhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsamūlam (अंसमूलम्; SAT SAT-B.115): apex of the scapula. The glenoid region. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).
title: aṁsamūlam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsadeśaḥ (अंसदेशः; SAT SAT-B.116): shoulder region. The junction of the clavicle and scapula where the arm meets the trunk. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).
title: aṁsadeśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrdhvatrikam (ऊर्ध्वत्रिकम्; SAT SAT-B.117): inter-scapular region. Area between the scapulae. Category: shoulder (aṁsaḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kakṣaḥ (कक्षः/कक्षा; SAT SAT-B.118): axilla/armpit. Also called kakṣā. The pyramidal space between the lateral part of the upper part of thorax and the upper limbs. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: kakṣaḥ kakṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uraḥ (उरः; SAT SAT-B.119): chest/thorax. The part of the human body enclosed by the ribs and sternum. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: uraḥ

text: uraḥkoṣṭhaḥ (उरःकोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.120): thoracic cavity. The space lying above the diaphragm and closed within the walls of the thorax. Category: chest/thorax (uraḥ).
title: uraḥkoṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: urogrīvam (उरोग्रीवम्; SAT SAT-B.121): thorax and neck. The part of the body between the base of the neck superiorly and the diaphragm inferiorly. Category: chest/thorax (uraḥ).
title: urogrīvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: stanaḥ (स्तनः/ पयोधरौ/ कुचौ; SAT SAT-B.122): breast/mammary gland. Also called payodharau and kucau. Prominences on the anterior part of thorax in females which enclose lactifercous ducts and having function of lactation which are rudimentary in males. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: stanaḥ payodharau kucau

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cūcukam (चूचुकम्; SAT SAT-B.123): nipple. The conical protuberance in each breast from which the lactiferous ducts discharge in the females which are rudimentary in males. Category: breast/mammary gland (stanaḥ).
title: cūcukam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udaraḥ (उदरः/कुक्षिः; SAT SAT-B.124): abdomen. Also called kukṣiḥ. Part of the body between the thorax and the pelvis. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: udaraḥ kukṣiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antaḥkukṣiḥ (अन्तःकुक्षिः; SAT SAT-B.125): abdominal/uterine cavity. Cavity of the portion of the trunk located between chest and pelvis/ cavity within the uterus. Category: abdomen (udaraḥ).
title: antaḥkukṣiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: taila-vartikā (तैल-वर्तिका; SAT SAT-B.126): omentum. Structure which is suspended from the curvatures of the stomach and covers the intestine like an apron. Category: abdomen (udaraḥ).
title: taila-vartikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udarapārśvam (उदरपार्श्वम्/ पार्श्वम्; SAT SAT-B.127): flank. Also called pārśvam. Side of abdomen. Category: abdomen (udaraḥ).
title: udarapārśvam pārśvam

title: yoniḥ apatyapathaḥ apatyamārgaḥ

text: praśastayoniḥ (प्रशस्तयोनिः; SAT SAT-B.129): normal female external genitalia. The normal strucural and functinal state of the external genitalia indicative of woman fit for reproductive function. Category: vagina (yoniḥ).
title: praśastayoniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vaṅkṣaṇa (वङ्क्षण/ गण्डकः; SAT SAT-B.130): groin. Also called gaṇḍakaḥ. The depression between thigh and trunk. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: vaṅkṣaṇa gaṇḍakaḥ

title: vṛṣaṇaḥ

title: koṣaḥ(śaḥ) aṇḍakoṣaḥ

text: sīvanī (सीवनी; SAT SAT-B.134): suture/frenulum. Stracture having appiriance of sutures which are seven in number. Category: testicle (vṛṣaṇaḥ).

title: gudam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāyuvalayaḥ (पायुवलयः; SAT SAT-B.136): mucous folds of rectum. Horizontal mucous folds of rectum (Houston's valves). Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: poṭṭalakaḥ (पोट्टलकः; SAT SAT-B.137): caecum. A blind pouch like structure forming the first part of the large intestine. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adharagudam (अधरगुदम्; SAT SAT-B.138): lower part of the rectum/anal canal. The terminal part of the digestive tract. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).

title: gudapārśvakṣetram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gudāsthivivaram (गुदास्थिविवरम्; SAT SAT-B.140): outlet of pelvis. The lower outlet of the pelvic cavity which gives passage to the anal canal and the reproductive and urinary passages. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: gudāsthivivaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guda-upastha-deśaḥ (गुद-उपस्थ-देशः/ पायुमेढ्रान्तरम्; SAT SAT-B.141): perineum. Also called pāyumeḍhrāntaram. The structures occupying the pelvic outlet and constituting the pelvic floor. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).

title: kaśerukā pṛṣṭhavaṁśaḥ pṛṣṭheṣikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jaghanam (जघनम्; SAT SAT-B.144): waist. Hip and loins. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).

title: sphik kaṭī-prothaḥ nitambaḥ prothau

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śroṇiḥ (श्रोणिः; SAT SAT-B.146): pelvis. The bony structure formed by the innomimante bones, sacrum coccyx, and the ligaments uniting them. Category: groin (vaṅkṣaṇa).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pārśvajaghanam (पार्श्वजघनम्; SAT SAT-B.147): side of pelvis. Side of a bony structure formed by the innominate bones. the sacrum, the coccyx and the ligaments joining them. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: pārśvajaghanam

text: trikam (त्रिकम्; SAT SAT-B.148): 1. sacral region or sacrum 2. region around shoulder girdle. 1. sacral region or sacrum; the region behind the triangular bone situated dorsal and caudal from the two ilia between the fifth lumbar vertebra and coccyx. 2. region around shoulder girdle. Category: trunk (antarādhiḥ).
title: trikam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bāhuḥ (बाहुः; SAT SAT-B.149): upper limb. Part of the body extending from the deltoid region to the hand. Category: six divisions of the body (ṣaḍaṅgam).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avarodhaḥ (अवरोधः; SAT SAT-B.150): shoulder. The region where the upperlimb meets the trunk. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: aratniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kūrparaḥ (कूर्परः/कफोणिः/कुहणिका; SAT SAT-B.152): elbow. Also called kaphoṇiḥ and kuhaṇikā. The joint between the arm and the forearm. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: kūrparaḥ kaphoṇiḥ kuhaṇikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāṇiḥ (पाणिः/करः; SAT SAT-B.153): hand/manus. Also called karaḥ. The part of the upper limb distal to the wrist. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: pāṇiḥ karaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karamūlam (करमूलम्/पाणिमूलम्; SAT SAT-B.154): wrist. Also called pāṇimūlam. The joint between the forearm and the hand. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: karamūlam pāṇimūlam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāṇitalam (पाणितलम्/ पाणिहृदयम्; SAT SAT-B.155): palm. Also called pāṇihṛdayam. Anterior or flexor surface of the hand from wrist to base of the fingers. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: pāṇitalam pāṇihṛdayam

text: prakoṣṭhaḥ (प्रकोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.157): forearm or antebrachium/distal third of the forearm. The portion of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist/lower one third of the forearm. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: prakoṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṅguliḥ (अङ्गुलिः; SAT SAT-B.158): fingers/toes (digits). The most mobile and distal part of the limbs; five in number for each limb. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: aṅguliḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaniṣṭhikā (कनिष्ठिका/ कनिष्ठा; SAT SAT-B.159): little finger. Also called kaniṣṭhā. The fifth digit of the limb which is also the smallest. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: kaniṣṭhikā kaniṣṭhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṅgulyagram (अङ्गुल्यग्रम्; SAT SAT-B.163): tip of the finger. The distalmost part of the digit. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).

text: aṅguṣṭhaḥ (अङ्गुष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.164): thumb/great toe. The first digit of the hand or foot. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).

title: aṅguṣṭhodaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anāmikā (अनामिका/पवित्राङ्गुलिः; SAT SAT-B.167): annularis. Also called pavitrāṅguliḥ. Ring finger or the fourth digit. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: anāmikā pavitrāṅguliḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tarjanī (तर्जनी/ प्रदेशिनी; SAT SAT-B.168): index finger. Also called pradeśinī. Forefinger or the second digit. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: tarjanī pradeśinī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: piṇḍikā (बाहु-पिण्डिका; SAT SAT-B.169): biccipital prominance. Muscular prominence on the anterior part of the arm due to underlying biceps brachii muscle. Category: upper limb (bāhuḥ).
title: piṇḍikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sakthi (सक्थि; SAT SAT-B.170): lower limb. Part of the body extending from the gluteal region to the foot specialized for weight-bearing and locomotion. Category: six divisions of the body (ṣaḍaṅgam).
title: sakthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūru (ऊरु; SAT SAT-B.171): thigh. The part of the lower limb between the groins and the knee anteriorly and the lower margins of the buttocks and the knee posteriorly. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: ūru

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrupiṇḍikā (ऊरुपिण्डिका; SAT SAT-B.172): quadricipatal prominance. Muscular prominance on the front of thigh due to underlying quadriceps femoris muscles. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: ūrupiṇḍikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrumūlam (ऊरुमूलम्; SAT SAT-B.173): inguinal region. Groin or the junctional area between thigh and the trunk. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: ūrumūlam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrvī sirā (ऊर्वी सिरा; SAT SAT-B.174): femoral vessels. Deep seated branches of femoral vessels. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: ūrvī sirā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jānu (जानु; SAT SAT-B.175): knee. The joint between the thigh and leg. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: jānu

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jaṅghā (जङ्घा; SAT SAT-B.176): leg. The part of the lower limb between the knee and the ankle. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: jaṅghā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jaṅghā-piṇḍikā (जङ्घा-पिण्डिका; SAT SAT-B.177): calf muscle. The muscular prominece on the posterior upper part of the leg due to underlying gastrocnemius and soleus muscles. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: jaṅghā-piṇḍikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gulphaḥ (गुल्फः/ घुटिका/ घुण्टिका; SAT SAT-B.178): ankle. Also called ghuṭikā and ghuṇṭikā. The joint between the leg and the foot. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: gulphaḥ ghuṭikā ghuṇṭikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gulphakarṇaḥ (गुल्फकर्णः; SAT SAT-B.179): malleoli. Bony prominences on the either side of the ankle. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: gulphakarṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: khuḍakaḥ (खुडकः/ खुलकः; SAT SAT-B.180): ankle joint. Also called khulakaḥ. The joint between the leg and the foot. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: khuḍakaḥ khulakaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādaḥ (पादः; SAT SAT-B.181): foot. The part of the lower limb distal to the ankle joint. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: pādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pārṣṇiḥ (पार्ष्णिः; SAT SAT-B.182): heel. Rounded posterior portion of the foot. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: pārṣṇiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādāgram (पादाग्रम्; SAT SAT-B.183): fore-foot. Anterior 1/3rd part of the foot. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: pādāgram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādāṅguliḥ (पादाङ्गुलिः; SAT SAT-B.184): toes. Digits of the foot. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: pādāṅguliḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādatalam (पादतलम्; SAT SAT-B.185): sole. Under surface of the foot. Category: lower limb (sakthi).
title: pādatalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karmendriyaḥ (कर्मेन्द्रियः; SAT SAT-B.186): faculties of action. The five faculties of action namely vāk, pāṇiḥ, pādaḥ, pāyuḥ and upasthaḥ. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: karmendriyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāk (वाक्; SAT SAT-B.187): speech faculty. One among the karmendriya - the combined function of phonatin and articulation. Category: faculties of action (karmendriyaḥ).
title: vāk

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāṇiḥ (पाणिः; SAT SAT-B.188): motor faculty of upper limb. One among the karmendriya - related to the function of the upper limb. Category: faculties of action (karmendriyaḥ).
title: pāṇiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādaḥ (पादः; SAT SAT-B.189): motor faculty of lower limb. One among the karmendriya - related to movements, the function of the lower limb. Category: faculties of action (karmendriyaḥ).
title: pādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāyuḥ (पायुः; SAT SAT-B.190): excretory faculty of anus. One among the karmendriya having the function of excretion which is associated with the anus. Category: faculties of action (karmendriyaḥ).
title: pāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upasthaḥ (उपस्थः; SAT SAT-B.191): reproductive faculty of penis. One among the karmendriya having the function of procreation which is associated with the penis. Category: faculties of action (karmendriyaḥ).
title: upasthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jñānendriyaḥ (ज्ञानेन्द्रियः; SAT SAT-B.192): sensory faculties. The five sensory or cognitive faculties namely śrotrendriyam, cakṣurindriyam, rasanendriyam, ghrāṇendriyam and tvagindriyam. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: jñānendriyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śrotrendriyam (श्रोत्रेन्द्रियम्; SAT SAT-B.193): sensory faculty of ear. One among the jñānendriya- the faculty responsible for perception of sound or hearing. Category: sensory faculties (jñānendriyaḥ).
title: śrotrendriyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cakṣurindriyam (चक्षुरिन्द्रियम्; SAT SAT-B.194): sensory faculty of eye. One among the jñānendriya - the faculty responsible for vision. Category: sensory faculties (jñānendriyaḥ).
title: cakṣurindriyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasanendriyam (रसनेन्द्रियम्; SAT SAT-B.195): sensory faculty of tongue. One among the jñānendriya - the faculty responsible for perception of taste or gustation. Category: sensory faculties (jñānendriyaḥ).
title: rasanendriyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ghrāṇendriyam (घ्राणेन्द्रियम्; SAT SAT-B.196): sensory faculty of nose. One among the jñānendriya - the faculty responsible for perception of smell or olfaction. Category: sensory faculties (jñānendriyaḥ).
title: ghrāṇendriyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tvagindriyam (त्वगिन्द्रियम्/ स्पर्शनेन्द्रियम्; SAT SAT-B.197): sensory faculty of skin. Also called sparśanendriyam. One among the jñānendriya - the faculty responsible for perception of touch sensation. Category: sensory faculties (jñānendriyaḥ).
title: tvagindriyam sparśanendriyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: carma (चर्म/त्वक्; SAT SAT-B.198): skin. Also called tvak. The outer covering of the body which is the substratum for sensory faculty. Category: sensory faculties (jñānendriyaḥ).
title: carma tvak

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kūyakam (कूयकम्; SAT SAT-B.199): hair follicles. Invagination of the epidermis from which a hair develops. Category: skin (carma).
title: kūyakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: keśabhūmiḥ (केशभूमिः; SAT SAT-B.200): field of hairs. Area of the skin from where hairs arise. Category: skin (carma).
title: keśabhūmiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kacaḥ (कचः; SAT SAT-B.201): hair. Pigmented proteinaceous filamentous outgrowths from the epidermis of skin which is a part of exoskeleton. Category: skin (carma).
title: kacaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kacāntaḥ (कचान्तः; SAT SAT-B.202): hairline. Boundry where the hairs end. Category: skin (carma).
title: kacāntaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karajaḥ (करजः/नखः; SAT SAT-B.203): nail. Also called nakhaḥ. Horny cell structure of the epidermis forming flat plates upon the dorsal surface of the terminal phalanges. Category: skin (carma).
title: karajaḥ nakhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upanakham (उपनखम्; SAT SAT-B.204): nail fold. A groove in the cutaneous tissue surrounding the margins and proximal edges of nail. Category: skin (carma).
title: upanakham

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nakha-māṁsam (नख-मांसम्; SAT SAT-B.205): nail bed. Portion of a finger or toe covered by the nail. Category: skin (carma).
title: nakha-māṁsam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nakha-sandhiḥ (नख-सन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.206): nail root and nail fold. Nail root and nail fold. Root of a horny cell structure of the epidermis forming flat plates upon the dorsal surface of the terminal phalanges. Category: skin (carma).
title: nakha-sandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: keśaḥ (केशः/ अङ्गजः/अङ्गजम्; SAT SAT-B.207): hair. Also called aṅgajaḥ and aṅgajam. Pigmented proteinaceous filamentous outgrowths from the epidermis of skin which is a part of exoskeleton. Category: skin (carma).
title: keśaḥ aṅgajaḥ aṅgajam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: loma (लोम; SAT SAT-B.208): body hairs. Hairs located on areas other than the scalp. Category: skin (carma).
title: loma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: koṣṭhāṅgam (कोष्ठाङ्गम्; SAT SAT-B.209): viscera/splanchna. Internal organs enclosed within the cavity especially the abdominal organs. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: koṣṭhāṅgam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mastuluṅgam (मस्तुलुङ्गम्/ मस्तिष्कम्/ घृतिका; SAT SAT-B.210): brain. Also called mastiṣkam and ghṛtikā. Part of the central nervous system situtated within the cranial cavity. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: mastuluṅgam mastiṣkam ghṛtikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hṛdayam (हृदयम्; SAT SAT-B.211): heart or cardiac region. A hollow muscular contractile organ; the centre of circulatory system. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: hṛdayam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: arthaḥ (अर्थः; SAT SAT-B.212): heart. Hollow muscular contractile organ; the centre of circulatory system. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: arthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kroḍaḥ (क्रोडः; SAT SAT-B.213): cardiac region. Region containing the heart. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: kroḍaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kloma (क्लोम; SAT SAT-B.214): pancreas. Gland with endocrine as well as exocrine functions situated behind the stomach which secretes digestive enzymes into the duodenum. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: kloma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yakṛt (यकृत्/कालखण्डः; SAT SAT-B.215): liver. Also called kālakhaṇḍaḥ. Largest organ in the body situated on the right side below the diaphragm. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: yakṛt kālakhaṇḍaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: plīhā (प्लीहा; SAT SAT-B.216): spleen. Abdominal organ which is a part of the reticulo-endothelial system mainly involved in the production and removal of blood cells. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: plīhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vṛkkā (वृक्का/कालेयकम्/ कुक्षिगोलकः; SAT SAT-B.217): kidney. Also called kāleyakam and kukṣigolakaḥ. Paired retroperitoneal organs on each side of vertebral column. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: vṛkkā kāleyakam kukṣigolakaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bastiḥ (बस्तिः/ वस्तिः; SAT SAT-B.218): urinary bladder. Also called vastiḥ. Hollow muscular pelvic organ responsible for collection storage and voiding of urine. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: bastiḥ vastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gavinī (गविनी; SAT SAT-B.219): ureter. Tube which carries urine from kidney to the bladder. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: gavinī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: purīṣādhāraḥ (पुरीषाधारः; SAT SAT-B.220): sigmoid colon and rectum. Distal part of the large intestine responsible for storage of faecal matter until its elimination. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: purīṣādhāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āmāśayaḥ (आमाशयः/अन्नसम्पुटम्/ अन्नाशयः; SAT SAT-B.221): stomach. Also called annasampuṭam and annāśayaḥ. Dilated sac like distensible portion of alimentary canal between the esophagus and the duodenum which contains partially digested food. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: āmāśayaḥ annasampuṭam annāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: paktisthānam (पक्तिस्थानम्; SAT SAT-B.222): place of digestion. Major sites of the alimentary tract responsible for digestion of ingested food. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: paktisthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pakvāśayaḥ (पक्वाशयः/ पक्वस्थानम्/ पक्वाधानम्; SAT SAT-B.223): large intestine. Also called pakvasthānam and pakvādhānam. Part of alimentary canal extending from the ileum to the anus. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: pakvāśayaḥ pakvasthānam pakvādhānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āmapakvāśayaḥ (आमपक्वाशयः; SAT SAT-B.224): gastro-intestinal tract. The digestive tube from stomach and intestines. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: āmapakvāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uttaragudam (उत्तरगुदम्; SAT SAT-B.225): rectum. Part which attaches to the anal canal having the function of storage of faecal matter. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: uttaragudam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adharagudam (अधरगुदम्; SAT SAT-B.226): anal canal. Terminal part of the large intestine connecting the lower part of rectum to the anal canal which is the passage for faecal matter during its elimination from the body through the anus. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: adharagudam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antrāśayaḥ (अन्त्राशयः; SAT SAT-B.227): lumen of intestine. Cavity of the alimentary canal extending from the pylorus to the anus. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: antrāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣudrāntram (क्षुद्रान्त्रम्/ पच्यमानाशयः; SAT SAT-B.228): small intestine. Also called pacyamānāśayaḥ. The alimentary canal extending from the pylorus to the caecum where the consumed food undergoes transformation or digestion. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: kṣudrāntram pacyamānāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: grahaṇī (ग्रहणी; SAT SAT-B.229): duodenum. Part of the gut lying between the stomach and intestines. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: grahaṇī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣudrāntrāvayavaḥ (क्षुद्रान्त्रावयवः; SAT SAT-B.230): loop of small intestine. Convoluted parts of small intestine. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: kṣudrāntrāvayavaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: agnyadhiṣṭhānam (अग्न्यधिष्ठानम्/ अग्निस्थानम्; SAT SAT-B.231): seat of agni. Also called agnisthānam. Synonym of agnisthāna and means ‘the part of the kośṭha which is the substratum of agni’; generally refers to duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: agnyadhiṣṭhānam agnisthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthūlāntram (स्थूलान्त्रम्/ कट्यन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-B.232): large intestine. Also called kaṭyantram. The alimentary canal extending from the ileum to the anus. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: sthūlāntram kaṭyantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uṇḍukaḥ (उण्डुकः; SAT SAT-B.233): caecum. Blind pouch or cul-de-sac like structure forming the first part of the large intestine. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: uṇḍukaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vapāvahanam (वपावहनम्; SAT SAT-B.234): omentum. Large apron-like fold of visceral peritoneum that hangs down from the stomach and covers the abdominal viscera. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: vapāvahanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āśayaḥ (आशयः; SAT SAT-B.235): receptacle. Some particular organ or group of organs which act as container of something. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: āśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vātāśayaḥ (वाताशयः; SAT SAT-B.236): receptacle for vāta. Promient site of vāta doṣa; mainly large intestines. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: vātāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pittāśayaḥ (पित्ताशयः; SAT SAT-B.237): receptacle for pitta/ gall bladder. Site for storage of pitta which has an important role in digestion of ingested food such as gall bladder. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: pittāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaphāśayaḥ (कफाशयः; SAT SAT-B.238): receptacle for kapha. Especially chest, stomach and head. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: kaphāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: raktāśayaḥ (रक्ताशयः; SAT SAT-B.239): receptacle for rakta. Seats of storage or collection of blood viz. liver, spleen or heart. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: raktāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pakvāśayaḥ (पक्वाशयः; SAT SAT-B.240): large intestine. Major seat of vāta doṣa. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: pakvāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūtrāśayaḥ (मूत्राशयः; SAT SAT-B.241): urinary bladder. Hollow muscular pelvic organ responsible for collection storage and voiding of urine. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: mūtrāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: annamārgaḥ (अन्नमार्गः; SAT SAT-B.242): esophagus. Muscular canal extending from the pharynx to the stomach. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: annamārgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: agnyāśayaḥ (अग्न्याशयः; SAT SAT-B.243): pancreas. Compound acinotubular gland situated behind the stomach in front of the first and second lumbar vertebrae in horizontal position. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: agnyāśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhāśayaḥ (गर्भाशयः/ गर्भशय्या; SAT SAT-B.244): uterus. Also called garbhaśayyā. Receptacle for the foetus; the organ of female reproductive system for containing and nourishing the embryo/fetus. Category: receptacle (āśayaḥ).
title: garbhāśayaḥ garbhaśayyā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhakoṣaḥ (गर्भकोषः; SAT SAT-B.245): bag of foetal membrane. Membranes that hold a developing embryo/fetus until shortly before birth. Category: uterus (garbhāśayaḥ).
title: garbhakoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhakoṣṭhaḥ (गर्भकोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.246): uterine cavity. Cavity of the uterus/bag of foetal membrane necessary for containing and nourishing the embryo. Category: uterus (garbhāśayaḥ).
title: garbhakoṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhacchidram (गर्भच्छिद्रम्; SAT SAT-B.247): os uteri. Mouth of uterus. Category: uterus (garbhāśayaḥ).
title: garbhacchidram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhiḥ (नाभिः; SAT SAT-B.248): umbilicus. Depressed point in the middle of the abdomen; scar that marks the former attachment of umbilical cord to the fetus. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: nābhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhibandhanam (नाभिबन्धनम्; SAT SAT-B.249): foetal end of umbilical cord. Foetal end of attachment connecting the foetus with the placenta. Category: umbilicus (nābhiḥ).
title: nābhibandhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhimaṇḍalam (नाभिमण्डलम्; SAT SAT-B.250): round area of umbilicus. Depressed point in the middle of the abdomen, the scar that marks the former attachment of umbilical cord to the fetus. Category: umbilicus (nābhiḥ).
title: nābhimaṇḍalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhipradeśaḥ (नाभिप्रदेशः; SAT SAT-B.251): umbilical region. Area near and around the umbilicus. Category: umbilicus (nābhiḥ).
title: nābhipradeśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aparā (अपरा/ अमरा; SAT SAT-B.252): placenta. Also called amarā. Oval or discoid spongy structure in the uterus through which the fetus derives its nourishment. Category: umbilicus (nābhiḥ).
title: aparā amarā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhināḍī (नाभिनाडी; SAT SAT-B.253): umbilical cord. Attachment conecting the fetus with the placenta. Category: umbilicus (nābhiḥ).
title: nābhināḍī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhanābhināḍī (गर्भनाभिनाडी; SAT SAT-B.254): umbilical cord. Attachment conecting the fetus with the placenta. Category: umbilicus (nābhiḥ).
title: garbhanābhināḍī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kalā (कला; SAT SAT-B.255): membrane. General name given to the membranes of the body such as māmsadharā, raktadharā, medodharā, śleṣmadharā, purīṣadharā, pittadharā and śukradharā. Category: viscera/splanchna (koṣṭhāṅgam).
title: kalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: māṁsadharākalā (मांसधराकला; SAT SAT-B.256): deep fascia. Layer of dense fibrous connective tissue which surrounds individual muscles, and also divide groups of muscles into fascial compartments. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: māṁsadharākalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: raktadharākalā (रक्तधराकला; SAT SAT-B.257): vascular endothelium. Epithelium that lines the interior surface of blood vessels composed of endothelial cells. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: raktadharākalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: medodharākalā (मेदोधराकला; SAT SAT-B.258): omentum and lining of medullary canal. Fat filled double layered serous membrane lining visceral organs inside the abdominal cavity and the inner lining of the bones which wall the bone marrow. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: medodharākalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śleṣmadharākalā (श्लेष्मधराकला; SAT SAT-B.259): synovial membrane. Specialized connective tissue lining the inner surface of capsules of synovial joints and tendon sheaths primarily responsible for secretion of synovial fluid which acts as lubricant to the joint. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: śleṣmadharākalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: purīṣadharākalā (पुरीषधराकला; SAT SAT-B.260): mucosa of colon and rectum. Mucous membrane of large intestine and rectum. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: purīṣadharākalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pittadharā-kalā (पित्तधरा-कला; SAT SAT-B.261): gastro-intestinal mucosa. Mucous membrane of stomach, large intestine and small intestine. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: pittadharā-kalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukradharākalā (शुक्रधराकला; SAT SAT-B.262): germinal epithelium. Innermost layer of the testicle and wall of the seminiferous tubule within the testes in males and ovary in females which gives origin to germ cells. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: śukradharākalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lasikā (लसीका; SAT SAT-B.263): watery component of the skin. Watery component of the skin which exudates as clear fluid on injury to skin; one of the sites of pitta. Category: membrane (kalā).
title: lasikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthi (अस्थि; SAT SAT-B.264): bone. Type of connective tissue which is hard and rigid, constituting most of the skeleton of vertebrates. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: asthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṇvasthi (अण्वस्थि; SAT SAT-B.265): small bones. Bones of small dimensions such as carpal bones, tarsal bones, metacarpals etc. Category: bone (asthi).
title: aṇvasthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kapālāsthi (कपालास्थि/ कर्परम्; SAT SAT-B.266): flat bone. Also called karparam. Bones such as skull bones consisting of only a thin layer of compact bone, or of two layers with intervening cancellous bone and marrow; one among the classification on asṭhi according to Ayurveda based on shape. Category: bone (asthi).
title: kapālāsthi karparam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rucakāsthi (रुचकास्थि; SAT SAT-B.267): teeth. Bone like structures attached to upper and lower jaws which aids in mastication and articulation, one among the classification on asṭhiaccording to Ayurveda based on shape. Category: bone (asthi).
title: rucakāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: taruṇāsthi (तरुणास्थि; SAT SAT-B.268): cartilage. Connective tissue structures which act as precursors for bone, one among the classification on asṭhiaccording to Ayurveda based on shape. Category: bone (asthi).
title: taruṇāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: valayāsthi (वलयास्थि; SAT SAT-B.269): curved bone. Long, flat and curved bones such as ribs, one among the classification on asṭhi according to Ayurveda based on shape. Category: bone (asthi).
title: valayāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nalakāsthi (नलकास्थि; SAT SAT-B.270): long bone. Bones such as femur, tibia, humerus etc. generally of the limbs whose length far exceeds its breadth and thickness, one among the classification on asṭhiaccording to Ayurveda based on shape. Category: bone (asthi).
title: nalakāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hanvasthi (हन्वस्थि; SAT SAT-B.271): mandible. The horseshoe-shaped bone forming the lower jaw which gives attachment to the lower jaw of teeth. Category: bone (asthi).
title: hanvasthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tālvasthi (ताल्वस्थि; SAT SAT-B.272): bones of palate. Two halves of the bones forming the anterior part of the palate consisting of the maxillary and palatine bones. Category: bone (asthi).
title: tālvasthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: akṣaḥ (अक्षः/ अक्षकः/ कीलकः/ कोष्ठकम्/ कोष्ठकास्थि; SAT SAT-B.273): clavicle. Also called akṣakaḥ, kīlakaḥ, koṣṭhakam and koṣṭhakāsthi. Collar bone; bone which articulates with the sternum and the scapula. Category: bone (asthi).
title: akṣaḥ akṣakaḥ kīlakaḥ koṣṭhakam koṣṭhakāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsaphalakaḥ (अंसफलकः; SAT SAT-B.274): scapula. Large flat triangular bone that forms the posterior part of shoulder. Category: bone (asthi).
title: aṁsaphalakaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uraḥphalakam (उरःफलकम्; SAT SAT-B.275): sternum. Flat bone consisting of three parts, the manubrium, the body, and the xiphoid process which forms the middle of the anterior wall of the thorax and articulating with the clavicles and the cartilages of the first seven ribs. Category: bone (asthi).
title: uraḥphalakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parśukā (पर्शुका; SAT SAT-B.276): rib/costa. Curved bones extending laterally and anteriorly from sides of thoracic vertebrae and forming skeletal thorax. Category: bone (asthi).
title: parśukā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parśukāgram (पर्शुकाग्रम्; SAT SAT-B.277): anterior end of the rib. Anterior end of rib usually covered with cartilage. Category: bone (asthi).
title: parśukāgram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthālakam (स्थालकम्; SAT SAT-B.278): head of the rib. The rounded medial extremity of a rib that, except for ribs 1, 10, 11, and 12, articulates by two facets with the bodies of vertebrae. Category: bone (asthi).
title: sthālakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthālakārbudam (स्थालकार्बुदम्; SAT SAT-B.279): tubercle of rib. The small rounded elevation on the posterior surface of a rib, at the junction of its neck and shaft, which articulates with the transverse process of the vertebra. Category: bone (asthi).
title: sthālakārbudam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bāhunalakam (बाहुनलकम्; SAT SAT-B.280): humerus. The bone of the upper arm, extending from shoulder to elbow. Category: bone (asthi).
title: bāhunalakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṅgulāsthi (अङ्गुलास्थि; SAT SAT-B.281): phalange. Any one of the bones of toes or fingers. Category: bone (asthi).
title: aṅgulāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṭikapālaḥ (कटिकपालः/ जघनकपालः; SAT SAT-B.282): hip bone. Also called jaghanakapālaḥ. Pair of irregularly shaped bones which form the pelvis along with the sacral bone. Category: bone (asthi).
title: kaṭikapālaḥ jaghanakapālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kuṭakāsthi (कुटकास्थि/ मयूरास्थि; SAT SAT-B.283): sacrum/ sacrum with coccyx. Also called mayūrāsthi. Bones forming the lower part of the vertebral column. Category: bone (asthi).
title: kuṭakāsthi mayūrāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhagāsthi (भगास्थि; SAT SAT-B.284): pubis. A part of hip bone which articulates with its fellow on the opposite side to form the pubic symphysis. Category: bone (asthi).
title: bhagāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jānukapālikā (जानुकपालिका; SAT SAT-B.285): patella. Largest sesamoid bone of the body which forms in the tendon of quadriceps muscle. Category: bone (asthi).
title: jānukapālikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrunalakam (ऊरुनलकम्/ ऊर्वस्थि; SAT SAT-B.286): femur. Also called ūrvasthi. Thigh bone; the longest and strongest bone in the body which extends from the pelvis to the knee and articulates proximally with the acetabulum and distally with the upper end of tibia. Category: bone (asthi).
title: ūrunalakam ūrvasthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jaṅghāsthinī (जङ्घास्थिनी; SAT SAT-B.287): tibia and fibula. Bones of the leg. Category: bone (asthi).
title: jaṅghāsthinī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pārṣṇyasthi (पार्ष्ण्यस्थि; SAT SAT-B.288): calcaneus. Heel bone. Category: bone (asthi).
title: pārṣṇyasthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādakurcāsthi (पादकुर्चास्थि; SAT SAT-B.289): tarsal bones excluding talus and calcaneus. Bones which give attachment to metacarpals of foot. Category: bone (asthi).
title: pādakurcāsthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāṇiśalākādhiṣṭhānam (पाणिशलाकाधिष्ठानम्; SAT SAT-B.290): distal row of carpal bones. The row of carpal bones which give attachment to the metacarpal bones of the upper limb. Category: bone (asthi).
title: pāṇiśalākādhiṣṭhānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sandhiḥ (सन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.291): joint/articulation. The site of the junction or union of two or more bones of the body. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: sandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthisaṅghātaḥ (अस्थिसङ्घातः; SAT SAT-B.292): conglomeration of bones. Sites where more than two bones articulate or come together. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: asthisaṅghātaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ceṣṭāvantasandhiḥ (चेष्टावन्तसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.293): movable joint. Joint characterized by the presence of a cavity within the capsule separating the bony elements. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: ceṣṭāvantasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: korasandhiḥ (कोरसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.294): condyloid and hinge joint. Type of joint in which movement occurs in one plane. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: korasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ulūkhalasandhiḥ (उलूखलसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.295): ball and socket joint. Joint in which the round end of one bone fits into the cavity of other. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: ulūkhalasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tunnasevanī (तुन्नसेवनी; SAT SAT-B.296): sutural joint. Type of fibrous joint mainly seen in the skull which has limited movement. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: tunnasevanī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: grīvā-adhaḥsandhiḥ (ग्रीवा-अधःसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.297): sternoclavicular joint. Joint space between the sternum and the medial extrimity of the clavicle. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: grīvā-adhaḥsandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jatrusandhiḥ (जत्रुसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.298): sternoclavicular joint. Joint space between the sternum and the medial extrimity of the clavicle. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: jatrusandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: akṣakasandhiḥ (अक्षकसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.299): sterno-clavicular joint. Joint formed between manubrium of the sternum and the medial end of clavicle. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: akṣakasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṁsasandhiḥ (अंससन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.300): shoulder joint. Joint formed by humerus and glenoid cavity of scapula. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: aṁsasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kūrparasandhiḥ (कूर्परसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.301): elbow joint. Joint between arm and forearm. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: kūrparasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṭisandhiḥ (कटिसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.302): hip joint. Joint between the acetabulum of the hip bone and the rounded head of the femur. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: kaṭisandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jānusandhiḥ (जानुसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.303): knee joint. The joint between the distal end of femur and the condyles of tibia. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: jānusandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jānvadhaḥsandhiḥ (जान्वधःसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.304): proximal tibio-fibular joint. Upper tibiofibular joint. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: jānvadhaḥsandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gulphasandhiḥ (गुल्फसन्धिः; SAT SAT-B.305): ankle joint. Joint between tibia, fibula and talus bones. Category: joint/articulation (sandhiḥ).
title: gulphasandhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: snāyuḥ (स्नायुः; SAT SAT-B.306): sinew. Includes connective tissue elements such as ligaments, tendons, nerves etc. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: snāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratānavatī snāyuḥ (प्रतानवती स्नायुः; SAT SAT-B.307): nerve. Cord like structures comprising of nerve fibres, part of the nervous system. Category: sinew (snāyuḥ).
title: pratānavatī snāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vṛttasnāyuḥ (वृत्तस्नायुः; SAT SAT-B.308): tendon. Band of fibrous tissue connecting muscle to a bone. Category: sinew (snāyuḥ).
title: vṛttasnāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pṛthulā snāyuḥ (पृथुला-स्नायुः; SAT SAT-B.309): aponeurosis. Fibrous or membranous sheet of connective tissue that serves to attach muscle to bone. Category: sinew (snāyuḥ).
title: pṛthulā snāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

It performs the functions like controlling the intellect, heart, sensory and motor organs and mind. It also regulates the activities like respiration, spitting, sneezing, belching and swallowing. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: prāṇa-vāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ambarapīyūṣam (अम्बरपीयूषम्; SAT SAT-B.386): nectar from sky. A nectar-like vital entity present in the atmosphere, indicative of oxygen. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: ambarapīyūṣam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāṇaḥ (प्राणः; SAT SAT-B.387): the breath of life. Also denoted by filled with life; spirit; vitality. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: prāṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāṇāpānau (प्राणापानौ; SAT SAT-B.388): respiration. The combined term for both inspiration and expiration. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: prāṇāpānau

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udāna-vāyuḥ (उदान-वायुः; SAT SAT-B.389): one of the five subtypes of vāta (vāyu), that is seated in thorax. One of the five subtypes of vāta (vāyu) that is seated in thorax. It performs the functions like effort, strength and recollection required for the production of speech. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: udāna-vāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyānavāyuḥ (व्यानवायुः; SAT SAT-B.390): a subtype of vāta, that is seated in hṛdaya. Subtype of vāta, that is seated in hṛdaya. It is responsible for the circulation of rasa from hṛdaya to all parts of the body. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: vyānavāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samāna-vāyuḥ (समान-वायुः; SAT SAT-B.391): one of the five subtypes of vāta (vāyu) that is seated in proximity to agni. One of the five subtypes of vāta (vāyu) that is seated in proximity to agni (in between stomach and large intestine). It performs the functions like receiving the food, digestion of the food, division of the food into useful and waste portions, and propulsion of the food. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: samāna-vāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: apāna-vāyuḥ (अपान-वायुः; SAT SAT-B.392): one of the five subtypes of vāta (vāyu), situated in the pelvic region. One of the five subtypes of data (vāta), situated in the pelvic region. It performs the functions like defecation, micturition, parturition, menstruation, and ejaculation. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: apāna-vāyuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāyu-karma (वायु-कर्म; SAT SAT-B.393): functions of vātadoṣa. Combined term for functions of vāta doṣa such as utsāha, uchhvāsa, ceṣṭā etc. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: vāyu-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: utsāhaḥ (उत्साहः; SAT SAT-B.394): enthusiasm. Enthusiasm, motivation, effort, activness, to have willingness to do adventure. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: utsāhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ucchvāsaḥ (उच्छ्वासः; SAT SAT-B.395): breath, expiration. Flow of air from the lungs to the exterior to due to the elastic recoil of the lungs. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: ucchvāsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: niḥśvāsaḥ (निःश्वासः; SAT SAT-B.396): inspiration, inhalation. A function of prāṇa vāta; the flow of air from the exterior to the lungs due to the contraction of respriratory muscles, mainly diaphragm. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: niḥśvāsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ceṣṭā (चेष्टा; SAT SAT-B.397): motion, action, function. A function of vyāna vāta; motor functions of the body including movements of limbs etc. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: ceṣṭā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gatiḥ (गतिः; SAT SAT-B.398): motion, moving, gait. Movements happening within the body such as transportation of dhātu etc. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: gatiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nimeṣaḥ (निमेषः; SAT SAT-B.399): closure of the eyelids. Movement of the eye lid resulting from the contraction of orbicularis oculi muscle supplied by facial nerve. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: nimeṣaḥ
