source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: unmeṣaḥ (उन्मेषः; SAT SAT-B.400): opening of eyelids. The movement of eye lid due to action of levator palpebrae superioris supplied by the trigeminal nerve. Category: functions of vātadoṣa (vāyu-karma).
title: unmeṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pittam (पित्तम्; SAT SAT-B.401): doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities. One of the three bodily doṣa that is responsible for digestion and metabolism in the body which is agni mahābhūta predominant. This is of five subtypes: pācaka, ālocaka, rañjaka, bhrājaka and sādhaka. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: pittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pācaka-pittam (पाचक-पित्तम्; SAT SAT-B.402): one of the five subtypes of pitta that is situated in between the āmāśaya and pakvāśaya. One of the five subtypes of pitta that is situated in between the āmāśaya and pakvāśaya which divides the food into sāra (nutritive) and kitta (waste) portions and also supports other subtypes of pitta. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities (pittam).
title: pācaka-pittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rañjakapittam (रञ्जकपित्तम्; SAT SAT-B.403): one of the five subtypes of pitta that is situated in yakṛt and plīhā. One of the five subtypes of pitta that is situated in yakṛt and plīhā. This transforms rasa-dhātuḥ into rakta-dhātu. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities (pittam).
title: rañjakapittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ālocaka-pittam (आलोचक-पित्तम्; SAT SAT-B.404): one of the five subtypes of pitta that is responsible for vision and perception. One of the five subtypes of pitta that is responsible for vision and perception. It is of two types- buddhi vaiśeṣika and dṛṣti vaiśeṣika. The former is at the level of intelligence and latter at the level of the sense organ (eye). Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities (pittam).
title: ālocaka-pittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhrājakapittam (भ्राजकपित्तम्; SAT SAT-B.405): one of the five subtypes of pitta that causes illumination or shining of the skin. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities (pittam).
title: bhrājakapittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sādhakapittam (साधकपित्तम्; SAT SAT-B.406): one of the five subtypes of pitta situated in the hṛdaya. The pitta responsible for seeking of objects desired by the intellect or self esteem. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities (pittam).
title: sādhakapittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pitta-karma (पित्त-कर्म; SAT SAT-B.407): functions of pitta. The pitta responsible for functions such as prabhā, pakti, darśana etc. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body temperature and metabolic activities (pittam).
title: pitta-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prabhā (प्रभा; SAT SAT-B.408): lustre. Caused due to agni mahābhūta predominance. Category: functions of pitta (pitta-karma).
title: prabhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣudhā (क्षुधा; SAT SAT-B.409): hunger. Sensation associated with the desire for food. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: kṣudhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: darśanam (दर्शनम्; SAT SAT-B.410): vision. Perception of form, colour etc. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: darśanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: paktiḥ (पक्तिः; SAT SAT-B.411): metabolic transformation. Process of digestive / metablic transformation resulting from the action of agni. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: paktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śauryam (शौर्यम्; SAT SAT-B.412): valour. Readiness to face adverse situations or danger. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: śauryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tṛṣṇā (तृष्णा/ पिपासा; SAT SAT-B.413): thirst. Also called pipāsā. Sensation of dryness in the mouth and throat associated with a desire for liquids. Category: suprasternal notch (grīvāmūlam).
title: tṛṣṇā pipāsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śleṣmā (श्लेष्मा/ कफः; SAT SAT-B.414): doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive. Also called kaphaḥ. One among the three doṣa responsible for stability, unctousness, lubrication, immunity, and cohesion. This is predominant of pṛthvī and jala mahābhūta. The five subtypes are avalambaka, kledaka, bodhaka, śleṣaka, tarpaka. Category: three regulatory functional factors of the body (tridoṣaḥ).
title: śleṣmā kaphaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avalambaka-kaphaḥ (अवलम्बक-कफः; SAT SAT-B.415): one of the subtypes of kapha situated in the chest region. Supports and sustains the heart and other sites of kapha. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: avalambaka-kaphaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kledaka-kaphaḥ (क्लेदक-कफः; SAT SAT-B.416): one of the subtypes of kapha situated in the āmāśaya. Causes moistening and losening of the food particles to help in the process of digestion. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: kledaka-kaphaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bodhaka-kaphaḥ (बोधक-कफः; SAT SAT-B.417): one of the subtypes of kapha situated on the tongue. Helps in the perception of taste; comparable to saliva. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: bodhaka-kaphaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tarpaka-kaphaḥ (तर्पक-कफः; SAT SAT-B.418): one of the subtypes of kapha situated in the head region. Nourishes the different sensory organs. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: tarpaka-kaphaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śleṣaka-kaphaḥ (श्लेषक-कफः; SAT SAT-B.419): one of the subtypes of kapha situated in the joints. Provides lubrication to the joints. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: śleṣaka-kaphaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaphasthānam (कफस्थानम्; SAT SAT-B.420): seat of kapha. Includes chest, head, joints, stomach etc. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: kaphasthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kapha-karma (कफ-कर्म; SAT SAT-B.421): actions of kapha. Functions such as dārḍhya, kṣamā etc. Category: doṣa responsible for regulating body fluids and keeping the body constituents cohesive (śleṣmā).
title: kapha-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣamā (क्षमा; SAT SAT-B.422): patience. Patience, forebearance, forgiveness, resistance. Category: actions of kapha (kapha-karma).
title: kṣamā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dārḍhyam (दार्ढ्यम्; SAT SAT-B.423): firmness. Hardness, fixedness, stability, strength. Category: actions of kapha (kapha-karma).
title: dārḍhyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dūṣyam (दूष्यम्; SAT SAT-B.424): which gets vitiated. Any bodily structure that gets vitiated by aggravated doṣa. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: dūṣyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhātuḥ (धातुः; SAT SAT-B.425): major structural components of the body. Seven major structural components that stabilize and sustain the body (rasa, rakta, māmsa, meda, asthi, majjā and śukra). The previous dhātu nourishes the next in a sequential fashion. Each dhātu is of two forms: A. sthāyi (stable) and poṣaka(nourishing) B. asthāyi and poṣya dhātu; Each dhātu undergoes a cyclical process of origin, maturation and degeneration. Category: which gets vitiated (dūṣyam).
title: dhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhāraṇam (धारणम्; SAT SAT-B.426): holding. Holding, carrying, preserving, protecting, possessing; Common function of all dhātu; Specific function of asthi dhātu. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: dhāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhātusāmyam (धातुसाम्यम्; SAT SAT-B.427): equilibrium of dhātu. Equilibrium of dhātu which is indicated by absence/alleviation of disorder. Criteria for dhātusāmya include alleviation of disorder, normalcy of voice and complexion, development of body, increase in strength, desire for food, proper and timely digestion of the food taken, timely sleep, elimination of urine, faeces and semen and overall normalcy of mind, intellect and sense organs. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: dhātusāmyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasa-dhātuḥ (रस-धातुः; SAT SAT-B.428): primary product of digested food. First dhātu among seven dhātu and is dominated by jala; this is pumped out of hṛdaya and continuously circulates all over the body to nourish other tissues; it is of nine añjali in quantity; vyāna and samāna vāyu help in its circulation. the major function of rasa dhātu is prīṇana (nourishing). Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: rasa-dhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rakta-dhātuḥ (रक्त-धातुः; SAT SAT-B.429): blood tissue. Second dhātu among seven dhātu whose function is jivana (to give life). It is formed in yakṛt (liver) and plīhā (spleen) with the help of rañjakapitta and rakta dhātvagni. This is dominant in agni mahābhūta. It is named so because of its red colour. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: rakta-dhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śoṇitam (शोणितम्; SAT SAT-B.430): blood. Synonym of rakta. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: śoṇitam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jīvanam (जीवनम्; SAT SAT-B.431): to give life. One of the functions of rakta dhātu. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: jīvanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: raktapuṣṭiḥ (रक्तपुष्टिः; SAT SAT-B.432): nourishment of raktadhātu. One of the functions of rasadhātu. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: raktapuṣṭiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: māṁsa-dhātuḥ (मांस-धातुः; SAT SAT-B.433): muscle tissue. Third among the seven dhātu, whose function is to provide covering over the skeleton. It is dominant of pṛthvī mahābhūta. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: māṁsa-dhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: peśī (पेशी; SAT SAT-B.434): muscle. Type of tissue composed of contractile cells or fibers. Category: muscle tissue (māṁsa-dhātuḥ).
title: peśī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: medo-dhātuḥ (मेदो-धातुः; SAT SAT-B.435): fat tissue. Fourth among seven dhātu of the body, whose function is to provide snehana (oleation). It is dominant of jala and pṛthvī mahābhūta designative of adipose tissue and other lipids in the body. Category: muscle tissue (māṁsa-dhātuḥ).
title: medo-dhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthi-dhātuḥ (अस्थि-धातुः; SAT SAT-B.436): bone tissue. Fifth of the seven basic dhātu, whose function is to provide stability to the body. It is predominant of pṛthvī and ākāśa mahābhūta. It is comparable to bone tissue (specialized form of dense connective tissue consisting of bone cells embedded in a matrix made of calcified intercellular substance). Category: muscle tissue (māṁsa-dhātuḥ).
title: asthi-dhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāṇḍam (काण्डम्; SAT SAT-B.437): shaft of the bone. Central or core part of bone. Category: bone tissue (asthi-dhātuḥ).
title: kāṇḍam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṇvasthi (अण्वस्थि; SAT SAT-B.438): short bones. Short bones such as carpal bones, tarsal bones etc. Category: bone tissue (asthi-dhātuḥ).
title: aṇvasthi

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthiparva (अस्थिपर्व; SAT SAT-B.439): joint. Articulation or junction between two bones. Category: bone tissue (asthi-dhātuḥ).
title: asthiparva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthipañjaraḥ (अस्थिपञ्जरः; SAT SAT-B.440): bony skeleton. Bone framework of the body. Category: bone tissue (asthi-dhātuḥ).
title: asthipañjaraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthivivaram (अस्थिविवरम्; SAT SAT-B.441): medullary canal. Cavity within the bone containing marrow. Category: bone tissue (asthi-dhātuḥ).
title: asthivivaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthisandhayaḥ (अस्थिसन्धयः; SAT SAT-B.442): articulation/joint. Point of junction between two bones. Category: bone tissue (asthi-dhātuḥ).
title: asthisandhayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: majjā-dhātuḥ (मज्जा-धातुः/ अस्थिसारम्/ अस्थिस्नेहः; SAT SAT-B.443): bone marrow. Also called asthisāram and asthisnehaḥ. Sixth of the seven basic dhātu, whose function is to fill the bony cavities. It is predominance of jala mahābhūta; the soft organic material that fills the cavities of the bones. Category: muscle tissue (māṁsa-dhātuḥ).
title: majjā-dhātuḥ asthisāram asthisnehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pūraṇam (पूरणम्; SAT SAT-B.444): filling up. Filling up, completing, something used to fill a cavity or container. The primary function of majjā dhātu. Category: bone marrow (majjā-dhātuḥ).
title: pūraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukradhātuḥ (शुक्रधातुः; SAT SAT-B.445): reproductive fluids; semen. Seventh dhātu having the function of reproduction which is generally equated with semen; present in two forms: former pervading the entire body and the latter which fertilizes the ovum. It is dominant in jala mahābhūta. Category: major structural components of the body (dhātuḥ).
title: śukradhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: retaḥ (रेतः; SAT SAT-B.446): semen. Part of śukradhātu which forms the ejaculate and carries the male gametes. Category: reproductive fluids; semen (śukradhātuḥ).
title: retaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: strībījam (स्त्रीबीजम्; SAT SAT-B.447): ovum. Female sexual entity capable of developing into a new individual of the same species when fertilized by spermatozoa. Category: reproductive fluids; semen (śukradhātuḥ).
title: strībījam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vṛṣatā (वृषता; SAT SAT-B.448): virility. Generative power, ability to reproduce. Category: reproductive fluids; semen (śukradhātuḥ).
title: vṛṣatā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kārmuka-bījam (कार्मुक-बीजम्; SAT SAT-B.449): healthy sperm/ovum. Normal, healthy and effective sperm/ovum. Category: reproductive fluids; semen (śukradhātuḥ).
title: kārmuka-bījam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ojaḥ (ओजः; SAT SAT-B.450): essence of all seven dhātu. Essence of all seven dhātu, that is vital for life characterized by bala (immunity). It is of two types: 1. para, which is present in the hṛdaya and 2. apara, which is present all over the body. The ten attributes of ojas are: guru (heavy), śīta (cold), mṛdu (soft), ślakṣṇa (smooth), bahala (abundant), madhura (sweet), sthira (stable), prasanna (bright), picchila (sticky) and snigdha (unctuous). Category: which gets vitiated (dūṣyam).
title: ojaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upadhātuḥ (उपधातुः; SAT SAT-B.451): the minor structural components that stabilize and sustain the body. By-products of convertion of one dhātu to the next which are essential for the body. Unlike dhātu, they do not transform further into another dhātu. Category: which gets vitiated (dūṣyam).
title: upadhātuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: stanyam (स्तन्यम्; SAT SAT-B.452): breast milk. Upadhātu of rasadhātu which is dominant of jala mahābhūta and nourishes the baby. Category: the minor structural components that stabilize and sustain the body (upadhātuḥ).
title: stanyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ārtavam (आर्तवम्/ पुष्पम्/ आर्तवशोणितम्/ अन्तःपुष्पम्/ रजस्रावः/शोणितम्; SAT SAT-B.453): menstrual blood. Also called puṣpam, ārtavaśoṇitam, antaḥpuṣpam, rajasrāvaḥ and śoṇitam. Monthly periodic physiological uterine bleeding through vagina, with the duration of 3-7 days symbolizing the forthcoming fertile period; also used in some contexts for ovum and the functionality of female reproductive hormones and also. Category: the minor structural components that stabilize and sustain the body (upadhātuḥ).
title: ārtavam puṣpam ārtavaśoṇitam antaḥpuṣpam rajasrāvaḥ śoṇitam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṇḍarā (कण्डरा; SAT SAT-B.454): tendon. A band of fibrous tissue connecting muscle to a bone. Kaṇḍarā is an upadhātu of raktadhātu. Category: the minor structural components that stabilize and sustain the body (upadhātuḥ).
title: kaṇḍarā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sirā (सिरा; SAT SAT-B.455): any tubular vessel of the body. Commonly used for veins. Category: the minor structural components that stabilize and sustain the body (upadhātuḥ).
title: sirā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vasā (वसा; SAT SAT-B.456): muscle fat. Unctuous portion of pure māṁsa which is the upadhātu of māṁsa dhātu. Category: the minor structural components that stabilize and sustain the body (upadhātuḥ).
title: vasā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: malaḥ (मलः; SAT SAT-B.457): waste products. One of the fundamental constituent of the human body along with doṣa and dhātu which include the various waste products formed during various stages of digestion and metabolism. Mala are of two classes: āhāramala and dhātumala. āhāramala include mūtra (urine) and purīṣa (faeces). Category: which gets vitiated (dūṣyam).
title: malaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kiṭṭam (किट्टम्; SAT SAT-B.458): waste product. By-products of metabolism which are to be eliminated from the body. Category: waste products (malaḥ).
title: kiṭṭam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: purīṣam (पुरीषम्; SAT SAT-B.459): faeces. One of the āhāramala, the function of which is to support the body in general and vāyu and agni in particular. Category: waste products (malaḥ).
title: purīṣam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūtram (मूत्रम्; SAT SAT-B.460): urine. One of the āhāra-mala whose function is to carry away kleda (watery waste) from the body. Category: waste products (malaḥ).
title: mūtram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śakṛt (शकृत्; SAT SAT-B.461): feaces. Synonym of purīṣa. Category: waste products (malaḥ).
title: śakṛt

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svedaḥ (स्वेदः; SAT SAT-B.462): sweat. Mala of meda dhātu whose function is to withhold kleda (watery portion) in the skin. Category: waste products (malaḥ).
title: svedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viṭ (विट्/विड्; SAT SAT-B.463): excreta. Also called viḍ. Waste products of the body especially faeces. Category: waste products (malaḥ).
title: viṭ viḍ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: balam (बलम्; SAT SAT-B.464): immunity/ strength/physical endurance. Classified in 3 types: sahaja – hereditary, yuktikṛta- gained from exercise, food, rasāyana etc. kālaja – natural strength attained during visargakāla i.e. varṣā ṛtu (rainy season) , śarad ṛtu (autumn) and hemanta ṛtu (early winter). Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: balam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sahaja-balam (सहज-बलम्; SAT SAT-B.465): innate immunity. Immunity present since birth. Category: immunity/ strength/physical endurance (balam).
title: sahaja-balam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yuktikṛta-balam (युक्तिकृत-बलम्; SAT SAT-B.466): artificial immunity. Immunity attained by artifitial means such as rasāyana. Category: immunity/ strength/physical endurance (balam).
title: yuktikṛta-balam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālaja-balam (कालज-बलम्; SAT SAT-B.467): temporal strength, acquired immunity. Strength of the body attained by virtue of favourable season, such as hemanta ṛtu (early winter). Category: immunity/ strength/physical endurance (balam).
title: kālaja-balam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: srotas (स्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.468): structural or functional channels. Structural or functional channels meant for the transportation of dhātu undergoing transformation having appearance similar to the dhātu that it transports. They are of two types: sthūla (macro) and aṇu (micro). Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: srotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāyacchidram (कायच्छिद्रम्; SAT SAT-B.469): apertures of the body. The external and internal openings of the body. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: kāyacchidram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anilāyanam (अनिलायनम्; SAT SAT-B.470): air passages. Passages for air inside the body. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: anilāyanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antarmukhasrotas (अन्तर्मुखस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.471): internal channels. Internal tracts, channels, tubes, ducts. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: antarmukhasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adhaḥsrotaḥ (अधःस्रोतः; SAT SAT-B.472): anal or urethral passage. Lower passages of the body. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: adhaḥsrotaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāṇavahasrotas (प्राणवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.473): channels carrying prāṇa/ channels of respiration/respiratory system. Channels which carry prāṇa throughout the body which originate from the hṛdaya and circulate throughout the body. It is compared to the respiratory system and the diseases of prāṇavahasrotas are to be treated on the basis of treatment principles of respiratory diseses like śwāsa. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: prāṇavahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ārtavavaha-srotas (आर्तववह-स्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.474): fallopian or uterine tubes. Also includes the channels with physiological importance in regulation of menstrual cycles (hypothalamo-pituitary-ovarian axis). Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: ārtavavaha-srotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ambuvaha srotas (अम्बुवह स्रोतस्/ उदकवहस्रोतस्/ अम्बुमार्गः; SAT SAT-B.475): channels/pathways for fluid circulation. Also called udakavahasrotas and ambumārgaḥ. Pathways which originate from the tālu or kloma through which fluids circulate throughout the body. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: ambuvaha srotas udakavahasrotas ambumārgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asṛgvahā (असृग्वहा; SAT SAT-B.476): blood vessels. Veins, arteries and capillaries. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: asṛgvahā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ucchvāsamārgaḥ (उच्छ्वासमार्गः; SAT SAT-B.477): respiratory tract. Pathway for inhaled and exhaled air extending from the external nares to the alveoli. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: ucchvāsamārgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: annavahasrotas (अन्नवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.478): digestive tract. Channels carrying food which is in the process of digestion. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: annavahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasavahasrotas (रसवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.479): channels carrying nutrient fluids. Channels which carry and distribute the primary products of digestion to nourish the various body tissues which originate from the hṛdaya and rasavaha dhamanī. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: rasavahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: raktavahasrotas (रक्तवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.480): channels carrying blood tissue. Originates from the yakṛt and plīhā. Some of the diseases involving this srotas include kuṣṭha, visarpa, raktapitta, vidradhi etc. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: raktavahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: māṁsavahasrotas (मांसवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.481): channels carrying muscle tissue. Originates from the snāyu and tvacā. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: māṁsavahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: medovahasrotas (मेदोवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.482): channels carrying fat tissue. Originates from vṛkka and vapāvahana and is associated with diseases such as sṭhaulya. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: medovahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asthivahasrotas (अस्थिवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.483): channels carrying bone tissue. Originates from medas and jaghana. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: asthivahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: majjāvahasrotas (मज्जावहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.484): channels carrying bone marrow. Originates from asṭhi and sandhi. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: majjāvahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukravahasrotas (शुक्रवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.485): channels carrying reproductive tissues. Originates from vṛṣaṇa and śepha and is associated with diseases such as klaibya. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: śukravahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūtravahasrotas (मूत्रवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.486): urinary tract. Channels in which urine is formed and excreted which originates from the vasti and vaṁkṣana and is involved in diseases such as prameha, mūtrakṛchra, aśmari etc. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: mūtravahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: purīṣavahasrotas (पुरीषवहस्रोतस्; SAT SAT-B.487): channels in which faeces is formed and excreted. Originates from pakvāśaya and sṭhūlaguda and is involved in diseases such as atisāra, pravāhikā etc. Category: structural or functional channels (srotas).
title: purīṣavahasrotas

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: agniḥ (अग्निः; SAT SAT-B.488): digestive/metabolic factors. All factors responsible for digestion and metabolism / transformation having predominance of agnimahābhūta. This is of three classes: jatharāgni bhūtāgni and dhātvagni. The intensity of āgni is influenced by doṣa and is of four types: viṣama (irregular due to the dominance of vāta), tīkṣna (intense, due to the dominance of pitta), manda (depressed due to the dominance of kapha) and sama (normal, due to the balanced state of all three. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: agniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāyāgniḥ (कायाग्निः; SAT SAT-B.489): metabolic factors of the body. Factors responsible for digestion and metabolism / transformation. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: kāyāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jāṭharāgniḥ (जाठराग्निः; SAT SAT-B.490): metabolic factors located in digestive tract. Agni responsible for digestion of food in the gastro intestinal tract. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: jāṭharāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhātvagniḥ (धात्वग्निः; SAT SAT-B.491): metabolic factors located in dhātu. Agni located in the dhatu responsible for transformation of one dhātu into another namely rasāgni, raktāgni, māṁsāgni, medo-agni, asthyagni and śukrāgni. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: dhātvagniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhūtāgniḥ (भूताग्निः; SAT SAT-B.492): metabolic factors acting at the level of mahābhūta. Five types of āgni, those act after jāṭharāgni, but before dhātvagni on the food and its metabolites. They are: pārthiva, āpya, taijasa, vāyavya and nābhasa. They act on the corresponding substrate based on mahābhūta composition to make them homologous to that of the bodily constituents. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: bhūtāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samāgniḥ (समाग्निः; SAT SAT-B.493): normal state of agni. State in which the action of agni is normal due to a balanced state of all the three doṣa. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: samāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tīkṣṇāgniḥ (तीक्ष्णाग्निः; SAT SAT-B.494): intense state of agni. State in which the action of agni is considerably intensified due to dominant influence of pitta. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: tīkṣṇāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viṣamāgniḥ (विषमाग्निः; SAT SAT-B.495): irregular state of agni. State in which the action of agni is rendered erratic (either excessive or decreased, variable from time to time) due to the dominant influence of vāta. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: viṣamāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mandāgniḥ (मन्दाग्निः; SAT SAT-B.496): depressed/weak state of agni. State in which the action of agni is weak/depressed due to dominant influence of kapha. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: mandāgniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pākaḥ (पाकः; SAT SAT-B.497): digestion or transformation. The function of agni mahābhūta. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: pākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jaraṇaśaktiḥ (जरणशक्तिः; SAT SAT-B.498): digestive power. Capacity to digest the consumed food. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: jaraṇaśaktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abhyavaharaṇa-śaktiḥ (अभ्यवहरण-शक्तिः; SAT SAT-B.499): power of ingestion. Capacity of food intake; the quantity of the food which does not disturb the physiological function of an individual. This differs from person to person and time to time, it directly depends on the digestive fire and psychological status of the person. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: abhyavaharaṇa-śaktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: trividha-kukṣiḥ (त्रिविध-कुक्षिः; SAT SAT-B.500): three divisions of stomach capacity. Division of stomach capacity into three parts,such as one portion of the space for solid items, one for liquids and one part to be left empty for vāta, pitta and kapha. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: trividha-kukṣiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pācanam (पाचनम्; SAT SAT-B.501): digestion. Process of digestive / metablic transformation occuring mainly because of the action of āgni. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: pācanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prasādaḥ (प्रसादः; SAT SAT-B.502): nutrient part of food. Nutrient portion formed during various processes of biotransformation. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: prasādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avasthā-pākaḥ (अवस्था-पाकः; SAT SAT-B.503): phases of digestion. Three phases of correspondingly producing kapha, pitta and vāta. Category: digestive/metabolic factors (agniḥ).
title: avasthā-pākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: antarbahirvibhāgaḥ (अन्तर्बहिर्विभागः; SAT SAT-B.504): internal-external division. Arbitrary division into interior and exterior parts for descriptive purposes. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: antarbahirvibhāgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uttarādhara-vibhāgaḥ (उत्तराधर-विभागः; SAT SAT-B.505): superior-inferior division. Superior (proximal) and inferior (distal) classification of the body for descriptive purposes. Category: internal-external division (antarbahirvibhāgaḥ).
title: uttarādhara-vibhāgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pūrvapaścima-vibhāgaḥ (पूर्वपश्चिम-विभागः; SAT SAT-B.506): anterior-posterior division. Anterior (ventral) and posterior (dorsal) classification of the body for descriptive purposes. Category: internal-external division (antarbahirvibhāgaḥ).
title: pūrvapaścima-vibhāgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: koṣṭhaḥ (कोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.507): nature of bowel. Dependending on the dominance of doṣa, depending on the ability to digest the food, and depending on the bowel movements, the koṣṭha of an individual can be classified as krūra, mṛdu and madhyama. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: koṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: madhyama-koṣṭhaḥ (मध्यम-कोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.508): normal bowel nature. Physiological type of koṣṭha produced because of the dominance of either kapha, or due to the balanced state of all the three doṣa. The individual with this type of koṣṭha passes normal bowels and has normal digestive ability. Category: nature of bowel (koṣṭhaḥ).
title: madhyama-koṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mṛdukoṣṭhaḥ (मृदुकोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.509): loose nature of bowel. Physiological type of koṣṭha produced because of the dominance of pitta. The individual with this type of koṣṭha passes soft bowels and has good digestive ability. Category: nature of bowel (koṣṭhaḥ).
title: mṛdukoṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: krūra-koṣṭhaḥ (क्रूर-कोष्ठः; SAT SAT-B.510): irregular nature of bowel. Physiological type of koṣṭha produced because of the dominance of vāta. The individual with this type of koṣṭha, passes hard stools and has irregular digestive ability. Category: nature of bowel (koṣṭhaḥ).
title: krūra-koṣṭhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vegaḥ (वेगः; SAT SAT-B.511): natural urges (for elimination). Natural urges for elimination which are of two types dhāraṇīya (suppressible) such as greed, anger etc and adhāraṇīya (non suppressible) such as sneezing, sleep etc. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: vegaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adhāraṇīya-vegaḥ (अधारणीय-वेगः; SAT SAT-B.512): non- suppressible urges. Natural urges of the body which should not be supressed. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: adhāraṇīya-vegaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pramāṇam (प्रमाणम्; SAT SAT-B.513): anthropometry. Measurements of the body in terms of height,breadth and length described in proportions of width of individual's fingers. Category: body (śarīraḥ).
title: pramāṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhiḥ (व्याधिः; SAT SAT-C.1): disease/ syndrome. The term signifies disease or ailment which brings about grief or pain to the individual; the word meaning implies an abnormal state of distress or pain, wherein the mind resolves to counteract the disturbances in the body to bring a healthy state. vyadhi brings about distress to physical and mental wellbeing of individual.
title: vyādhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhiparyāyaḥ (व्याधिपर्यायः; SAT SAT-C.2): synonym of disease. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: vyādhiparyāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āmayaḥ (आमयः; SAT SAT-C.3): disease/ syndrome. The structure of the word signifies the diseases originating in the body secondary to disturbances in the process of digestion, due to accumulation of āma in body channels. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: āmayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gadaḥ (गदः; SAT SAT-C.4): disease/ syndrome. The term implies diseases that arise out of multiple factors simultaneously. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: gadaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ātaṅkaḥ (आतङ्कः; SAT SAT-C.5): disease/ syndrome. The term signifies that disease makes life miserable by causing fear, terror or distress in the person. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: ātaṅkaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yakṣmā (यक्ष्मा; SAT SAT-C.6): disease/ syndrome. The term implies diseases characterised by a constellation of symptoms which occur together. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: yakṣmā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jvaraḥ (ज्वर:; SAT SAT-C.7): disease/ syndrome. Jwara is the most important among diseases and here the term implies the ability of a disease to cause anguish to mind and body. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: jvaraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vikāraḥ (विकारः; SAT SAT-C.8): disorder/ disease/ syndrome. Vikara is the condition which causes deviation from the normal physiological state of health of an individual. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: vikāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogaḥ (रोगः; SAT SAT-C.9): disease/ syndrome. Literally, the opposite of ease, when something is wrong with a bodily function. an interruption, cessation, or disorder of functions at the level of psyche, mind or body. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pāpmā (पाप्मा; SAT SAT-C.10): disease/ syndrome/ skin disease. The term literally signifies disease, originating from physical or mental si ns of the individual in present or past life. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: pāpmā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhisaṅkaraḥ (व्याधिसङ्करः; SAT SAT-C.11): co-morbidity. A disease that gives rise to another disease and still continues to exist. it can also signify a condition when two or more diseases co-exist together and may produce as a result of similarity in etiology, or pathogenic mechanism. Category: synonym of disease (vyādhiparyāyaḥ).
title: vyādhisaṅkaraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhibhedaḥ (व्याधिभेदः; SAT SAT-C.12): disease classification. The term signifies the categorization of diseases as per various criteria. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: vyādhibhedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dvividha-mānasika-rogaḥ (द्विविध-मानसिक-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.13): two types of psychological disease. The diseases which affects the psyche, can be classified as rajasika and tamasika. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: dvividha-mānasika-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rājasa-rogaḥ (राजस-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.14): diseases caused by rajas. Disorders of psyche caused by increase in rajo guna in the individual such as excessive anger, jealousy etc. Category: two types of psychological disease (dvividha-mānasika-rogaḥ).
title: rājasa-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tāmasa-rogaḥ (तामस-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.15): diseases caused by tamas. Disorders of psyche caused by increase in tamo guna in the individual such as grief, slothfulness, excessive sleepiness etc. Category: two types of psychological disease (dvividha-mānasika-rogaḥ).
title: tāmasa-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: trividha-śārīrika-rogaḥ (त्रिविध-शारीरिक-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.16): three types of somatic disease. Classification of somatic diseases on the basis of vitiation of sareerika doshas. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: trividha-śārīrika-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āgneya-rogaḥ (आग्नेय-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.17): diseases caused by pitta. This term implies diseases caused by vitiation of pitta dosha such as amlapitta, raktapitta, kamala etc. Category: three types of somatic disease (trividha-śārīrika-rogaḥ).
title: āgneya-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saumya-rogaḥ (सौम्य-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.18): diseases caused by kapha. This term implies diseases caused by vitiated kapha dosha in the body such as aruchi. Category: three types of somatic disease (trividha-śārīrika-rogaḥ).
title: saumya-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāyavya-rogaḥ (वायव्य-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.19): diseases caused by vāta. This term implies diseases produced by vitiated vata dosha in the body such as sandhivata, gridhrasi, pakshaghata etc. Category: three types of somatic disease (trividha-śārīrika-rogaḥ).
title: vāyavya-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: trividharogaḥ (त्रिविधरोगः; SAT SAT-C.20): three fold disease classification. Three fold classification of diseases by acharya susruta on the basis of etiology. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: trividharogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ādhyātmika-rogaḥ (आध्यात्मिक-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.21): psychosomatic diseases. This term signifies diseases produced as a result of affliction of psyche and body, all psychosomatic diseases are included in this categorisation. Category: three fold disease classification (trividharogaḥ).
title: ādhyātmika-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ādibalapravṛtta-rogaḥ (आदिबलप्रवृत्त-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.22): hereditary anomalies. Diseases caused due to morbidity of sperm and ovum and all hereditary diseases are classified under this. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: ādibalapravṛtta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mātṛjarogaḥ (मातृजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.23): hereditary anomalies by maternal origin. Hereditary anomalies inherited through maternal genetic defects due to morbidity in ovum. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: mātṛjarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pitṛjarogaḥ (पितृजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.24): hereditary anomalies by paternal origin. Hereditary anomalies inherited through paternal genetic defects due to morbidity in sperm. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: pitṛjarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: janmabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ (जन्मबलप्रवृत्त-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.25): congenital anomalies. Diseases that occur at the time of birth due to improper dietetics and life style practices followed by mother during conception and various stages of foetal development. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: janmabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasakṛtarogaḥ (रसकृतरोगः; SAT SAT-C.26): diseases due to dietary indiscretions. Congenital disorders that occur in infant due to dietary indiscretions of the mother practiced during conception and pregnancy. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: rasakṛtarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dauhṛdāpacārakṛta-rogaḥ (दौहृदापचारकृत-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.27): diseases due to non-fulfilment of special cravings of the mother. The congenital or other diseases that occur in the infant due to non-fulfillment of mothers cravings during pregnancy. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: dauhṛdāpacārakṛta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣabalapravṛttarogaḥ (दोषबलप्रवृत्तरोगः; SAT SAT-C.28): diseases caused by vitiated doṣha. Diseases that manifest in the body due to vitiation of body humors such as jwara, raktapitta etc. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: doṣabalapravṛttarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āmāśayasamuttha-rogaḥ (आमाशयसमुत्थ-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.29): diseases of gastric origin. Diseases which have their origin in the gastro-duodenal tract such as amlapitta(hyperacidity), chardi(vomiting ). Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: āmāśayasamuttha-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pakvāśayasamuttha-rogaḥ (पक्वाशयसमुत्थ-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.30): diseases of intestinal origin. Diseases which have their origin in the large intestinal tract such as arsas(piles), udavartha(constipation) etc. Category: psychosomatic diseases (ādhyātmika-rogaḥ).
title: pakvāśayasamuttha-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ādhibhautikarogaḥ (आधिभौतिकरोगः; SAT SAT-C.31): traumatic (exogenous) diseases. Diseases caused in the body due to exogenous or traumatic causes such as injury from accidents, fall or from animal bite or poisons. Category: three fold disease classification (trividharogaḥ).
title: ādhibhautikarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁghātabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ (संघातबलप्रवृत्त-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.32): traumatic diseases. Diseases caused by trauma such as accidents, falls etc. Category: traumatic (exogenous) diseases (ādhibhautikarogaḥ).
title: saṁghātabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śastrakṛtarogaḥ (शस्त्रकृतरोगः; SAT SAT-C.33): diseases caused by sharp instruments. Diseases caused by weapons or instruments such as swords, surgical instruments, stones, wood etc. Category: traumatic (exogenous) diseases (ādhibhautikarogaḥ).
title: śastrakṛtarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyālakṛtarogaḥ (व्यालकृतरोगः; SAT SAT-C.34): diseases caused by wild animals. The diseases which are produced due to attack and bite of tame and wild animals and include attacks by animals and injuries caused by their nails, horns and bites, snake poison, bee sting etc. Category: traumatic (exogenous) diseases (ādhibhautikarogaḥ).
title: vyālakṛtarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ādhidaivikarogaḥ (आधिदैविकरोगः; SAT SAT-C.35): natural diseases. Diseases that arise out of disturbances in nature such as natural calamities, seasonal or climatic variations or due to tempestuous divine interventions such as floods, epidemics, draught etc. Category: three fold disease classification (trividharogaḥ).
title: ādhidaivikarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ (कालबलप्रवृत्त-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.36): seasonal diseases. Diseases that are manifested in the body due to abnormal variations in the climate such as due to excessive rain, excessive heat, excessive cold and include conditions such as heatstroke, frost bite etc. Category: natural diseases (ādhidaivikarogaḥ).
title: kālabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāpannartukṛtarogaḥ (व्यापन्नर्तुकृतरोगः; SAT SAT-C.37): diseases caused by abnormality of the season. Diseases that manifest in the body due to unexpected variation in the character of seasons such as excessive rain during rainy season, excessive snowfall during winter etc. Category: natural diseases (ādhidaivikarogaḥ).
title: vyāpannartukṛtarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avyāpannartukṛta-rogaḥ (अव्यापन्नर्तुकृत-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.38): diseases which are not caused by abnormality of the season. The diseases that are caused due to vitiation of body humors that are consistent with that of a normal season and manifests mainly because of non-adaptation of suitable dietetics and regimen prescribed for that season. Category: natural diseases (ādhidaivikarogaḥ).
title: avyāpannartukṛta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: daivabalapravṛttarogaḥ (दैवबलप्रवृत्तरोगः; SAT SAT-C.39): diseases caused by supernatural agencies. Diseases that are believed to be caused by divine or supernatural causes without any other apparent cause and includes diseases caused by destruction by natural calamities such as floods, cyclones etc. Category: natural diseases (ādhidaivikarogaḥ).
title: daivabalapravṛttarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vidyudaśanikṛta-rogaḥ (विद्युदशनिकृत-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.40): diseases caused by lightning and thunder. Diseases caused by natural disasters such as thunder, lightning, asteroids and fall of comets on earth surface. Category: natural diseases (ādhidaivikarogaḥ).
title: vidyudaśanikṛta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: piśācādikṛta-rogaḥ (पिशाचादिकृत-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.41): diseases caused by evil spirits. Diseases caused by ominous evil forces such as spirits etc are included in this. Category: natural diseases (ādhidaivikarogaḥ).
title: piśācādikṛta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁsargajarogaḥ (संसर्गजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.42): infectious diseases. Diseases that are caused and transmitted in individuals by close contact or by being in proximity with individuals affected with some diseases such as kushta( leprosy), netrabhisyanda( conjunctivitis) etc. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: saṁsargajarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ākasmikarogaḥ (आकस्मिकरोगः; SAT SAT-C.43): idiopathic diseases. The diseases which manifest suddenly in the body without any apparent cause. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: ākasmikarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svabhāvabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ (स्वभावबलप्रवृत्त-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.44): natural diseases (physiological diseases). A variety of diseases, brought about by natural progression of bodily processes such as hunger, thirst, sleep, old age etc. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: svabhāvabalapravṛtta-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālajarogaḥ (कालजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.45): timely occurring natural diseases. The diseases that manifest in the body naturally due to the effect of time and physiological progression such as ageing, wrinkling, greying of hair etc. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: kālajarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: akālajarogaḥ (अकालजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.46): untimely occurring natural diseases. The conditions that manifest prior to their natural time of occurrence in the body due to improper dietetics, erratic lifestyles etc such as premature greying and wrinkling etc. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: akālajarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhi-sādhyāsādhyatvam (व्याधि-साध्यासाध्यत्वम्; SAT SAT-C.47): disease classification according to prognosis. The classification of diseases based on their prognosis such as good prognosis(sadhya), incurable(asadhya), curable with difficulty( krichrasadhya) and palliative (yapya). Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: vyādhi-sādhyāsādhyatvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sādhyarogaḥ (साध्यरोगः; SAT SAT-C.48): curable diseases. Diseases having good prognosis such as chardi (vomiting), mandagni ( depleted digestive fire). Category: disease classification according to prognosis (vyādhi-sādhyāsādhyatvam).
title: sādhyarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sukhasādhya-rogaḥ (सुखसाध्य-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.49): easily curable diseases. Easily curable diseases, having less causative factors, less amount of vitiation of doṣa and manifested in comparatively less deteriorated body tissues. Category: curable diseases (sādhyarogaḥ).
title: sukhasādhya-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṛcchrasādhya-rogaḥ (कृच्छ्रसाध्य-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.50): disease curable with difficulty. The diseases that are curable with difficulty owing to various factors such as multiplicity of etiological factors, depleted strength of individual, diseases involving multiple tissue; including diseases such as piles caused by involvement of two body humors. Category: curable diseases (sādhyarogaḥ).
title: kṛcchrasādhya-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asādhyarogaḥ (असाध्यरोगः; SAT SAT-C.51): incurable disease. The diseases which are incurable owing to involvement of all body humors, multiple tissues and tracts and presenting with arishta lakshana(signs that are markers of impending death) and includes diseases such as urdhwaswasa(severe respiratory disease), hemorrhagic diathesis due to all humors etc. Category: disease classification according to prognosis (vyādhi-sādhyāsādhyatvam).
title: asādhyarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yāpyarogaḥ (याप्यरोगः; SAT SAT-C.52): incurable but manageable disease. The diseases which by nature are not completely curable , but only palliable with suitable medicines and dietetics such as prameha(obstinate urinary disease), tamaka swasa(bronchial asthma ) etc. Category: incurable disease (asādhyarogaḥ).
title: yāpyarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratyākhyeya-rogaḥ (प्रत्याख्येय-रोगः; SAT SAT-C.53): absolutely incurable disease. The diseases which could not be managed at all even with excellence of medicine, physicians, health etc. Category: incurable disease (asādhyarogaḥ).
title: pratyākhyeya-rogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmānyajavikāraḥ (सामान्यजविकारः; SAT SAT-C.54): common diseases. Diseases caused due more than one vitiated dosha. Category: disease classification (vyādhibhedaḥ).
title: sāmānyajavikāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogaviniścayaḥ (रोगविनिश्चयः/ व्याधिविनिश्चयः; SAT SAT-C.55): definitive diagnosis. Also called vyādhiviniścayaḥ. Definite diagnosis of a disease. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: rogaviniścayaḥ vyādhiviniścayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogaparīkṣā (रोगपरीक्षा; SAT SAT-C.56): examination of diseases. Examination / investigation of the disease; it is carried out with the help of païcalakshananidana. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: rogaparīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nidānapañcakaḥ (निदानपञ्चकः; SAT SAT-C.57): five diagnostic principles. The fivefold factors that help in understanding and diagnosis of a disease, including etiology(nidana), purvarupa(prodromal symptoms), rupa(signs and symptoms of the disease), samprapthi(pathogenesis) and upasaya(understanding of aggravating and relieving factors). Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: nidānapañcakaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhijanaka-nidānam (व्याधिजनक-निदानम्; SAT SAT-C.58): aetiology. The factors that directly or indirectly act as aetiology of a disease. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: vyādhijanaka-nidānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nidānaparyāyaḥ (निदानपर्यायः; SAT SAT-C.59): synonym of aetiology. Category: aetiology (vyādhijanaka-nidānam).
title: nidānaparyāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetuḥ (हेतुः; SAT SAT-C.60): causative factors. The term literally means causative factors of the disease. ayurveda gives immense importance to understanding the cause of the disease and mentions evading the cause as prime and important measure in preventing or curing a disease. they are classified into different categories. Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: hetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nimittam (निमित्तम्; SAT SAT-C.61): causative factors. Synonym of nidana which literally means sakuna(omen or prognostic). Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: nimittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āyatanam (आयतनम्; SAT SAT-C.62): causative factors. Synonym of nidana which means cause of disease.ayatana also means the site which provide shelter. Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: āyatanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kartāḥ (कर्ताः; SAT SAT-C.63): causative factors. Synonym of nidana which literally means the perpetrator; that which act as cause of disease. Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: kartāḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāraṇam (कारणम्; SAT SAT-C.64): causative factors. The word implies primal cause. Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: kāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratyayam (प्रत्ययम्; SAT SAT-C.65): causative factors. Synonym of nidana meaning cause; used in terms of faith also. Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: pratyayam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samutthānam (समुत्थानम्; SAT SAT-C.66): causative factors. Literal meaning of the word implies origin/progress of a disease which would point to its aetiology. Category: synonym of aetiology (nidānaparyāyaḥ).
title: samutthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dvividhahetuḥ (द्विविधहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.67): two types of aetiological factors. The two fold type of aetiological factors that is based on the nature of etiology as those which directly cause disease and those which act as additional cause in manifestation of disease. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: dvividhahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: utpādakahetuḥ (उत्पादकहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.68): originating causes of disease. Etiological factors that act as direct cause for the initiation of a disease by favouring accumulation of respective doshas. Category: two types of aetiological factors (dvividhahetuḥ).
title: utpādakahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyañjakahetuḥ (व्यञ्जकहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.69): agrevating causes of disease. Etiological cause that sustains the aggravation and stimulates progression of a disease. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: vyañjakahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bāhyahetuḥ (बाह्यहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.70): extrinsic cause. External causes that include vitiation of dosha through alterations in food, behavioral aspects and time. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: bāhyahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ābhyantarahetuḥ (आभ्यन्तरहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.71): intrinsic cause. Internal factors like doṣa, dushya that exist inside the body which act as the ultimate cause in disease manifestation, when deviated from normal stage of equilibrium. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: ābhyantarahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śārīrikahetuḥ (शारीरिकहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.72): somatic cause. Causes leading to disturbances in the anatomy and physiology of the body. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: śārīrikahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mānasikahetuḥ (मानसिकहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.73): psychological cause. Causes leading to disturbances in the functions of mind. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: mānasikahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: trividhahetuḥ (त्रिविधहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.74): three types of aetiological factors. Classification of etiology into three types including asatmyendriyartha samyoga (improper use of sense organs), prajnaparadha(intellectual blasphemy) and parinama (transformation attributed to time). Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: trividhahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: asātmyendriyārtha- saṁyogaḥ (असात्म्येन्द्रियार्थ- संयोगः; SAT SAT-C.75): improper use of sensory organs. Misuse of the senses in wrongful manner, in excess or in less than normal way; included as one of the three prime causes of a disease. Category: three types of aetiological factors (trividhahetuḥ).
title: asātmyendriyārtha- saṁyogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prajñāparādhaḥ (प्रज्ञापराधः; SAT SAT-C.76): intellectual blasphemy; knowingly opting the wrong things may be dietetic or behavioural. Included as one of the three prime causes of a disease; the misuse of a person’s intellect in identifying the wholesome / beneficial thing, any act done bereft of intelligence, perseverance and mindfulness. such an act aggravates all the three doṣa thus should be avoided by a wise person. Category: three types of aetiological factors (trividhahetuḥ).
title: prajñāparādhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pariṇāmaḥ (परिणामः; SAT SAT-C.77): seasonal variation as a cause of disease. The negative impact of the season; included as one of the three prime causes of a disease. Category: three types of aetiological factors (trividhahetuḥ).
title: pariṇāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣahetuḥ (दोषहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.78): vitiated doṣha as a cause of disease. The seasonal variations causing natural accumulation and aggravation of the doṣa. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: doṣahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prākṛtadoṣaḥ (प्राकृतदोषः; SAT SAT-C.79): normal physiological state of doṣha. The normal physiological state of dosa which brings about state of equilibrium and health in body. Category: vitiated doṣha as a cause of disease (doṣahetuḥ).
title: prākṛtadoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vaikṛtadoṣaḥ (वैकृतदोषः; SAT SAT-C.80): deviation of doṣha from its normal state. The deviation of dosa from normal physiological state of equilibrium with derangement of functional, qualitative or quantitative aspects of dosa which is the basis for disease. Category: vitiated doṣha as a cause of disease (doṣahetuḥ).
title: vaikṛtadoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anubandhyaḥ (अनुबन्ध्यः; SAT SAT-C.81): primary or independent. Independent disease having its own set of symptoms and classical line of therapy. Category: vitiated doṣha as a cause of disease (doṣahetuḥ).
title: anubandhyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anubandhaḥ (अनुबन्धः; SAT SAT-C.82): secondary or dependent. Any disease which does not have an independent existence or line of treatment. Category: vitiated doṣha as a cause of disease (doṣahetuḥ).
title: anubandhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakṛti (प्रकृति; SAT SAT-C.83): normalcy. State of normalcy in any aspect without any deviation or derangement from normal state, function or quality. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: prakṛti

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vikṛtaḥ (विकृतः/विकृति; SAT SAT-C.84): abnormal. Also called vikṛti. Not normal; differing in any way from the usual state, structure or condition. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: vikṛtaḥ vikṛti

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āśayāpakarṣaḥ (आशयापकर्षः; SAT SAT-C.85): phenomenon of propulsion of normal dosha to another site to produce its symptoms. Specific term which represents a pathological phenomenon when vitiated vata dosa forcefully shifts another dosha from its normal site to another and produces symptoms. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: āśayāpakarṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣagatiḥ (दोषगतिः; SAT SAT-C.86): the physiological and pathological movement of doṣa within the body. The movement of doshas within the body(apart from physiological movement) is a pathogenic mechanism which results in manifestation of disease in different tracts. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: doṣagatiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sañcārasthānam (सञ्चारस्थानम्; SAT SAT-C.87): way of the movement of doṣa. The term signifies spread of the vitiated dosha. Category: the physiological and pathological movement of doṣa within the body (doṣagatiḥ).
title: sañcārasthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śākhāgatiḥ (शाखागतिः; SAT SAT-C.88): movements of doṣa from viscera to tissues. Movements of doṣa towards tissues (shakha), either physiological or pathological; manifestation of diseases occur when the vitiated dosas gets dislodged in sakha. Category: the physiological and pathological movement of doṣa within the body (doṣagatiḥ).
title: śākhāgatiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: madhyamagatiḥ (मध्यमगतिः; SAT SAT-C.89): movements of doṣa towards vital parts, head and junctures and junctions of the body. Category: the physiological and pathological movement of doṣa within the body (doṣagatiḥ).
title: madhyamagatiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmadoṣaḥ (सामदोषः; SAT SAT-C.90): doṣa associated with āma. Dosa when associated with ama undergoes qualitative and functional alteration and become capable of producing diseases. Āma: The term is used as a technical word for anything that exists in a state of incomplete transformation. It is mentioned in various contexts like a) In particular, it can refer to a toxic by product generated due to improper or incomplete digestion. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ). Classical references: W.H.O Ayu Terminology Draft 2010[1.154.0].
title: sāmadoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirāmadoṣaḥ (निरामदोषः; SAT SAT-C.91): doṣa not associated with āma. When ama associated with any dosha undergoes depletion, the resultant dosha is termed as nirama, which is still in vitiated state and has not returned to normalcy. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: nirāmadoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣahetuḥ (दोषहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.92): causes which aggravate doṣa. Causes which aggravate doṣa irrespective of the disease. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: doṣahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhihetuḥ (व्याधिहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.93): disease specific causes. Factors that cause a disease irrespective of the doṣa involved in it. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: vyādhihetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ubhayahetuḥ (उभयहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.94): causes which aggravate doṣa as well as disease specific causes. Factors which not only aggravate particular dosha but also cause for a particular disease; causes affecting both mind and body. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: ubhayahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: caturvidhahetuḥ (चतुर्विधहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.95): four types of aetiological factors. The classification of hetu as four types based on its capability in producing disease. Category: five diagnostic principles (nidānapañcakaḥ).
title: caturvidhahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sannikṛṣṭahetuḥ (सन्निकृष्टहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.96): direct cause. The potent cause which can directly cause a disease i.e. ruksha diet is the sannikrishta nidan for vatika type of jwara. Category: four types of aetiological factors (caturvidhahetuḥ).
title: sannikṛṣṭahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viprakṛṣṭahetuḥ (विप्रकृष्टहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.97): indirect cause. Distant causative factors which are comparatively less influential in causing a disease i.e. rudra kopa (wrath of god rudra) is said as viprakrushta hetu for jwara. Category: four types of aetiological factors (caturvidhahetuḥ).
title: viprakṛṣṭahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyabhicārīhetuḥ (व्यभिचारीहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.98): weak cause of the disease. Non – dominant causative factor; thus cannot independently cause a disease and may produce when suitable situation arises in body. Category: four types of aetiological factors (caturvidhahetuḥ).
title: vyabhicārīhetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prādhānikahetuḥ (प्राधानिकहेतुः; SAT SAT-C.99): more powerful and prime cause. Dominant causative factors which play dominant role in causing a disease; such factors produce instantaneous dosha dushti and are very potent in causation of disease e.g. poison. Category: four types of aetiological factors (caturvidhahetuḥ).
title: prādhānikahetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pūrvarūpam (पूर्वरूपम्; SAT SAT-C.100): prodromes. It is the premonitory symptom by learning about which one can avoid the manifestation of the disease; depending on their nature they are classified into two types. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: pūrvarūpam
