source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pūrvarūpa-bhedaḥ (पूर्वरूप-भेदः; SAT SAT-C.101): classification of prodromes. Classification of prodromal symptoms on the basis of their general and specific nature, which points to any disease or any particular disease. Category: prodromes (pūrvarūpam).
title: pūrvarūpa-bhedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viśeṣapūrvarūpam (विशेषपूर्वरूपम्; SAT SAT-C.102): disease specific prodromes. They signify two meanings a) specific symptom pertaining to particular dosha. b) those premonitory symptoms which convert into signs and symptoms of a particular condition. Category: classification of prodromes (pūrvarūpa-bhedaḥ).
title: viśeṣapūrvarūpam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmānyapūrvarūpam (सामान्यपूर्वरूपम्; SAT SAT-C.103): general prodromes. They signify two meanings a) general premonitory symptoms b) those premonitory symptoms which does not convert into signs and symptoms. Category: classification of prodromes (pūrvarūpa-bhedaḥ).
title: sāmānyapūrvarūpam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: liṅagaḥ (लिङगः; SAT SAT-C.104): symptoms. Any morbid phenomenon or departure from the normal in structure, function, or sensation, experienced by either the patient or physician and indicative of disease syn: li~gaga. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: liṅagaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: liṅaga-paryāyaḥ (लिङग-पर्यायः; SAT SAT-C.105): synonyms of symptoms. Various synonyms of linga such as lakshana, chihna, akrti etc. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: liṅaga-paryāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ākṛtiḥ (आकृतिः; SAT SAT-C.106): form. Synonyms of liṅga; denotes the symptoms that is manifested in a disease. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: ākṛtiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lakṣaṇam (लक्षणम्; SAT SAT-C.107): symptoms/ characteristics. Synonyms of liṅga; any morbid phenomenon or departure from the normal in structure, function, or sensation, understood by physician which is indicative of disease. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: lakṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cihnam (चिह्नम्; SAT SAT-C.108): sign. Synonyms of liṅga; signs which points toward any disease such as krichraswasanam (difficulty breathing) pointing towards swasa roga ( respiratory disease). Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: cihnam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁsthānam (संस्थानम्; SAT SAT-C.109): place of manifestation/ shape. Synonyms of liṅga; literal meaning denotes the type of manifestation in the body. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: saṁsthānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyañjanam (व्यञ्जनम्; SAT SAT-C.110): symptom. Synonyms of liṅga; this term denotes the manifestations of disease. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: vyañjanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rūpam (रूपम्; SAT SAT-C.111): sign. Synonyms of liṅga; any morbid phenomenon or departure from the normal in structure, function, or sensation, understood by physician which is indicative of disease. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: rūpam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hṛtadoṣa-lakṣaṇam (हृतदोष-लक्षणम्; SAT SAT-C.112): symptoms seen in the body after the complete expulsion of the impaired doṣa. The symptoms and signs that points to a normal state after the expulsion of vitiated doshas. Category: symptoms (liṅagaḥ).
title: hṛtadoṣa-lakṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upaśayaḥ (उपशयः; SAT SAT-C.113): favourable treatment and intervantion. The signs and symptoms of improvement signifying relief / alleviation of the disease. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: upaśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upaśaya-bhedaḥ (उपशय-भेदः; SAT SAT-C.114): types of assuagement. Classification of assuagement on the basis of their nature. Category: favourable treatment and intervantion (upaśayaḥ).
title: upaśaya-bhedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetuviparītaḥ (हेतुविपरीतः; SAT SAT-C.115): drug ,food, behaviour aspects that are antagonistic to causative factors of disease. Judicious use of medicines, regimen and dietetics that is antagonistic to the etiology of disease. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: hetuviparītaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhiviparītaḥ (व्याधिविपरीतः; SAT SAT-C.116): drug ,food, behaviour aspects that are antagonistic to disease. Judicious use of medicines, regimen and dietetics that is antagonistic to the nature of disease itself. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: vyādhiviparītaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetu-vyādhi- viparītaḥ (हेतु-व्याधि- विपरीतः; SAT SAT-C.117): drug ,food, behaviour aspects that are antagonistic to both causative factors of disease and disease itself. Judicious use of medicines, regimen and dietetics that are antagonistic to both the etiology and disease itself. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: hetu-vyādhi- viparītaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viparītārthakāriḥ (विपरीतार्थकारिः; SAT SAT-C.118): drug ,food, behaviour aspects that are similar. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: viparītārthakāriḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetuviparītārthakāriḥ (हेतुविपरीतार्थकारिः; SAT SAT-C.119): drug , food, behaviour aspects are similar to causative factors of disease. Judicious use of medicines, regimen and dietetics that is similar to the etiology, but capable of producing assuagement. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: hetuviparītārthakāriḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhi- viparītārthakāriḥ (व्याधि- विपरीतार्थकारिः; SAT SAT-C.120): drug ,food, behaviour aspects that are similar to disease. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: vyādhi- viparītārthakāriḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetu-vyādhi viparītārthakāriḥ (हेतु-व्याधि विपरीतार्थकारिः; SAT SAT-C.121): drug ,food, behaviour aspects that are similar to both causative factors of disease and disease itself. Judicious use of medicines, regimen and dietetics that is similar to both the etiology and disease, but capable of producing assuagement. Category: types of assuagement (upaśaya-bhedaḥ).
title: hetu-vyādhi viparītārthakāriḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anupaśayaḥ (अनुपशयः; SAT SAT-C.122): unfavourable treatment and intervantion. Intervention of the diet and medicine which is neither good for health nor for diseases. and it is one of the tools of the diagnosis where the diseases cannot be diagnosed by referring merely its clinical features. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: anupaśayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samprāptiḥ (सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.123): pathogenesis. The term signifies the mechanism starting from vitiation of doṣa till the origin and complete manifestation / development of the disease. further pathogenesis is classified into six types. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samprāptiparyāyaḥ (सम्प्राप्तिपर्यायः; SAT SAT-C.124): synonyms of pathogenesis. Category: pathogenesis (samprāptiḥ).
title: samprāptiparyāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jātiḥ (जातिः; SAT SAT-C.125): synonym of pathogenesis. Denotes the synonym of pathogenesis.
title: jātiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āgatiḥ (आगतिः; SAT SAT-C.126): synonym of pathogenesis. Denotes the synonym of pathogenesis. Category: synonym of pathogenesis (jātiḥ).
title: āgatiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samprāptibhedaḥ (सम्प्राप्तिभेदः; SAT SAT-C.127): classification of pathogenesis. Category: pathogenesis (samprāptiḥ).
title: samprāptibhedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṅkhyā-samprāptiḥ (सङ्ख्या-सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.128): stage wise pathogenesis. Classification of the pathogenesis according to enumeration. Category: classification of pathogenesis (samprāptibhedaḥ).
title: saṅkhyā-samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prādhānya-samprāptiḥ (प्राधान्य-सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.129): main pathogenesis. Classification of the pathogenesis according to primary or secondary ailment. Category: classification of pathogenesis (samprāptibhedaḥ).
title: prādhānya-samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vidhi-samprāptiḥ (विधि-सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.130): variety specific pathogenesis. Classification of the pathogenesis according to the categorization based on various aspects such as based on prognosis a disease can be classified as saadhya (easily curable), aasadhya( incurable), krichsaadhya(difficult to cure) etc. Category: classification of pathogenesis (samprāptibhedaḥ).
title: vidhi-samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vikalpa-samprāptiḥ (विकल्प-सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.131): variation specific pathogenesis. Classification of the pathogenesis according to the predominance of one or other fraction of the three doshas. Category: classification of pathogenesis (samprāptibhedaḥ).
title: vikalpa-samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bala-samprāptiḥ (बल-सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.132): intensity specific pathogenesis. Classification of the pathogenesis according to strength of the disease. Category: classification of pathogenesis (samprāptibhedaḥ).
title: bala-samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāla-samprāptiḥ (काल-सम्प्राप्तिः; SAT SAT-C.133): time specific pathogenesis. Classification of the pathogenesis according to time of occurrence or aggravation of the disease. Category: classification of pathogenesis (samprāptibhedaḥ).
title: kāla-samprāptiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upadravaḥ (उपद्रवः; SAT SAT-C.134): complications. The diseases that develop subsequent to a disease or during the course of the main disease that is being treated, and is dependent upon the main disease for its origination, nature and the strength. it is called secondary in the sense that its onset follows the presence of the primary disease. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: upadravaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāpad (व्यापद्; SAT SAT-C.135): complication. Complications caused during therapeutic procedures like panchakrma (eg. basti vyapada). Category: complications (upadravaḥ).
title: vyāpad

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āturanimittajaḥ (आतुरनिमित्तजः; SAT SAT-C.136): complications due to patient. Complications that arise during treatment due to non- obedience from the side of the patient. Category: complications (upadravaḥ).
title: āturanimittajaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhiṣak-nimittajaḥ (भिषक्-निमित्तजः; SAT SAT-C.137): iatrogenic complications. Complications that arise by the false application of medical or surgical procedures. Category: complications (upadravaḥ).
title: bhiṣak-nimittajaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bheṣaja-nimittajaḥ (भेषज-निमित्तजः; SAT SAT-C.138): complications due to drug. Complications which arise as a result of improper usage of drugs, usage of poor standard drugs etc. Category: complications (upadravaḥ).
title: bheṣaja-nimittajaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ariṣṭalakṣaṇam (अरिष्टलक्षणम्; SAT SAT-C.139): fatal signs of disease. Fatal sign and symptoms which arises in patients denoting poor prognosis or death. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: ariṣṭalakṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogāvasthā (रोगावस्था; SAT SAT-C.140): stage of disease. The term signifies different stages of diseases. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: rogāvasthā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pakvāvasthā (पक्वावस्था; SAT SAT-C.141): ripened stage of doṣa in a disease. The transforming phase of a disease-course or vrana denoting post- inflammatory condition /suppurative condition of a disease or vrana. Category: stage of disease (rogāvasthā).
title: pakvāvasthā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pacyamānāvasthā (पच्यमानावस्था; SAT SAT-C.142): transforming stage of desease. The transforming phase of a disease-course or vrana denoting the inflammatory condition. Category: stage of disease (rogāvasthā).
title: pacyamānāvasthā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirāmāvasthā (निरामावस्था; SAT SAT-C.143): devoid of āma. State when the ama state is converted by either the effect of time or therapeutic measures. Category: stage of disease (rogāvasthā).
title: nirāmāvasthā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kriyākālaḥ (क्रियाकालः; SAT SAT-C.144): stages of disease manifestation and its management. Six chief stages in the management of diseases/ step wise description of a disease’s pathogenesis. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: kriyākālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sañcayaḥ (सञ्चयः; SAT SAT-C.145): accumulative stage. It is the first stage of kriyakala. the stage of accumulation of doshas in their own place (swasthana). Category: stages of disease manifestation and its management (kriyākālaḥ).
title: sañcayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakopaḥ (प्रकोपः; SAT SAT-C.146): provocative stage. It is the second stage of kriyakala. the stage of provocation or aggravation of the doshas. Category: stages of disease manifestation and its management (kriyākālaḥ).
title: prakopaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prasaraḥ (प्रसरः; SAT SAT-C.147): migration stage. It is the third stage of kriyakala. prasara means leave & spread and thus it is the stage of migration of vitiated doshas from their usual places to different places. Category: stages of disease manifestation and its management (kriyākālaḥ).
title: prasaraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthānasaṁśrayaḥ (स्थानसंश्रयः; SAT SAT-C.148): stage of localization. It is the fourth stage of kriyakala. the term literally means taking shelter in a place. it is the stage of disease augmentation wherein the vitiated doshas lodges into other body parts consisting of khavaigunya(vacant space) and causes functional, structural or both deformities. Category: stages of disease manifestation and its management (kriyākālaḥ).
title: sthānasaṁśrayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyaktiḥ (व्यक्तिः; SAT SAT-C.149): manifestation stage. It is the fifth stage of kriyakala. the stage of symptom manifestation of the disease. Category: stages of disease manifestation and its management (kriyākālaḥ).
title: vyaktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhedaḥ (भेदः; SAT SAT-C.150): stage of complication. It is the sixth stage of kriyakala, the stage of complications and here the symptoms can be differentiated on the basis of doshas. Category: stages of disease manifestation and its management (kriyākālaḥ).
title: bhedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogīparīkṣā (रोगीपरीक्षा; SAT SAT-C.151): examination of patient. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: rogīparīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: trividhaparīkṣā (त्रिविधपरीक्षा; SAT SAT-C.152): three folds examination of patient. Examination of patient done by darshan(observation), sparshan(palpation) and prashna (interrogation). Category: examination of patient (rogīparīkṣā).
title: trividhaparīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣaḍvidha-parīkṣā (षड्विध-परीक्षा; SAT SAT-C.153): six folds examination of patient. Examination of patient done by five senses and interrogation. Category: examination of patient (rogīparīkṣā).
title: ṣaḍvidha-parīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṣṭasthāna-parīkṣā (अष्टस्थान-परीक्षा; SAT SAT-C.154): eight folds examination of patient. Eight folds examination of patient as : 1. examination of pulse (nadi)2. examination of urine (mootra) 3. examination of the excreta (mala) 4 . examination of tongue (jihwa) 5. examination of voice, sounds produced from body like percussion etc. (shabda) 6. tactile examination (sparsha) 7. examination of eyes and eyesight (driga) 8. examination of the body stature (akruti). Category: examination of patient (rogīparīkṣā).
title: aṣṭasthāna-parīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: daśavidha-parīkṣā (दशविध-परीक्षा; SAT SAT-C.155): ten fold examination of patient. Ten folds of examination considering below mentioned criteria: 1. physical constitution (prakruti) 2. morbidity (vikruti) 3. excellence of dushya or tissue elements (sara). 4. compactness or tissues or organs (samhanana) 5. measurement of body constituents (pramana) 6. homologation (saatmya). 7. psycic condition (satwa) 8. power of intake and digestion of food (aaharshakti) 9. power of performing exercise (vyayam shakti) 10. age (vayah). Category: examination of patient (rogīparīkṣā).
title: daśavidha-parīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhikṣamatvam (व्याधिक्षमत्वम्; SAT SAT-C.156): immunity. Resisting power of the body, which reacts to arrest the progress, occurrence, and reoccurrence of diseases. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: vyādhikṣamatvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhi balavirodhitatvam (व्याधि बलविरोधितत्वम्; SAT SAT-C.157): direct resistance to disease. Natural, non-specific type of immunity which defends the body in the first occurrence of any disease. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: vyādhi balavirodhitatvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhyudpādapratibandhakatvam (व्याध्युद्पादप्रतिबन्धकत्वम्; SAT SAT-C.158): resistance to manifestation of disease. Body’s defence mechanism which checks the occurrence or reoccurrence of diseases. Category: disease/ syndrome (vyādhiḥ).
title: vyādhyudpādapratibandhakatvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: srotorodhaḥ (स्रोतोरोधः; SAT SAT-C.159): obstructive pathology occurring in channels. Complete or partial obstruction in the body channels leading their malfunctioning. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: srotorodhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: srotovaiguṇyam (स्रोतोवैगुण्यम्; SAT SAT-C.160): deformity in the body channels. The term physiological or structural signifies deformity in the body channels leading to manifestation of the diseases. Category: obstructive pathology occurring in channels (srotorodhaḥ).
title: srotovaiguṇyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: srotoduṣṭi-hetuḥ (स्रोतोदुष्टि-हेतुः; SAT SAT-C.161): causes of deformity in the body channels. The term signifies the etiological factors for the deformity in the body channels. Category: obstructive pathology occurring in channels (srotorodhaḥ).
title: srotoduṣṭi-hetuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: srotoduṣṭiprakāraḥ (स्रोतोदुष्टिप्रकारः; SAT SAT-C.162): types deformity in body channels. Types of the deformity in the body channels. Category: obstructive pathology occurring in channels (srotorodhaḥ).
title: srotoduṣṭiprakāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: atipravṛttiḥ (अतिप्रवृत्तिः; SAT SAT-C.163): increase or over flow of the contents in the body channels. Category: types deformity in body channels (srotoduṣṭiprakāraḥ).
title: atipravṛttiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṅgaḥ (सङ्गः; SAT SAT-C.164): obstruction due to contraction of lumen. Obstruction in the pathway of body channels which restricts the movements and may also forms a collateral way sometimes. Category: types deformity in body channels (srotoduṣṭiprakāraḥ).
title: saṅgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vimārgagamanam (विमार्गगमनम्; SAT SAT-C.165): diversion to the flow of the contents to the improper channels. Category: types deformity in body channels (srotoduṣṭiprakāraḥ).
title: vimārgagamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sirāgranthiḥ (सिराग्रन्थिः; SAT SAT-C.166): occurrence of nodular growth in the body channels. Occurrence of nodular growth in the lumen of body channels. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: sirāgranthiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sannipātaḥ (सन्निपातः; SAT SAT-C.167): conglomeration. Literally, it signifies parts or items that are grouped together. generally the term is used to state the involvement of all the three doshas, in the pathogenesis of diseases. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: sannipātaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogānīkaḥ (रोगानीकः; SAT SAT-C.168): comorbidity. The simultaneous appearance of two or more illnesses. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: rogānīkaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogādhiṣṭhānam (रोगाधिष्ठानम्; SAT SAT-C.169): place of manifestation of diseases. The term literally means abode , place where diseases take shelter and from where manifestation of disease occurs. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: rogādhiṣṭhānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rogānutpādanīyam (रोगानुत्पादनीयम्; SAT SAT-C.170): measures for prevention of disease. Syn: anagata badhapratishedha. ref.code: 1.36.0. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: rogānutpādanīyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: līnadoṣāvasthā (लीनदोषावस्था; SAT SAT-C.171): concealed and opportunistic doṣa. The abnormal state of the vitiated doṣa where in they become concealed in the body channels and remain opportunistic to cause abnormality in the body in presence of a favourable condition. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: līnadoṣāvasthā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthānāntaragata-doṣaḥ (स्थानान्तरगत- दोषः; SAT SAT-C.172): movement of dosha from its usual place. Syn: agantu doshah ref.code: 1.137.0 dosha when moves to other place and shows disease manifestation there. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: sthānāntaragata-doṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthānika-doṣaḥ (स्थानिक-दोषः; SAT SAT-C.173): dosha residing at its usual place. The term literally means inhabitant dosha, that is dosha residing at its own place. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: sthānika-doṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakṛtisamasamaveta-sannipātajarogaḥ (प्रकृतिसमसमवेत-सन्निपातजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.174): the disease in which symptoms manifest in accordance to dosa involved. A disease caused due to sannipaata, in which dosha dominance can be understood on the basis of symptoms. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: prakṛtisamasamaveta-sannipātajarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vikṛtiviṣama-samaveta-sannipātajarogaḥ (विकृतिविषम-समवेत-सन्निपातजरोगः; SAT SAT-C.175): the disease in which symptoms other than that of dosa involved also manifested. A disease caused due to sannipaata, in which dosha dominance cannot be understood on the basis of symptoms. Category: definitive diagnosis (rogaviniścayaḥ).
title: vikṛtiviṣama-samaveta-sannipātajarogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: liṅgam (लिङ्गम्/ लक्षणम्/ चिह्नम्/ संस्थानम्/ व्यञ्जनम्/ आकृतिः; SAT SAT-D). Also called lakṣaṇam, cihnam, saṃsthānam, vyañjanam and ākṛtiḥ. Signs and symptoms.
title: liṅgam lakṣaṇam cihnam saṃsthānam vyañjanam ākṛtiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ avanunnata iva (अंसः अवनुन्नत इव; SAT SAT-D.1). Constricting feeling in shoulder.
title: aṃsaḥ avanunnata iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ avapāṭita iva (अंसः अवपाटित इव; SAT SAT-D.2). Splitting type of pain in shoulder.
title: aṃsaḥ avapāṭita iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ caṭita iva (अंसः चटित इव; SAT SAT-D.3). Feeling as if shoulder is broken.
title: aṃsaḥ caṭita iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ bhagna iva (अंसः भग्न इव; SAT SAT-D.4). Breaking type of pain in shoulder.
title: aṃsaḥ bhagna iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ mathita iva (अंसः मथित इव; SAT SAT-D.5). Feeling as if shoulder is being churned.
title: aṃsaḥ mathita iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ mṛdita iva (अंसः मृदित इव; SAT SAT-D.6). Feeling as if shoulder is being crushed.
title: aṃsaḥ mṛdita iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsaḥ rugṇa iva (अंसः रुग्ण इव; SAT SAT-D.7). Cutting type of pain in shoulder.
title: aṃsaḥ rugṇa iva

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsadāhaḥ (अंसदाहः; SAT SAT-D.8). Burning in shoulder.
title: aṃsadāhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsadeśe sphoṭasannibhaḥ eka piṭikā (अंसदेशे स्फोटसन्निभः एक पिटिका; SAT SAT-D.9). Single vesicular lesion in the shoulder region.
title: aṃsadeśe sphoṭasannibhaḥ eka piṭikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsadeśe sphoṭāḥ (अंसदेशे स्फोटाः; SAT SAT-D.10). Vesicular lesions in shoulder.
title: aṃsadeśe sphoṭāḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsapīḍanam (अंसपीडनम्; SAT SAT-D.11). Squeezing pain in shoulder.
title: aṃsapīḍanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsabandhanaśoṣaḥ (अंसबन्धनशोषः; SAT SAT-D.12). Atrophy of the structure binding the shoulder joints/ wasting of shoulder region.
title: aṃsabandhanaśoṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsayoḥ śūlam (अंसयोः शूलम्; SAT SAT-D.13). Pain in shoulders.
title: aṃsayoḥ śūlam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsayoḥ saṃkocaḥ (अंसयोः संकोचः/ अंससंलोचः; SAT SAT-D.14). Also called aṃsasaṃlocaḥ. Contraction of shoulders.
title: aṃsayoḥ saṃkocaḥ aṃsasaṃlocaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsarujā (अंसरुजा; SAT SAT-D.15). Pain in shoulder.
title: aṃsarujā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsavyathā (अंसव्यथा; SAT SAT-D.16). Pain in scapular regions.
title: aṃsavyathā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsasantāpaḥ (अंससन्तापः/ अंसाभितापः/ अंसतापः; SAT SAT-D.17). Also called aṃsābhitāpaḥ and aṃsatāpaḥ. Burning sensation in shoulders/ scapular region.
title: aṃsasantāpaḥ aṃsābhitāpaḥ aṃsatāpaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsasthitapiḍikā (अंसस्थितपिडिका; SAT SAT-D.18). Eruption located at shoulder.
title: aṃsasthitapiḍikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṃsāvamardanam (अंसावमर्दनम्/ अंसमर्दनम्; SAT SAT-D.19). Also called aṃsamardanam. Crushing type of pain in shoulders.

title: prabhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: deśyoktiḥ (देश्योक्तिः; SAT SAT-F.19): nomenclature based on habitat. Nomenclature on the basis of their place of origin. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: deśyoktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lāñchanam (लाञ्छनम्; SAT SAT-F.20): a mark or sign, one of the basis for naming plants. Naming a dravya based on a specific mark or sign or specific character. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: lāñchanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upamā (उपमा; SAT SAT-F.21): nomenclature based on resemblance. Naming a dravya based on its resemblance to other objects. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: upamā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vīrya (वीर्य; SAT SAT-F.22): nomenclature based on potency or properties. Naming a dravya based on its potency or properties. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: vīrya

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: itarāhvaya (इतराह्वय; SAT SAT-F.23): nomenclature based on names of other objects. Naming a dravya based on names of other objects. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: itarāhvaya

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: paryāyaḥ (पर्यायः; SAT SAT-F.24): synonyms. Different names for the same dravya. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: paryāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyapadeśastu bhūyasā (व्यपदेशस्तु भूयसा; SAT SAT-F.25): law of predominence. Difference between dravya on the basis of the predominant mahābhūta within it. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: vyapadeśastu bhūyasā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣapraśamanam (दोषप्रशमनम्; SAT SAT-F.26): pacification of doṣa. Substances that pacify doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: doṣapraśamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhātu-pradūṣaṇam (धातु-प्रदूषणम्; SAT SAT-F.27): vitiation of dhātu. Commonly used to denote the substances that are harmful to the dhātu. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: dhātu-pradūṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svasthavṛttahitam (स्वस्थवृत्तहितम्; SAT SAT-F.28): substances that primarily maintains and promotes health. Dravya which do not vitiate doṣa or dhātu and are fit for daily use for a healthy individual. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: svasthavṛttahitam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśamanam (संशमनम्/ शमनम्; SAT SAT-F.29): pacifying. Also called śamanam. Pacification of vitiated doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: saṁśamanam śamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kopanam (कोपनम्; SAT SAT-F.30): aggravation of doṣa. Substances aggravating or initiating the vitiation of doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: kopanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāta-kopana (वात-कोपन; SAT SAT-F.31): vata vitiating. Substances that vitiates vata doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: vāta-kopana

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāta-saṁśamana (वात-संशमन; SAT SAT-F.32): vata pacifying. Substances that pacify vitiated vata doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: vāta-saṁśamana

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pitta-kopanam (पित्त-कोपनम्; SAT SAT-F.33): pitta vitiating. Substances that vitiates pitta doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: pitta-kopanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pitta-saṁśamanam (पित्त-संशमनम्; SAT SAT-F.34): pitta pacifying. Substances that pacify vitiated pitta doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: pitta-saṁśamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kapha-kopanam (कफ-कोपनम्; SAT SAT-F.35): kapha vitiating. Substances that vitiates kapha doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: kapha-kopanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kapha-saṁśamanam (कफ-संशमनम्; SAT SAT-F.36): kapha pacifying. Substances that pacify vitiated kapha doṣa. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: kapha-saṁśamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasapañcaka (रसपञ्चक; SAT SAT-F.37): five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa. Five attributes of dravya viz., rasa, guṇa, vīrya, vipāka, prabhāva. Category: basis of nomenclature (dravyanāmakaraṅa-āḍhāraḥ).
title: rasapañcaka

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasaḥ (रसः; SAT SAT-F.38): taste. Direct and immediate action of a dravya when it comes in contact with the tongue which are six in number and determined by its pāñcabhautika composition. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: rasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: madhuraḥ (मधुरः/ मधुररसः; SAT SAT-F.39): sweet taste. Also called madhurarasaḥ. One among the six types of rasa which is most pleasing to tongue e.g. sugar. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: madhuraḥ madhurarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: amlam (अम्लम्/ अम्लरसः; SAT SAT-F.40): sour taste. Also called amlarasaḥ. One among the six types of rasa which is acidic or sour in nature e.g. lemon. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: amlam amlarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lavaṇam (लवणम्/ लवण-रसः; SAT SAT-F.41): salty taste. Also called lavaṇarasaḥ. One among the six types of rasa which is saline in nature e.g. common salt. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: lavaṇam lavaṇarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṭuḥ (कटुः/कटुरसः; SAT SAT-F.42): pungent taste. Also called kaṭurasaḥ. One among the six types of rasa which is pungent in nature e.g. pepper. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: kaṭuḥ kaṭurasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tiktam (तिक्तम्/तिक्तरसः; SAT SAT-F.43): bitter taste. Also called tiktarasaḥ. One among the six types of rasa which is bitter in nature e.g. bittergourd. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: tiktam tiktarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṣāyaḥ (कषायः/ कषायरसः; SAT SAT-F.44): astringent taste. Also called kaṣāyarasaḥ. One among the six types of rasa which is astringent in nature e.g. black plum. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: kaṣāyaḥ kaṣāyarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anurasaḥ (अनुरसः; SAT SAT-F.45): unmanifestated/ latent taste. Latent taste of a dravya which is either not perceived or is perceived towards the end of its contact with the tongue. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: anurasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anirdeśyarasaḥ (अनिर्देश्यरसः; SAT SAT-F.46): unidentifiable taste. Rasa which even though present in the dravya is not perceived by the tongue. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: anirdeśyarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guṇaḥ (गुणः; SAT SAT-F.47): property/ quality/ attribute. Guṇa refers to the properties of drugs and dietary articles which are responsible for their respective action in the body and is defined as the characteristic by which people are attracted towards a particular substance. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: guṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vīryam (वीर्यम्; SAT SAT-F.48): potency. Potency of a drug in terms of dominant guṇa classified into two viz.uṣṇa(hot) and śīta (cold) or eight viz. guru, snigdha, śīta, mṛdu, laghu, rūkṣa, uṣṇa and tīkṣṇa by which the drug brings out the therapeutic effect or action. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: vīryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saumyaḥ (सौम्यः; SAT SAT-F.49): gentle/mild. Quality of a substance characterized by its gentleness. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: saumyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āgneyaḥ (आग्नेयः; SAT SAT-F.50): fiery. Opposite of saumya. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: āgneyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aśītoṣṇam (अशीतोष्णम्; SAT SAT-F.51): neither hot nor cold. State of temperature which is neither hot nor cold. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: aśītoṣṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tīkṣṇa-vīryam (तीक्ष्ण-वीर्यम्; SAT SAT-F.52): high potency. Having strong or higher grade of potency. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: tīkṣṇa-vīryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: madhya-vīryam (मध्य-वीर्यम्; SAT SAT-F.53): moderate potency. Substances which have a moderate degree of potency. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: madhya-vīryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mṛduvīryam (मृदुवीर्यम्; SAT SAT-F.54): mild potency. Which produce only mild action. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: mṛduvīryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirvīryam (निर्वीर्यम्; SAT SAT-F.55): having no potency. Substances not having any potency. Category: potency (vīryam).
title: nirvīryam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vipākaḥ (विपाकः; SAT SAT-F.56): bio-transformed rasa. Vipāka is the rasa of the drug after it has undergone digestive and assimilative transformations which is classified into three viz. kaṭu (pungent) amla (sour) madhura(sweet). Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: vipākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prabhāvaḥ (प्रभावः; SAT SAT-F.57): exceptional activity. An exceptional or unique therapeutic effect of a dravya by which drugs having similar rasa, guṇa, vīrya and vipāka have different therapeutic actions. Category: bio-transformed rasa (vipākaḥ).
title: prabhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: acintyavīrya (अचिन्त्यवीर्य; SAT SAT-F.58): inconceivable potency. Synonym of prabhāva. Category: bio-transformed rasa (vipākaḥ).
title: acintyavīrya

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karma (कर्म; SAT SAT-F.59): action. Action of dravya which is determined in order of significance by the prabhāva, vīrya, vipāka and rasa of that dravya. Category: five attributes of dravya beginning with rasa (rasapañcaka).
title: karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dīpanam (दीपनम्; SAT SAT-F.60): digestion and metabolism enhancing. Therapeutic action which kindles the agni but cannot digest the āma. Category: action (karma).
title: dīpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pācanam (पाचनम्; SAT SAT-F.61): enhancing digestion. Process by which the undigested food, doṣa, āma etc are digested. Category: action (karma).
title: pācanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśamana-karma (संशमन-कर्म; SAT SAT-F.62): pacifying therapy, alleviating therapy. Therapy which neither removes doṣa from the body nor increases normal doṣa but only corrects the imbalance of doṣa. Category: action (karma).
title: saṁśamana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anulomanam (अनुलोमनम्; SAT SAT-F.63): mild purgative action/regularizing physiological movement. Therapeutic action of digesting or transforming the undigested materials (food, doṣa etc.) and propels them downward by acting as mild laxatives or normalizing the physiological movements of doṣa. Category: action (karma).
title: anulomanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sraṁsana-karma (स्रंसन-कर्म; SAT SAT-F.64): laxative. Kind of purgatives which separate and remove the undigested substances and toxins adhered to the linings of the intestines without digesting them. Category: action (karma).
title: sraṁsana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhedanam (भेदनम्; SAT SAT-F.65): drastic purgatives. Purgatives which breaks down the hardness of stool and eliminate them. Category: action (karma).
title: bhedanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: recana-karma (रेचन-कर्म/ विरेचन-कर्म/ प्रस्कन्दन-कर्म; SAT SAT-F.66): a form of osmotic laxative. Also called virecana-karma and praskandana-karma. Class of purgatives which liquefies the doṣa and eliminate them or substances that expels excreta by increasing its liquid content;. Category: action (karma).
title: recana-karma virecana-karma praskandana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśodhanam (संशोधनम्; SAT SAT-F.67): eliminative. Expelling out vitiated doṣa and mala through various body openings viz mouth, nose, anus, etc. Category: action (karma).
title: saṁśodhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: chedanam (छेदनम्; SAT SAT-F.68): detachment of vitiated doṣa. Therapeutic action which forcefully separate the doṣa completely and remove them out of body. Category: action (karma).
title: chedanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lekhanam (लेखनम्; SAT SAT-F.69): therapeutic scrapping. Therapeutic action which dries up body tissues and then literally scraps up the unwanted substances out from the body. Category: action (karma).
title: lekhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: grāhī (ग्राही; SAT SAT-F.70): absorptive. Substances with therapeutic action of both dīpana and pācana which dries up excessive liquid portion due to its uṣṇa property. Category: action (karma).
title: grāhī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: stambhanam (स्तम्भनम्; SAT SAT-F.71): check any flow through or out of the body. Action of rūkṣa, śīta and kaṣāya dravya which increase vāta and check any flow through or out of the body or has styptic action. Category: action (karma).
title: stambhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukrajananam (शुक्रजननम्; SAT SAT-F.72): reproductive tissue promoting. Therapeutic measure having spermatogenic properties. Category: action (karma).
title: śukrajananam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukraprasādanam (शुक्रप्रसादनम्; SAT SAT-F.73): normalizers of semen. Substances or therapeutic action which bring back normalcy in quality/ quanity of semen/sperm. Category: action (karma).
title: śukraprasādanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukralaḥ (शुक्रलः; SAT SAT-F.74): semenogague. Therapeutic action that causes increase of semen. Category: action (karma).
title: śukralaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukraśodhanam (शुक्रशोधनम्; SAT SAT-F.75): reproductive tissue depurant. Therapy or medicines which have the potency of purifying the semen. Category: action (karma).
title: śukraśodhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukrotpādaka ḥ (शुक्रोत्पादकः; SAT SAT-F.76): semenogague/ spematogenic. Therapeutic action that generates semen and androgens. Category: action (karma).
title: śukrotpādaka ḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukrasya āpyāyanam (शुक्रस्य आप्यायनम्; SAT SAT-F.77): maintaining normal production of semen. Therapeutic measures done to maintain the normal production of the semen. Category: action (karma).
title: śukrasya āpyāyanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śukrapravartakaḥ (शुक्रप्रवर्तकः; SAT SAT-F.78): promoting ejaculation. Therapeutic action that causes ejaculation. Category: action (karma).
title: śukrapravartakaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣāṇḍhyakara (षाण्ढ्यकर/ पुंस्त्वोपघातिन्; SAT SAT-F.79): dravya that hamper male sexual and reproductive ability. Also called puṁstvopaghātin. Dravya hampering male sexual and reproductive ability. Category: action (karma).
title: ṣāṇḍhyakara puṁstvopaghātin

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ārtavajanana (आर्तवजनन; SAT SAT-F.80): drugs stimulating menstrual blood flow or ovulation. Dravya producing/inducing menstrual blood flow or ovulation. Category: action (karma).
title: ārtavajanana

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhasthāpakaḥ (गर्भस्थापकः; SAT SAT-F.81): preventive measures for abortion and promotive measures for fetal health and quality. Medicines used to prevent the abortion and to promote health and qualities of intrauterine fetus. Category: action (karma).
title: garbhasthāpakaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhasthāpanam (गर्भस्थापनम्/ प्रजास्थापनम्; SAT SAT-F.82): substances which helps sustenance of fetus. Also called prajāsthāpanam. Therapeutic measure which counteract the effect of harmful factors (acting as anti abortifacient) and helps in proper maintenance of fetus or pregnancy and also promotes fertility. Category: action (karma).
title: garbhasthāpanam prajāsthāpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhaśātana-dravyam (गर्भशातन-द्रव्यम्/गर्भपातन-द्रव्यम्; SAT SAT-F.83): abortificient drugs. Also called garbhapātanadravyam. Drugs which induces abortion. Category: action (karma).
title: garbhaśātana-dravyam garbhapātanadravyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: garbhapratibandhakayogaḥ (गर्भप्रतिबन्धकयोगः/वन्ध्याकरयोगः; SAT SAT-F.84): contraceptive drugs. Also called vandhyākarayogaḥ. Drugs which prevent conception. Category: action (karma).
title: garbhapratibandhakayogaḥ vandhyākarayogaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āvijananam (आविजननम्; SAT SAT-F.85): labor inducing drugs. Dravya having ability to induce labor pain. Category: action (karma).
title: āvijananam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: stanyajananam (स्तन्यजननम्; SAT SAT-F.86): galactagogue. Substances which increases the volume of breast milk. Category: action (karma).
title: stanyajananam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: stanyaśodhanam (स्तन्यशोधनम्; SAT SAT-F.87): galacto depurant. Substances which rectifies vitiated breast milk. Category: action (karma).
title: stanyaśodhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: netryam (नेत्र्यम्; SAT SAT-F.88): dravya or intervention good for eye and eye sight. Treatment modalities or drugs which are beneficial for the the eye. Category: action (karma).
title: netryam
