source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhaiṣajyakalpanā (भैषज्यकल्पना; SAT SAT-G.1): ayurvedic pharmaceutics. Preparation of medicines, specifically indicating compounds containing plant, mineral and animal origin ingredients.
title: bhaiṣajyakalpanā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasaśāstram (रसशास्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.2): science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications. Branch of ayurvedic pharmaceutics in which various metals, Minerals and other substances, including mercury, are purified and combined with herbs for therapeutic purpose.
title: rasaśāstram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anupānam (अनुपानम्; SAT SAT-G.3): co-administers with medicine. Adjunct administered either along with or just after the principal medicine to enhance its therapeutic action. (When administered with the principal medicine it is described as Sahapāna, though in practice, the term Anupāna connotes both). Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: anupānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: amṛtīkaraṇam (अमृतीकरणम्; SAT SAT-G.4): purifying procedure. Process adopted to remove the residual doṣa and to enhance the therapeutic action of drugs (as in the case of Tāmra Bhasma). Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: amṛtīkaraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kajjalī (कज्जली; SAT SAT-G.5): black mixture of mercury and sulphur. When sulphur (gandhaka) is added to mercury (pārada) and triturated without adding any liquid till it becomes a very fine black powder, akin to Aethiops Mineralis. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: kajjalī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāñjikam (काञ्जिकम्; SAT SAT-G.6): sour rice gruel. Powder of āśudhanya such as kulmāṣa, ṣaṣṭika rice etc., along with small quantity of white radish (mūlaka), cut into pieces, and placed in an closed earthen pot with water and kept for two to three weeks making a sour fluid called kāṅjika, dhānyāmla or ār. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: kāñjikam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kūpīpākaḥ (कूपीपाकः; SAT SAT-G.7): processing by heating medicines in glass flask/bottle. Process by which, formulations are prepared in a kāca kūpi which, is heated as directed. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: kūpīpākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ghanaḥ (घनः; SAT SAT-G.8): thick liquid concentrate. Desired drug is taken with eight or sixteen times of water and boiled with mild heat until one-eighth remains then filtered and boiled again to get a semi solid concentrate. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: ghanaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ghanasattvam (घनसत्त्वम्; SAT SAT-G.9): semisolid extract. Desired drug is washed well with water and cut into small pieces and added with four times water and boiled on mild heat till one-fourth water remains and then filtered and further heated till the water is evaporated and the decoction is reduced to a semi. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: ghanasattvam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ghṛtamūrcchanam (घृतमूर्च्छनम्; SAT SAT-G.10): process to remove ām and gandha doṣa from ghṛta. Ghṛta is boiled in a vessel till it becomes free from froth and cooled. The kalka (paste) of desired drugs is added and boiled with mild heated to remove ām and gandha doṣa from ghṛta. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: ghṛtamūrcchanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: caṇakāmlaḥ (चणकाम्लः; SAT SAT-G.11): powder made from dew drops collected from caṇa plant. Dew drops appearing on caṇa plant (Cicer arientinum) are collected and evaporated by heating until a very small amount remains and further dried by keeping the vessel under sun to make a powder. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: caṇakāmlaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cūrṇodakam (चूर्णोदकम्/ शुद्धोदकम्; SAT SAT-G.12): lime water. Also called śuddhodakam. Filtrate obtained by mixing 60ml of water with 250 mg of lime powder, keeping for 9 hours and then filtering through a filter paper after decantation. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: cūrṇodakam śuddhodakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirmalīkaraṇam (निर्मलीकरणम्; SAT SAT-G.13): purification method. Various methods for purification of the desired drug (like nirmalīkaraṇa of ṭaṅkaṇa where part of the drug is added to specific amount of water and filtered and the filtrate is boiled to evaporate the water and dried to remove moisture completely). Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: nirmalīkaraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ḍhālanam (ढालनम्; SAT SAT-G.14): pouring molten metal into a liquid. Process of process of pouring molten metal into specified liquid. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: ḍhālanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: taṇḍulodakam (तण्डुलोदकम्; SAT SAT-G.15): rice water. Liquid obtained by mixing 48 gm of rice with 385 ml of water keeping for two hours and thereafter decanting. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: taṇḍulodakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tuṣāmbu (तुषाम्बु; SAT SAT-G.16): barley water. Decanted liquid obtained from a mixture of equal quantity of crushed barley and warm water kept over night. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: tuṣāmbu

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tailamūrcchanam (तैलमूर्च्छनम्; SAT SAT-G.17): process to remove gandha doṣa from taila. Tila taila is taken in a vessel and boiled till it becomes free from froth then it is cooled and then added with water and the kalka of desired drugs and boiled till water content is lost, it removes gandhadoṣa (undesired smell) from oil. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: tailamūrcchanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhūpanam (धूपनम्; SAT SAT-G.18): fumigation. Process of fumigating a pot or a vessel with the prescribed drugs. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: dhūpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirutthaḥ (निरुत्थः/ अपुनर्भवः; SAT SAT-G.19): inability to revert back into its metal form. Also called apunarbhavaḥ. Property of bhasma from which it cannot be reverted to its metallic form (even if mixed with mitrapañcaka and heated to the temperature at which the bhasma is prepared). Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: nirutthaḥ apunarbhavaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirvāpaṇam (निर्वापणम्/ निमज्जनम्; SAT SAT-G.20): immersion of heated solid in liquid. Also called nimajjanam. Process of immersing the heated solid ingredients in a specified liquid. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: nirvāpaṇam nimajjanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parpaṭī (पर्पटी; SAT SAT-G.21): thin flakes made from kajjali. Thin flakes prepared from kajjali by heating and melting it with or without other drugs. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: parpaṭī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakṣepaḥ (प्रक्षेपः; SAT SAT-G.22): adding powdered substance. Fine powder of drugs added to a kalpa such as leha, Āsavāriṣṭa etc. to enhance taste, palatability and bioavailability of the drug. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: prakṣepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratinidhi dravyam (प्रतिनिधिद्रव्यम्; SAT SAT-G.23): substitute drug. Drug or herbs which can be used in unavailability of desired drug. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: pratinidhi dravyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhānupākaḥ (भानुपाकः; SAT SAT-G.24): heating by sun heat. Process of giving heat by keeping it under the sun like evaporation of water from a medicinal preparation by exposing to sun. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: bhānupākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhāvanā (भावना; SAT SAT-G.25): pulverization by adding a liquid to a powder. Process by which powders of drugs are pulverized to a soft mass with liquid substances and allowed to dry to enhance its properties. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: bhāvanā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mardanam (मर्दनम्; SAT SAT-G.26): pulverization. Triturating of drugs to a fine state of division with or without prescribed liquid. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: mardanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mastu (मस्तु; SAT SAT-G.27): curd whey. Liquid separated from curd. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: mastu

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: māraṇam (मारणम्; SAT SAT-G.28): process of making bhasma. Process by which metals and minerals are grinded with liquids and then dried and made into bhasma by heat. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: māraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūrcchanam (मूर्च्छनम्; SAT SAT-G.29): procedure for removal of āma and gandha doṣa of taila/ghṛta. Procedure for removal of āmadoṣa of taila/ghṛta and gives colour and fragrance. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: mūrcchanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūṣā (मूषा; SAT SAT-G.30): vessel for satvapātana etc.. Special kind of vessel used in satvapātana etc. It is generally prepared with burnt husk, china clay etc. after making them into a soft pulp. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: mūṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasakriyā (रसक्रिया; SAT SAT-G.31): concentrated thick liquid. Desired drug is made into decoction which is filtered and then concentrated to make a thick syrup of phāṇita (raw jaggery) like consistency similar to ghana. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: rasakriyā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lākṣārasaḥ (लाक्षारसः; SAT SAT-G.32): water made from lākṣā. Liquid obtained by subjecting the bundled mass of lākṣā (Laccifer Lacca) in six times of water in dolāyantra and straining it, twenty one times. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: lākṣārasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śarāvaḥ (शरावः; SAT SAT-G.33): earthen shallow vessel. Round shaped shallow earthen vessel. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: śarāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śodhanam (शोधनम्; SAT SAT-G.34): purifying process. Process of removal of impurities and potentiating of drugs. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: śodhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sandhānam (सन्धानम्; SAT SAT-G.35): fermentation. Process of fermentation of liquid with desired drugs. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: sandhānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sandhilepanam (सन्धिलेपनम्; SAT SAT-G.36): sealing of vessel joint. Sealing the edges of a vessel, with the lid on, at the point of contact, with a paste of clay and cloth. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: sandhilepanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: surā (सुरा/ प्रसन्ना; SAT SAT-G.37): supernatant alcohol. Also called prasannā. Supernatant liquid containing self generated alcohol obtained from fermentation any cooked cereal, prasannā is the clear supernatant portion Surā. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: surā prasannā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sthālīpākaḥ (स्थालीपाकः; SAT SAT-G.38): heating in pan under fire. Heating of desired substance in a pan under fire (pāka of lauha made in a sthāli (iron pan) on strong fire). Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: sthālīpākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svāṅgaśītam (स्वाङ्गशीतम्; SAT SAT-G.39): self cooled. When heated materials attain atmospheric temperature in situ by itself. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: svāṅgaśītam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kalpanā (कल्पना; SAT SAT-G.40): forms of medicine. Various forms in which medicine are made. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: kalpanā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kalkaḥ (कल्कः; SAT SAT-G.41): paste. Fine paste of the fresh herbal drug. Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: kalkaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kvāthaḥ (क्वाथः; SAT SAT-G.42): decoction. Decoction obtained by boiling coarse powder of drug(s) in specified proportions of water and reduced to certain amount. Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: kvāthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cūrṇam (चूर्णम्; SAT SAT-G.43): powder. Fine sieved powder of well-dried drug(s). Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: cūrṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: puṭapāka svarasaḥ (पुटपाकस्वरसः; SAT SAT-G.44): heat extracted juice. Juice extracted after heating a bolus of herbs covered in various substances at a desired temperature. Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: puṭapāka svarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: phāṇṭam (फाण्टम्; SAT SAT-G.45): hot infusion. The infusion obtained by pouring boiling water on the powdered drug(s) and used after filtering. Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: phāṇṭam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svarasaḥ (स्वरसः; SAT SAT-G.46): juice. Juice of fresh plant material obtained by various methods. Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: svarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: himakaṣāyaḥ (हिमकषायः; SAT SAT-G.47): cold infusion. The infusion obtained by keeping overnight the desired herb powder in cold water and used after filtering. Category: forms of medicine (kalpanā).
title: himakaṣāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: puṭaḥ (पुटः; SAT SAT-G.48): measure of heat. Measure of heat in terms of various heating arrangements meant for preparing various kinds of bhasma. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: puṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kapotapuṭaḥ (कपोतपुटः; SAT SAT-G.49): a type of heating arrangement. An arrangement using eight cow-dung cakes as fuel (vanyopala). Category: measure of heat (puṭaḥ).
title: kapotapuṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gajapuṭaḥ (गजपुटः; SAT SAT-G.50): a type of heating arrangement. An arrangement of heating in a pit of 90 cm in length, breadth and depth filled cow dung cakes. Category: measure of heat (puṭaḥ).
title: gajapuṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: varāhapuṭaḥ (वराहपुटः; SAT SAT-G.51): a type of heating arrangement. An arrangement of heating in a pit of 60 cm in length, breadth and depth filled with cow-dung cakes. Category: measure of heat (puṭaḥ).
title: varāhapuṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ardha-gajapuṭaḥ (अर्ध-गजपुटः; SAT SAT-G.52): a type of heating arrangement. An arrangement of heating of the size that is half of a gajapuṭa. Category: measure of heat (puṭaḥ).
title: ardha-gajapuṭaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yantram (यन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.53): instrument for medicine preparation. Instrument; equipment; Machine for the preparation of various types of medicines. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: yantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: arkayantram (अर्कयन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.54): instrument for distillation. An alchemical apparatus for distillation used to make arka. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: arkayantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: khalvayantram (खल्वयन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.55): mortar with pestle. Mortar with pestle, made of various stones in different shapes and sizes. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: khalvayantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ḍamaruyantram (डमरुयन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.56): instrument for sublimation. An alchemical apparatus in ḍamaru shape for sublimation. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: ḍamaruyantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tiryakapātana- yantram (तिर्यकपातन- यन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.57): oblique distillation instrument. An alchemical apparatus for distillation of various drugs like Mercury with the delivery tank weld to it obliquely. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: tiryakapātana- yantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: darvikayantram (दर्विकयन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.58): ladle shaped instrument for heating. Iron ladle, with a long handle. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: darvikayantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ḍolāyantram (डोलायन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.59): instrument for giving heat by suspension of drug in liquid. An alchemical apparatus consisting of a pot half filled with specified liquid with a horizontal rod placed on the rim from which the bundle of material to be treated will be immersed and heated. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: ḍolāyantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bālukāyantram (बालुकायन्त्रम्; SAT SAT-G.60): heating instrument using sand. Big-mouthed hollow earthen vessel filled with sand used to heat layered kāñca kūpī. Category: instrument for medicine preparation (yantram).
title: bālukāyantram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ (पारद-अष्टसंस्कारः; SAT SAT-G.61): eight processing done on pārada. Main eight procedures used for purification and potentiating pārada from its raw form to medically useful form and also for metallurgic procedures. Category: science dealing with study of metals especially mercury, minerals and their therapeutic applications (rasaśāstram).
title: pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svedanam (स्वेदनम्; SAT SAT-G.62): sudation of pārada. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, sudation of pārada (generally done in dolāyantra). Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: svedanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mardanam (मर्दनम्; SAT SAT-G.63): trituration of pārada. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, trituration of pārada (generally done in khalvayantra). Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: mardanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūrcchanam (मूर्च्छनम्; SAT SAT-G.64): trituration of pārada. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, where pārada is triturated to the level so as to remove all its impurities (vahni, mala, viṣa) and pārada become inactive (mūrchita or swooned). Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: mūrcchanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: utthāpanam (उत्थापनम्; SAT SAT-G.65): reviving of mūrchita pārada. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, where pārada is potentiated again from inactive (mūrchita or swooned) form of pārada done by sudations with various drugs. Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: utthāpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pātanam (पातनम्; SAT SAT-G.66): distillation producers of pārada. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, various procedures of distillation of pārada (three types Ūrdhvapātana, Adhahpātana and Tiryakpātana) done after utthāpana. Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: pātanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ūrdhvapātanam (ऊर्ध्वपातनम्; SAT SAT-G.67): upward distillation of pārada. Subtype of pātana samskara where distillation is done in upward direction. Category: distillation producers of pārada (pātanam).
title: ūrdhvapātanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adhaḥpātana (अधःपातनम्; SAT SAT-G.68): downward distillation of pārada. Subtype of pātana samskara where distillation is done in downward direction. Category: distillation producers of pārada (pātanam).
title: adhaḥpātana

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tiryak-pātanam (तिर्यक्-पातनम्; SAT SAT-G.69): oblique distillation of pārada. Subtype of pātana samskara where distillation is done in oblique direction. Category: distillation producers of pārada (pātanam).
title: tiryak-pātanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bodhanam (बोधनम्/ रोधनम्; SAT SAT-G.70): potentiation of pārada. Also called rodhanam. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, procedure to remove impotency of pārada by reducing impurities, which occurs due to its previous samskara (done by various methods including sudation, keeping it in salt water in a earthen pot etc.). Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: bodhanam rodhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: niyamanam (नियमनम्; SAT SAT-G.71): procedure to control mobility of pārada. One of the aṣṭa pārada saṁskāra, where paste of various drug with pārada kept in desired liquid and is bundled in a poṭṭali and sudation is done by dolāyantra to control its mobility which was imparted due to bodhana saṁskāra. Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: niyamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dīpanam (दीपनम्/ संदीपनम्; SAT SAT-G.72): procedure in which pārada is made capable of amalgamating other entities. Also called saṁdīpanam. Pārada after niyaman saṁskāra mixed with various herbs is subjected to sudation in dolāyantra to make it capable of swallowing, digesting or amalgamating other entities. Category: eight processing done on pārada (pārada-aṣṭasaṁskāraḥ).
title: dīpanam saṁdīpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mānam (मानम्; SAT SAT-G.73): nomenclature pertaining to measurement. Various nomenclatures used for measurement in different form like length, weight and volume. Category: ayurvedic pharmaceutics (bhaiṣajyakalpanā).
title: mānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhāraḥ (भारः/पौतवमानम्; SAT SAT-G.74): weight. Also called pautavamānabhāram. Various measures of weight. Category: nomenclature pertaining to measurement (mānam).
title: bhāraḥ pautavamānabhāram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rattī (रत्ती/ गुञ्जा; SAT SAT-G.75): weight equivalent to one standard fruit of guñjā/rattī. Also called guñjā. Measure of weight; equal to one fruit of guñjā rattī generally taken as 125 mg. Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: rattī guñjā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: māṣaḥ (माषः; SAT SAT-G.76): weight equivalent to eight standard fruit of guñjā/rattī. Measure of weight; equal to eight fruit of guñjā rattī generally taken as 1 gm. Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: māṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karṣaḥ (कर्षः/तोला; SAT SAT-G.77): weight equal to 12 māṣa. Also called tolā. Measure of weight; equal to 12 māṣa i.e. 11.66375 gm or 12 gm. Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: karṣaḥ tolā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śuktiḥ (शुक्तिः; SAT SAT-G.78): weight equivalent to two tolā. Measure of weight equal to 2 tolā i.e. 24 gm. Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: śuktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: palam (पलम्; SAT SAT-G.79): weight equivalent to 4 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 4 tolā i.e. 48 gm (2 śukti). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: palam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prasṛtiḥ (प्रसृतिः; SAT SAT-G.80): weight equivalent to 8 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 8 tolā i.e. 96 gm (2 pala). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: prasṛtiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kuḍavaḥ (कुडवः; SAT SAT-G.81): weight equivalent to 16 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 16 tolā i.e. 192 gm (2 prasṛti). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: kuḍavaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mānikā (मानिका/शरावः; SAT SAT-G.82): weight equivalent to 32 tolā. Also called śarāvaḥ. Measure of weight equal to 32 tolā i.e. 384 gm (2 kuḍava). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: mānikā śarāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prasthaḥ (प्रस्थः; SAT SAT-G.83): weight equivalent to 64 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 64 tolā i.e. 768 gm (2 mānikā). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: prasthaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āḍhakam (आढकम्; SAT SAT-G.84): weight equivalent to 256 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 256 tolā i.e. 3 kg and 72 gm (4 prastha). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: āḍhakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: droṇaḥ (द्रोणः; SAT SAT-G.85): weight equivalent to 1024 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 1024 tolā i.e. 12 kg and 288 gm (4 āḍhaka). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: droṇaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śūrpaḥ (शूर्पः; SAT SAT-G.86): weight equivalent to 2048 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 2048 tolā i.e. 24 kg and 576 gm (2 droṇa). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: śūrpaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: droṇī (vāhi) (द्रोणी (वाहि); SAT SAT-G.87): weight equivalent to 4096 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 4096 tolā i.e. 49 kg and 152 gm (2 śūrpa). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: droṇī (vāhi)

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: khāriḥ (खारिः; SAT SAT-G.88): weight equivalent to 16384 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 16384 tolā i.e. 196 kg and 608 gm (4 droṇi). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: khāriḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tulā (तुला; SAT SAT-G.89): weight equivalent to 400 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 400 tolā i.e. 4 kg 800 gm (100 pala). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: tulā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhāraḥ (भारः; SAT SAT-G.90): weight equivalent to 8000 tolā. Measure of weight equal to 8000 tolā i.e. 96 kg (20 tulā). Category: weight (bhāraḥ).
title: bhāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dairghyam (दैर्घ्यम्/ पाय्यमानम्; SAT SAT-G.91): measurement of distance. Also called pāyyamānam. Nomenclature of measurement of length. Category: nomenclature pertaining to measurement (mānam).
title: dairghyam pāyyamānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yavodaraḥ (यवोदरः; SAT SAT-G.92): length equivalent to thickness of yava at its center. Length taken by a thin string to cross through the center of one yava or thickness of yava at its center, equivalent to 1/8 of 3/4 inch i.e. 0.24 cm. Category: measurement of distance (dairghyam).
title: yavodaraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aṅgulaḥ (अङ्गुलः; SAT SAT-G.93): length equal to 8 yava. Distance of 8 yava dhānya (barley seed) placed one after other or 3/4 inches or 1.94 cm (average but it differs in every individual). Category: measurement of distance (dairghyam).
title: aṅgulaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vitastiḥ (वितस्तिः; SAT SAT-G.94): distance between tips of thumb and little finger spread out. Equivalent to distance between tip of thumb and tip of little finder spread out approximately 9 inches or 22.86 cm also taken equal to 12 aṅgula (23.4 cm). Category: measurement of distance (dairghyam).
title: vitastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aratniḥ (अरत्निः; SAT SAT-G.95): distance between elbow and the tip of little finger. Distance equivalent to distance between elbow and the tip of the little finger that is 16.5 inch, 41.91 cm or 22 aṅgula approximately. Category: measurement of distance (dairghyam).
title: aratniḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hastaḥ (हस्तः; SAT SAT-G.96): cubit. Distance equivalent to 18 inches or 45.72 cm from tip of middle finger to olecranon process or elbow. Category: measurement of distance (dairghyam).
title: hastaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāmaḥ (व्यामः; SAT SAT-G.97): between tip of middle fingers of out stretched upper limbs. Distance between tip of middle fingers of out stretched upper limbs equivalent to 72 inches or 182.88 cm. Category: measurement of distance (dairghyam).
title: vyāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālamānaḥ (कालमानः; SAT SAT-G.98): measure of time. Nomenclature for measurement of time. Category: nomenclature pertaining to measurement (mānam).
title: kālamānaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣaṇam (क्षणम्/ निमेषः; SAT SAT-G.99): time taken in one blink of eye. Also called nimeṣaḥ. Time taken in pronunciation of a syllable (laghu akṣara) i.e. 0.16 seconds approx. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: kṣaṇam nimeṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāṣṭhā (काष्ठा; SAT SAT-G.100): time equivalent to 15 nimeṣa. Time that is fifteen times of nimeṣa i.e. 2.38 second. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: kāṣṭhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kalā (कला; SAT SAT-G.101): time equivalent to 30 kāṣṭhā. Time which is 30 times of kāṣṭhā i.e. 71.4 seconds (1 minute 11 seconds approx.). Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: kalā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ghaṭī (घटी/ नाडिका; SAT SAT-G.102): time equal to 20 kalā and 3 kāṣṭhā. Also called nāḍikā. Time equal to 20 kalā and 3 kāṣṭhā i.e. 24 min (1440 seconds). Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: ghaṭī nāḍikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: muhūrtaḥ (मुहूर्तः; SAT SAT-G.103): time equivalent to two nāḍīkā. Time which is equal to two nāḍīkā i.e. 48 min. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: muhūrtaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yāmaḥ (यामः; SAT SAT-G.104): time equivalent to one fourth of a day or night. Time which is equal to ¼ of day or night; time that is four times of muhūrta plus 1/4th of muhūrta) i.e. 3 hours. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: yāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ahorātraḥ (अहोरात्रः; SAT SAT-G.105): time equivalent to a day and night. Time equal to a day and night i.e. 24 hours or a complete day. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: ahorātraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pakṣaḥ (पक्षः; SAT SAT-G.106): 15 days. Time that is half of a lunar month i.e. 15 days. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: pakṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: māsaḥ (मासः; SAT SAT-G.107): one month. Time that is equal to one lunar month or 30 days (two pakṣa). Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: māsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṛtuḥ (ऋतुः; SAT SAT-G.108): time of one season. Time that is equal to one season i.e. 2 lunar months or 60 days. Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).
title: ṛtuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ayanam (अयनम्; SAT SAT-G.109): time of three seasons. Time that is equal to three season i.e. 6 lunar months or 180 days (divided based on movement of sun in respect to earth as uttarāyana dakṣiṇāyana). Category: measure of time (kālamānaḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: kāmbalikaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: kṛśarā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: vāṭya-maṇḍaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: māṁsarasaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: kṣīra-vargaḥ

title: kṣīrāṣṭakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: dadhi-vargaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: gholaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mathitaḥ (मथितः; SAT SAT-H.84): buttermilk churned without water. Type of curd preparation in which curd is churned without adding water after removing butter. Category: group of yoghurts (dadhi-vargaḥ).
title: mathitaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udaśvit (उदश्वित्; SAT SAT-H.85): buttermilk having half quantity of water in it. Type of curd preparation in which curd is churned by adding 1/2 quantity of the water. Category: group of yoghurts (dadhi-vargaḥ).
title: udaśvit

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: takram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: kaṭvaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: takra-kūrcikā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dadhi-kūrcikā (दधि-कूर्चिका; SAT SAT-H.91): solid part of milk boiled with curd. When the milk is boiled with curd, the obtained solid portion is called dadhi kūrcikā. Category: group of yoghurts (dadhi-vargaḥ).
title: dadhi-kūrcikā

title: pīyūṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

text: dadhimastu (दधिमस्तु; SAT SAT-H.94): watery part of the curd. Supernatant liquid portion of the curd. Category: group of yoghurts (dadhi-vargaḥ).
title: dadhimastu

title: madhuvarga

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣaudram (क्षौद्रम्; SAT SAT-H.96): variety of honey. Variety of brownish colored honey produced by small type of honey-bee. Category: group of honey (madhuvarga).
title: kṣaudram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhrāmaram (भ्रामरम्; SAT SAT-H.98): variety of honey. Variety of whitish colored honey produced by large black bee. Category: group of honey (madhuvarga).
title: bhrāmaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mākṣikam (माक्षिकम्; SAT SAT-H.99): variety of honey. Variety of honey with color similar to oil and produced by tawny colored honey bee. It is considered as the best among other varieties of honey. Category: group of honey (madhuvarga).
title: mākṣikam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: antarikṣa-jalam āntarikṣa-udakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nādeya-udakam (नादेय-उदकम्; SAT SAT-H.103): river water. Water obtained from rivers. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).

text: tauṣāram (तौषारम्; SAT SAT-H.104): dew water. Water obtained from dew drops formed at night in the cold seasons or rain water accumulated on leaves. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: tauṣāram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: audbhida-jalam (औद्भिद-जलम्; SAT SAT-H.105): spring water. Water which springs naturally from the earth. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: audbhida-jalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāram (कारम्; SAT SAT-H.106): water derived from hailstone. Source of water which is drawn from liquefaction of hailstones. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaupam (कौपम्; SAT SAT-H.107): well water. Kind of water derived from well which is considered suitable in spring and summer seasons. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: kaupam

text: gāṅgajalam (गाङ्गजलम्; SAT SAT-H.108): uncontaminated water. Type of water which is not contaminated with dust, soot, and toxic gases other environmental impurities. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: gāṅgajalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhāram (धारम्; SAT SAT-H.109): fall water. Type of water which is originated from the mountain in the form of falls. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).

text: prāsravaṇam (प्रास्रवणम्; SAT SAT-H.110): water derived from a spring or fountain. Type of water derived from small falls or fountain. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: prāsravaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāpyam (वाप्यम्; SAT SAT-H.111): step well water. Type of water derived from step well. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: vāpyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmudra-jalam (सामुद्र-जलम्; SAT SAT-H.112): surface water. Surface water which is very much prone for contamination with dust, soot, toxic substances, micro organisms or any other environmental impurities. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: sāmudra-jalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sārasam (सारसम्; SAT SAT-H.113): lake water. Type of water derived from lakes which is best for consumption in hemanta ṛtu (early winter). Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: haṁsodakam (हंसोदकम्; SAT SAT-H.114): water detoxified by exposure to rays of the sun and the moon and also Agastya star.
