title: haṁsodakam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: haimam (हैमम्; SAT SAT-H.115): water derived from snow. Type of water derived from liquefaction of ice or snow. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: haimam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tāḍāgam (ताडागम्; SAT SAT-H.116): tank or pond water. Type of water which is derived from artificial tanks or ponds. Category: group of various types of water (ambuvargaḥ).
title: tāḍāgam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cikitsā (चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I): treatment. Various interventions such as drugs, procedures and life style modifications used for the management of various disease conditions.
title: cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāya-cikitsā (काय-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.1): general medicine. One among the eight clinical branches of āyurveda. It deals with management of generalised systemic diseases.
title: kāya-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāyaḥ (कायः; SAT SAT-I.2): digestive/metabolic factors of the body. All factors responsible for digestion and metabolism / transformation. Category: general medicine (kāya-cikitsā).
title: kāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cikitsā (चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.3): disease management/ treatment. Treatment which eradicate or normalise the impaired dośa and establishes the equilibrium of all the dhātu restoring the normal structure and function of bodily elements. Category: general medicine (kāya-cikitsā).
title: cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhiharam (व्याधिहरम्; SAT SAT-I.4): removal of disease. Synonym of cikitsā; Removal of disease e.g. jvara nivṛtti in jvara. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: vyādhiharam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pathyam (पथ्यम्; SAT SAT-I.5): compatible to health. Synonym of cikitsā; the dietary and behavioural practices helpful in treating the disease or maintaining health. e.g lāja in chardi. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: pathyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sādhanam (साधनम्; SAT SAT-I.6): practice towards mitigating the cause and effect of the disease. Synonym of cikitsā; instrument by which the disease is cured and health is restored. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: sādhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: auṣadham (औषधम्; SAT SAT-I.7): medicine. Synonym of cikitsā; therapeutic measures by which the disease is cured and health is restored. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: auṣadham

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upakramaḥ (उपक्रमः; SAT SAT-I.8): therapeutic methods/ measures. Synonym of cikitsā; the therapeutic measures to counteract the disease condition. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: upakramaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāyaścittam (प्रायश्चित्तम्; SAT SAT-I.9): repentance/ atonement. Synonym of cikitsā; atonement to cure the diseases caused due to wrong deeds [also mentioned as a type of daivavyapaśraya cikitsā]. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: prāyaścittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: praśamanam (प्रशमनम्; SAT SAT-I.10): subsiding the disease. Synonym of cikitsā; the process of subsidence of disease e.g alleviation of burning sensation (dāhapraśamana) in case of dāha. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: praśamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakṛti-sthāpanam (प्रकृति-स्थापनम्; SAT SAT-I.11): restoration of health. Synonym of cikitsā; process of restoration of health. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: prakṛti-sthāpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hitam (हितम्; SAT SAT-I.12): conducive to health. Synonym of cikitsā; wholesome āhāra (food), vihāra (all activities such as daily routine etc. and auṣadha (medication) which are conducive to health. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: hitam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vāraṇam (वारणम्; SAT SAT-I.13): warding off diseases. Synonym of cikitsā; the process by which the disease is ward off. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: vāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: daivavyapāśrayaḥ (दैवव्यपाश्रयः; SAT SAT-I.14): spiritual therapy. One of the classifications of treatment; spiritual therapies are incantation of mantra, talisman, wearing of gems, auspicious offerings, gifts, oblations, atonement, fasting, going to pilgrimage etc. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: daivavyapāśrayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mantra-cikitsā (मन्त्र-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.15): treatment through chanting of auspicious hymns. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; treatment of diseases by incantation of appropriate mantra under specified conditions. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: mantra-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: maṇiḥ (मणिः; SAT SAT-I.16): wearing of gems. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; treatment of diseases by wearing appropriate gems or precious stones according to the disease. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: maṇiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: maṅgalam (मङ्गलम्; SAT SAT-I.17): auspicious offerings. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: maṅgalam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: baliḥ (बलिः; SAT SAT-I.18): offerings to God exclusive of animal sacrifice. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; type of treatment where something auspicious is offered to God for the cure of ailment. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: baliḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upahāraḥ (उपहारः; SAT SAT-I.19): offerings to God inclusive of animal sacrifice. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; type of treatment with offerings inclusive of animal sacrifice for the cure of ailment. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: upahāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: homam (होमम्; SAT SAT-I.20): oblations or offerings given through fire. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; process of offering of various things in to fire for the cure of ailment. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: homam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: niyamaḥ (नियमः; SAT SAT-I.21): practicing auspicious rules. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; practice of following of certain rules to cure the ailment. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: niyamaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāyaścittam (प्रायश्चित्तम्; SAT SAT-I.22): atonement. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: prāyaścittam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upavāsaḥ (उपवासः; SAT SAT-I.23): fasting. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; practice of fasting for the cure of ailment. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: upavāsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svastyayanam (स्वस्त्ययनम्; SAT SAT-I.24): blessings from elders. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; taking blessings (āśirvāda) to get cured from ailment. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: svastyayanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: praṇipātagamanam (प्रणिपातगमनम्; SAT SAT-I.25): pilgrimage. Type of daivavyapāśraya cikitsā; visiting to some holy place to get cured from disease. Category: spiritual therapy (daivavyapāśrayaḥ).
title: praṇipātagamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yuktivyapāśraya-cikitsā (युक्तिव्यपाश्रय-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.26): logic based treatment. Rational and logical therapeutic intervention within the ambit of human intelligence; one of the classifications of treatment wherein modalities like administration of medicine, diet and other logical methods are applied for treatment. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: yuktivyapāśraya-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhāradravyayojanam (आहारद्रव्ययोजनम्; SAT SAT-I.27): therapeutic dietetics. Administration of proper diet for the management of diseases. Category: logic based treatment (yuktivyapāśraya-cikitsā).
title: āhāradravyayojanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: auṣadhadravyayojanam (औषधद्रव्ययोजनम्; SAT SAT-I.28): therapeutic medication. Administration of medicines for the management of diseases. Category: logic based treatment (yuktivyapāśraya-cikitsā).
title: auṣadhadravyayojanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abheṣajam (अभेषजम्; SAT SAT-I.29): detrimental to health. Antonym of medicine; substances with adverse effect to health. Category: therapeutic medication (auṣadhadravyayojanam).
title: abheṣajam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bādhanam (बाधनम्; SAT SAT-I.30): immediately detrimental to health. One of the two types of abheṣaja e.g. poison, burn by fire or cut by sharp instrument etc. that produce immediate effect after their use. Category: detrimental to health (abheṣajam).
title: bādhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sānubādhanam (सानुबाधनम्; SAT SAT-I.31): detrimental to health in long term. One of the two types of abheśaja e.g. use of incompatible food articles constantly for a long time causes diseases like kuṣṭa. Category: detrimental to health (abheṣajam).
title: sānubādhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bheṣajam (भेषजम्; SAT SAT-I.32): therapeutic measures. Procedure or medicine used for the treatment of disease. Category: therapeutic medication (auṣadhadravyayojanam).
title: bheṣajam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svasthasyorjaskaram (स्वस्थस्योर्जस्करम्; SAT SAT-I.33): which improves vitality in healthy. Medicine or regimen which tones up the health of a healthy person; a feature of rasāyana therapy. Category: therapeutic measures (bheṣajam).
title: svasthasyorjaskaram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rasāyanam (रसायनम्; SAT SAT-I.34): rejuvenation. The procedures or medicines used to improve health and longevity. Category: therapeutic measures (bheṣajam).
title: rasāyanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vājīkaraṇam (वाजीकरणम्; SAT SAT-I.35): aphrodisiac therapy. One among the eight clinical branches of āyurveda concerned with aphrodisiac management. Category: therapeutic measures (bheṣajam).
title: vājīkaraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ārtasyaroganut (आर्तस्यरोगनुत्; SAT SAT-I.36): curative medicine. Medicine which cures the ailments of a patient. Category: therapeutic measures (bheṣajam).
title: ārtasyaroganut

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśamanam (संशमनम्; SAT SAT-I.37): palliative procedure. Therapy which is aimed at mitigating the disease by pacifying dośa (in contrast to purifying therapies, which remove the dośa from the body). Category: therapeutic measures (bheṣajam).
title: saṁśamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dvividhopakramaḥ (द्विविधोपक्रमः; SAT SAT-I.38): two fold therapeutic regimen. A broad classification of therapeutic measures into two sub categories - santarpaṇam and apatarpaṇam. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: dvividhopakramaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: santarpaṇam (सन्तर्पणम्; SAT SAT-I.39): nourishing procedure. A procedure of alleviation of disease by nourishing of bodily tissues. Category: two fold therapeutic regimen (dvividhopakramaḥ).
title: santarpaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: apatarpaṇam (अपतर्पणम्; SAT SAT-I.40): depleting procedure. A procedure of alleviation of disease by depletion of bodily tissues. Category: two fold therapeutic regimen (dvividhopakramaḥ).
title: apatarpaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ (षड्विधोपक्रमाः; SAT SAT-I.41): six types of treatment modalities. Sub division of therapeutic measures in six sub categories namely bṛṁhaṇam, snehanam, stambhanam, laṁghanam, svedanam and rūkṣaṇam. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bṛṁhaṇam (बृंहणम्/बृंहणचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.42): nourishing therapy. Also called bṛṁhaṇacikitsā. One among the ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ; procedure which is nutritive/ nourishing/ increasing body weight / growth promoting or bulk enhancing. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: bṛṁhaṇam bṛṁhaṇacikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: snehanam (स्नेहनम्/स्नेहन-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.43): therapeutic oleation. Also called snehana-karma. One among the ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ which involves the lubricating of bodily systems internally or externally. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: snehanam snehana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: stambhanam (स्तम्भनम्/स्तम्भन-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.44): styptic therapy. Also called stambhana-karma. One among the ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ; procedure or action of drug causing arrest of secretion or control of bleeding. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: stambhanam stambhana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: laṁghanam (लङ्घनम्; SAT SAT-I.45): depleting therapy. One among the ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ; procedure that induces lightness in the body. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: laṁghanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dīpanam (दीपनम्; SAT SAT-I.46): enhancing metabolic fire. Process by which the metabolic fire is enhanced. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: dīpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pācanam (पाचनम्; SAT SAT-I.47): enhancing digestion. Process by which the undigested food, doṣa etc are digested. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: pācanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣudhā (क्षुधा; SAT SAT-I.48): hunger - treatment. Process of keeping the person hungry as a therapeutic measure. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: kṣudhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tṛṣṇā (तृष्णा; SAT SAT-I.49): thirst - treatment. Process of keeping the person thirsty as a therapeutic measure. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: tṛṣṇā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mārutaḥ (मारुतः; SAT SAT-I.50): exposure to wind. Process of exposing the person to wind as a therapeutic measure. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: mārutaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ātapaḥ (आतपः; SAT SAT-I.51): exposure to sunlight. Process of exposing the person to sunlight as a therapeutic measure. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: ātapaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāyāmaḥ (व्यायामः; SAT SAT-I.52): exercise as treatment. Process of making the person to exercise as a therapeutic measure. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: vyāyāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rūkṣaṇam (रूक्षणम्; SAT SAT-I.53): dryness inducing therapies. One among the ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ; procedure that induces dryness. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: rūkṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svedanam (स्वेदनम्; SAT SAT-I.54): sudation therapy. One among the ṣaḍvidhopakramāḥ; procedure adopted to induce sweating. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: svedanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: lepaḥ (लेपः; SAT SAT-I.55): anointment. External application of medicines in the form of a paste. Category: therapeutic measures (bheṣajam).
title: lepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pralepaḥ (प्रलेपः; SAT SAT-I.56): thin anointment. A type of lepa (anointment) which is cold in quality, loose in texture and thus dries up faster. Category: anointment (lepaḥ).
title: pralepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pradehaḥ (प्रदेहः; SAT SAT-I.57): thick anointment. A type of lepa (anointment) which is hot in quality. Category: anointment (lepaḥ).
title: pradehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ālepaḥ (आलेपः; SAT SAT-I.58): anointment with moderate thickness. A type of lepa (anointment) which is moderate in thickness. Category: anointment (lepaḥ).
title: ālepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣaghna-lepaḥ (दोषघ्न-लेपः; SAT SAT-I.59): anointment which alleviates dośa. One among the three types of lepa which alleviates doṣa. Category: anointment (lepaḥ).
title: doṣaghna-lepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viṣaghna-lepaḥ (विषघ्न-लेपः; SAT SAT-I.60): anti-poisonous anointment. One among the three types of lepa which has anti – poisonous effect. Category: anointment (lepaḥ).
title: viṣaghna-lepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: varṇya-lepaḥ (वर्ण्य-लेपः; SAT SAT-I.61): anointment which promotes complexion. One among the three types of lepa which promotes complexion. Category: anointment (lepaḥ).
title: varṇya-lepaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣāvasecanam (दोषावसेचनम्; SAT SAT-I.62): procedure to eliminate morbid doṣa from body. Synonym of śodhana-chikitsa. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: doṣāvasecanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āśukāri-cikitsā (आशुकारि-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.63): fast acting treatment. Treatment which acts quickly such as agnikarma. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: āśukāri-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: apakarṣaṇam (अपकर्षणम्; SAT SAT-I.64): removal of cause of disease. Removal of the doṣa or other harmful substances. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: apakarṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prakṛtivighātaḥ (प्रकृतिविघातः; SAT SAT-I.65): counteracting the cause of disease. Creating conditions hostile to the cause of disease. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: prakṛtivighātaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nidāna-parivarjanam (निदान-परिवर्जनम्; SAT SAT-I.66): avoidance of etiological factors. Necessary prerequisite for cure and prevention of recurrence of disease. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: nidāna-parivarjanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hetuviparītacikitsā (हेतुविपरीतचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.67): cause antagonistic treatment. One among the three fold classification of treatment which is antagonistic to cause. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: hetuviparītacikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyādhiviparītacikitsā (व्याधिविपरीतचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.68): disease antagonistic treatment. One among the three fold classification of treatment which is antagonistic to disease. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: vyādhiviparītacikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ubhayārthakāricikitsā (उभयार्थकारिचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.69): cause and disease antagonistic treatment. One among the three fold classification of treatment based on whether it is antagonist to both cause and disease. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: ubhayārthakāricikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dravyabhūtacikitsā (द्रव्यभूतचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.70): treatment using substances having physical form. Treatment using substances having physical form such as herbs, minerals, etc. (opposite of adravyabhūtacikitsā). Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: dravyabhūtacikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adravyabhūtacikitsā (अद्रव्यभूतचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.71): treatment using formless substances. Treatment without using substances having physical form such as upavāsa (fasting), mantra (incantations) etc. (opposite of dravyabhūtacikitsā). Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: adravyabhūtacikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: doṣopakramaḥ (दोषोपक्रमः; SAT SAT-I.72): therapeutic measure antagonistic to dośa. Therapeutic measures or set of therapies which are having characteristics or properties antagonistic to particular doṣa. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: doṣopakramaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kālapratīkṣā (कालप्रतीक्षा; SAT SAT-I.73): waiting for appropriate treatment time. Understanding the stage of the disease condition and waiting for appropriate time for treatment e.g. incision of an abscess only after it attains suppuration. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: kālapratīkṣā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁjñā-prabodhanam (संज्ञा-प्रबोधनम्; SAT SAT-I.74): regaining consciousness. Measures to bring back from the state of unconsciousness. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: saṁjñā-prabodhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: naiṣṭhikī-cikitsā (नैष्ठिकी-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.75): absolute treatment. The word naiṣṭhikīcikitsā is combination of two words niṣṭhā (definitive) and cikitsā (treatment), thus naiṣṭhikīcikitsā means definitive treatment or a permanent remedy to disease. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: naiṣṭhikī-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśodhana-karma (संशोधन-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.76): major purification therapy/ bio-cleansing therapy/ detoxification therapy. Treatment modality based on the principle of removal of vitiated doṣa (synonym of shodhanakarma). Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: saṁśodhana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pañcakarma (पञ्चकर्म; SAT SAT-I.77): five internal bio-cleansing therapies. Five fold therapeutic procedures; it includes the five therapeutic procedures of emesis, purgation, decoction enema, unctuous enema and errhine therapy. Category: major purification therapy/ bio-cleansing therapy/ detoxification therapy (saṁśodhana-karma).
title: pañcakarma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁśodhanārhaḥ (संशोधनार्हः; SAT SAT-I.78): person fit for cleansing procedures. Person who has no contra-indications for and hence is fit for undergoing bio-cleansing therapy. Category: five internal bio-cleansing therapies (pañcakarma).
title: saṁśodhanārhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pūrvakarma (पूर्वकर्म; SAT SAT-I.79): preparatory procedures. Preparatory procedures done for proper administration of any major procedure such as pañcakarma and śastra karma; in case of pañcakarma it comprises of dīpana, administration of snehana and svedana. Category: five internal bio-cleansing therapies (pañcakarma).
title: pūrvakarma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bāhyasnehaḥ (बाह्यस्नेहः; SAT SAT-I.80): external oleation. Lubrication of the body externally. Category: preparatory procedures (pūrvakarma).
title: bāhyasnehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bahiḥparimārjanam (बहिःपरिमार्जनम्; SAT SAT-I.81): external therapies. Therapeutic procedures involving application of medicines externally. Category: external oleation (bāhyasnehaḥ).
title: bahiḥparimārjanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abhyaṅgaḥ (अभ्यङ्गः; SAT SAT-I.82): therapeutic massage. Procedure to induce snehana done by external application of unctuous substance. Category: external oleation (bāhyasnehaḥ).
title: abhyaṅgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūrdhatailam (मूर्धतैलम्/ शिरस्तैलम्; SAT SAT-I.83): oil application over head. Also called śirastailam. Therapeutic procedure involving application of medicated oil over head, aimed to alleviating the diseases of head. Category: therapeutic massage (abhyaṅgaḥ).
title: mūrdhatailam śirastailam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śiraḥsekaḥ (शिरःसेकः; SAT SAT-I.84): therapeutic streaming over head. Type of mūrdhatailam in which the oil is made to fall in a fine stream over head (forehead) in a meticulous manner; pouring of oil over forehead is done either in pendulous movements or constant at one point. Category: oil application over head (mūrdhatailam).
title: śiraḥsekaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śiraḥpicuḥ (शिरःपिचुः; SAT SAT-I.85): therapeutic procedure of placing tampon with oil over head region. Type of mūrdhatailam in which a tampon prepared from either oil soaked cloth or cotton is kept over head. Category: oil application over head (mūrdhatailam).
title: śiraḥpicuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śirobastiḥ (शिरोबस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.86): therapeutic retention of oil over head region. Procedure involving holding of medicated oil over the head region for a specific duration. Category: oil application over head (mūrdhatailam).
title: śirobastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: Śiro-abhyaṅgaḥ (शिरोऽभ्यङ्गः; SAT SAT-I.87): therapeutic oil massage to head. Type of mūrdhatailam involving application of abhyaṅga to head region. Category: oil application over head (mūrdhatailam).
title: Śiro-abhyaṅgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāyasekaḥ (कायसेकः; SAT SAT-I.88): therapeutic streaming over body. Procedure in which oil or any medicated liquid is made to fall in a stream all over body. Category: therapeutic massage (abhyaṅgaḥ).
title: kāyasekaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tailadhārā (तैलधारा; SAT SAT-I.89): therapeutic oil-streaming over body. Procedure in which oil is made to fall in a stream (dhāra) all over body. Category: therapeutic massage (abhyaṅgaḥ).
title: tailadhārā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: takradhārā (तक्रधारा; SAT SAT-I.90): therapeutic butter milk -streaming over body. Procedure in which butter milk (takra) is made to fall in a stream (dhāra) all over body. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: takradhārā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṣāyadhārā (कषायधारा; SAT SAT-I.91): therapeutic medicated decoction-streaming over body. Procedure in which medicated decoction (kaṣāya) is made to fall in a stream (dhāra) all over body. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: kaṣāyadhārā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: manyābastiḥ (मन्याबस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.92): therapeutic retention of oil over cervical region. Procedure involving holding of medicated oil over the cervical region for a specific duration. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: manyābastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: hṛd-bastiḥ (हृद्-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.93): therapeutic retention of oil over cardiac region. Procedure involving holding of medicated oil over the cardiac region for a specific duration. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: hṛd-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pṛṣṭhabastiḥ (पृष्ठबस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.94): therapeutic retention of oil over thoraco-lumbar region. Procedure involving holding of medicated oil over the thoraco-lumbar region for a specific duration. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: pṛṣṭhabastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṭibastiḥ (कटिबस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.95): therapeutic retention of oil over lumbosacral region. Procedure involving holding of medicated oil over the lumbo-sacral region for a specific duration. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: kaṭibastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jānu-bastiḥ (जानु-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.96): therapeutic retention of oil over knee region. The procedure involving holding of medicated oil over the knee region for a specific duration. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: jānu-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁvāhanam (संवाहनम्; SAT SAT-I.97): soft massage. A procedure of massage with light pressure. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: saṁvāhanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mardanam (मर्दनम्; SAT SAT-I.98): massage with pressure. A procedure of therapeutic pressurised massage. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: mardanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udvartanam (उद्वर्तनम्; SAT SAT-I.99): therapeutic powder massage. Therapeutic massage using powders. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: udvartanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: utsādanam (उत्सादनम्; SAT SAT-I.100): therapeutic powder-oil mixture massage. Procedure characterized by rubbing of mixture prepared out of coarse powder and oil (or other unctuous liquid substances). Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: utsādanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udgharṣaṇam (उद्घर्षणम्; SAT SAT-I.101): therapeutic coarse powder massage. Procedure characterized by rubbing of coarse powder on the body in the reverse direction of the body hairs. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: udgharṣaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: unmardanam (उन्मर्दनम्; SAT SAT-I.102): manual massage in ascending direction. A type of therapeutic massage of the body parts wherein the gentle strokes are applied in the ascending direction by the palms of the masseur. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: unmardanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādāghātaḥ (पादाघातः; SAT SAT-I.103): therapeutic pedal massage. Therapeutic massage done using the feet using body weight as pressure. Category: external therapies (bahiḥparimārjanam).
title: pādāghātaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ābhyantarasnehaḥ (आभ्यन्तरस्नेहः; SAT SAT-I.104): internal oleation. Administration of appropriate dose of ghee, oil or any other unctuous substance internally for achieving oleation. Category: five internal bio-cleansing therapies (pañcakarma).
title: ābhyantarasnehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sadyasnehaḥ (सद्यस्नेहः; SAT SAT-I.105): quick oleation. Unctuous substance administered internally which induces quick oleation. Category: internal oleation (ābhyantarasnehaḥ).
title: sadyasnehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: acchasnehaḥ (अच्छस्नेहः; SAT SAT-I.106): administration of unctuous substance exclusively. Therapeutic procedure of administration of unctuous substance in pure form per oral (without mixing with any medicine or food or any other route). Category: internal oleation (ābhyantarasnehaḥ).
title: acchasnehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pravicāraṇāsnehaḥ (प्रविचारणास्नेहः/ विचारणास्नेहः; SAT SAT-I.107): co-administration of unctuous substance in various forms. Also called vicāraṇāsnehaḥ. Methods of inducing oleation by administering various unctuous substances along with food or medicine or from other par-enteral route. Category: internal oleation (ābhyantarasnehaḥ).
title: pravicāraṇāsnehaḥ vicāraṇāsnehaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svedanam (स्वेदनम्; SAT SAT-I.108): sudation therapy. Therapeutic procedure for inducing diaphoresis. Category: preparatory procedures (pūrvakarma).
title: svedanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: agnisvedaḥ (अग्निस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.109): sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire. Sudation therapy which induce diaphoresis by mean of heat directly or indirectly from fire. Category: sudation therapy (svedanam).
title: agnisvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṅkarasvedaḥ (सङ्करस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.110): sudation by medicated bolus. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by external application of prewarmed medicine in the form of bolus with or without covering cloth. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: saṅkarasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prastarasvedaḥ (प्रस्तरस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.111): sudation by lying on bed. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by making the person lay down on bed with pre-warmed medicine spread over it. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: prastarasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nāḍīsvedaḥ (नाडीस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.112): sudation using pipe like instrument. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by steam from a tube like instrument. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: nāḍīsvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pariṣekasvedaḥ (परिषेकस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.113): sudation by streaming of pre-warmed liquid. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by sprinkling of pre warmed liquid. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: pariṣekasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avagāhasvedaḥ (अवगाहस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.114): sudation by sitting in tub. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by sitting in a tub filled with pre warmed liquid. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: avagāhasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jentākasvedaḥ (जेन्ताकस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.115): sudation done in a particular chamber. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by making a person sit in specially designed chamber with heating arrangement inside it for desired period of time. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: jentākasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aśmaghanasvedaḥ (अश्मघनस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.116): sudation on stone bed. Type of agnisvedaḥ in which sudation is done by making the person lay down on pre-warmed stone bed. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: aśmaghanasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karṣūsvedaḥ (कर्षूस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.117): sudation by a pit filled with ember of desired substances. A type of agni svedaḥ in which sudation is done by making the person lay down or sit over a bed placed above a pit filled with ember of desired substances. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: karṣūsvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kuṭīsvedaḥ (कुटीस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.118): sudation done in cottage. A type of agni svedaḥ in which sudation is done by making a person sit in specially designed cottage with source of heat placed outside the cottage. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: kuṭīsvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhūsvedaḥ (भूस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.119): sudation on warm earth surface. A type of agni svedaḥ in which sudation is done by making the person lay down on pre-warmed earth which is devoid of breeze. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: bhūsvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kumbhīsvedaḥ (कुम्भीस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.120): sudation with buried pot filled with decoctions. A type of agni svedaḥ in which sudation is done by making the person lay down or sit over a bed placed above a buried pot filled with hot decoction or liquid. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: kumbhīsvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kūpasvedaḥ (कूपस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.121): sudation from a well. A type of agni svedaḥ in which sudation is done by making the person lay down or sit over a bed placed above a shallow well containing ember of various substances filled in it. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: kūpasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: holākasvedaḥ (होलाकस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.122): sudation induced by burning substances in a specially made pot. A type of agni svedaḥ in which sudation is done by making a person lay down or sit over a bed placed above specially designed pot which generate heat from for burning of dry substance like gomaya (cowdung). Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: holākasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: piṇḍasvedaḥ (पिण्डस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.123): sudation by application of poultice. Sudation with application of a bolus prepared with medicated substances. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: piṇḍasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upanāhasvedaḥ (sāgniḥ) (उपनाहस्वेदः (साग्निः); SAT SAT-I.124): sudation by application of medicated herbal paste or powders. Sudation with application of paste which is pre-warmed as in saṅkarasvedaḥ. Category: sudation by direct or indirect contact with fire (agnisvedaḥ).
title: upanāhasvedaḥ (sāgniḥ)

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: niragnisvedaḥ (निरग्निस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.125): sudation without involving fire. Sudation procedures which do not use any direct or indirect use of fire. Category: sudation therapy (svedanam).
title: niragnisvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāyāmaḥ (व्यायामः; SAT SAT-I.126): sudation by exercise. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by exercise. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: vyāyāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uṣṇasadanam (उष्णसदनम्; SAT SAT-I.127): sudation by sitting in a warm room. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by sitting in a warm room. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: uṣṇasadanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: guruprāvaraṇam (गुरुप्रावरणम्; SAT SAT-I.128): sudation by wearing heavy clothes. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by warm heavy clothes. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: guruprāvaraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣudhā (क्षुधा; SAT SAT-I.129): sudation by hunger. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by keeping a person hungry. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: kṣudhā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bahupānam (बहुपानम्; SAT SAT-I.130): sudation by drinking of lot of alcohol. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by drinking of lot of alcohol. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: bahupānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhayaḥ (भयः; SAT SAT-I.131): sudation by fear. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by frightening the person. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: bhayaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: krodhaḥ (क्रोधः; SAT SAT-I.132): sudation by anger. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by making a person angry. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: krodhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upanāhaḥ (niragniḥ) (उपनाहः (निरग्निः); SAT SAT-I.133): sudation by application of medicated herbal paste or powders. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation with application of paste to induce sudation by blocking body heat to escape. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: upanāhaḥ (niragniḥ)

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhavaḥ (आहवः/युध्दः; SAT SAT-I.134): sudation by fighting. Also called yudhdaḥ. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by fight. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: āhavaḥ yudhdaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ātapaḥ (आतपः; SAT SAT-I.135): sudation by exposure to sun. Type of niragnisvedaḥ in which sudation is induced by exposing a person to sun. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: ātapaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tāpasvedaḥ (तापस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.136): sudation by contact of warm substance. Procedure of inducing sudation by applying a warm substance on the surface. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: tāpasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dravasvedaḥ (द्रवस्वेदः; SAT SAT-I.137): sudation by warm liquid. Procedure of inducing sudation by applying a warm liquid. Category: sudation without involving fire (niragnisvedaḥ).
title: dravasvedaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pradhāna-karma (प्रधान-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.138): main therapeutic procedures. Main procedures; usually used in the context of pañcakarma and śastrakarma. Category: five internal bio-cleansing therapies (pañcakarma).
title: pradhāna-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vamana-karma (वमन-कर्म/ प्रच्छर्दनम्; SAT SAT-I.139): therapeutic emesis. Also called pracchardanam. Therapeutic process for controlled induction of vomiting along with a series of pre and post operative measures. Category: main therapeutic procedures (pradhāna-karma).
title: vamana-karma pracchardanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: virecana-karma (विरेचन-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.140): therapeutic purgation. Therapeutic process for controlled induction of purgation along with a series of pre and post operative measures. Category: main therapeutic procedures (pradhāna-karma).
title: virecana-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: basti-karma (बस्ति-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.141): therapeutic enema. Therapeutic procedure of giving medication per rectum through specially designed bastiḥ instrument. Category: main therapeutic procedures (pradhāna-karma).
title: basti-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: anuvāsana-bastiḥ (अनुवासन-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.142): therapeutic unctuous enema. A form of medicated unctuous enema; the dose of which is half of that of snehabastiḥ. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: anuvāsana-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sneha-bastiḥ (स्नेह-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.143): therapeutic unctuous enema. Medicated unctous enema usually given in quantity one fourth of that of decoction enema. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: sneha-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mātrābastiḥ (मात्राबस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.144): a form of unctuous enema. Medicated enema given in such a dose which will show no complications even if retained or post therapy regimen are not followed. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: mātrābastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āsthāpana-bastiḥ (आस्थापन-बस्तिः/ निरूह-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.145): therapeutic decoction enema. Also called nirūha-bastiḥ. Therapeutic procedure of giving medication with a mixture predominantly containing decoction by enema. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: āsthāpana-bastiḥ nirūha-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yāpana-bastiḥ (यापन-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.146): enema which prolongs the life span. Form of therapeutic enema which is used for maintenance of health to prolong life span. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: yāpana-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yuktaratha-bastiḥ (युक्तरथ-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.147): enema which can be administered even during travelling. Therapeutic enema that can be administered without major safety concerns and do not bind patients to take bed rest. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: yuktaratha-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mādhutailikabastiḥ (माधुतैलिकबस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.148): enema prepared from honey and oil. Medicated enema constituting mainly of honey and oil. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: mādhutailikabastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vaitaraṇa-bastiḥ (वैतरण-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.149): special type of enema with revival property. The term literally means revival, and the basti having such potency is called as vaitaraṇa-bastiḥ. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: vaitaraṇa-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: picchā (पिच्छा/पिच्छिल-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.150): slimy enema. Also called picchila-bastiḥ. Basti having slimy / unctous consistency is called as picchābasti. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: picchā picchila-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: siddha-bastiḥ (सिद्ध-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.151): enema, which improves strength, complexion and growth. The special medicated enema which cure certain diseases and provide longevity. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: siddha-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karma-bastiḥ (कर्म-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.152): course of thirty therapeutic enema. Form of therapeutic enema wherein a course of thirty enema which includes eighteen anuvāsana-basti and twelve nirūha- basti are administered in a particular sequence. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: karma-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kāla-bastiḥ (काल-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.153): course of sixteen therapeutic enema. Form of therapeutic enema wherein a course of sixteen enema which includes ten anuvāsana-basti and six nirūha- basti are administered in a particular sequence. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: kāla-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: yoga-bastiḥ (योग-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.154): Course of eight therapeutic enemas. A form of therapeutic enema wherein a course of eight enema which includes five anuvāsana-basti and three nirūha- basti are administered in a particular sequence. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: yoga-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uttara-bastiḥ (उत्तर-बस्तिः; SAT SAT-I.155): basti administered through vaginal or urethral route. Procedure in which medicated oil/ghee/decoction is administered through vaginal or urethral route. Category: therapeutic enema (basti-karma).
title: uttara-bastiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nasyam (नस्यम्/ नस्तम्; SAT SAT-I.156): medication through nasal route. Also called nastam. Procedure in which the medicine either in liquid form or in powder form is administered through the nose. Category: main therapeutic procedures (pradhāna-karma).
title: nasyam nastam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nāvanam (नावनम्; SAT SAT-I.157): medication of unctuous substance through nose. Type of nasyam in which the drops of medicated unctuous substance are used for nasyam. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: nāvanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śirovirecanam (शिरोविरेचनम्; SAT SAT-I.158): medication through nose for cleansing or errhine. Literally means cleaning of the head; a kind of nasyam therapy which eliminates the morbid factors out of the head region. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: śirovirecanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: marśaḥ (मर्शः; SAT SAT-I.159): high dose medication through nasal route. Kind of nasya therapy in which medicines mainly having the oil base is instilled in the nose in a comparatively higher dose. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: marśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pratimarśaḥ (प्रतिमर्शः; SAT SAT-I.160): low dose medication through nasal route. Kind of nasya therapy in which medicines mainly having the oil base is instilled in the nose in a lower dose. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: pratimarśaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avapīḍanam (अवपीडनम्; SAT SAT-I.161): nasya therapy by expressed juice from paste. Therapeutic instillation of juice expressed from kalka (paste) of a drug into nostril. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: avapīḍanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pradhamanam (प्रधमनम्/ ध्मापनम्; SAT SAT-I.162): nasya therapy by medicated powder insufflation. Also called dhmāpanam. Nasya in which medicated powder is puffed into the nostrils. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: pradhamanam dhmāpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhūmanasyam (धूमनस्यम्; SAT SAT-I.163): nasyam therapy using medicated smoke. Nasya in which medicated smoke is puffed up into the nostrils. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: dhūmanasyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: recananasyam (रेचननस्यम्; SAT SAT-I.164): cleansing type of nasya therapy. Nasya therapy which eliminates the morbid factors out of the head region. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: recananasyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bṛṁhaṇanasyam (बृंहणनस्यम्; SAT SAT-I.165): nourishing nasya therapy. Nasya therapy with primary aim of nourishment. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: bṛṁhaṇanasyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śamananasyam (शमननस्यम्; SAT SAT-I.166): nasyam therapy having pacifying effect. Nasya therapy which help in treatment by pacifying the morbid dośa. Category: medication through nasal route (nasyam).
title: śamananasyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śuddhiḥ (शुद्धिः; SAT SAT-I.167): cleansing. The term signifies internal and external purifications. Category: main therapeutic procedures (pradhāna-karma).
title: śuddhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: uttama-śuddhiḥ (उत्तम-शुद्धिः; SAT SAT-I.168): adequete cleansing. Achievement of the adequate degree of evacuation of doṣa during śodhana. Category: cleansing (śuddhiḥ).
title: uttama-śuddhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: madhyama-śuddhiḥ (मध्यम-शुद्धिः; SAT SAT-I.169): moderate cleansing. Achievement of the moderate degree of evacuation of doṣa during śodhana. Category: cleansing (śuddhiḥ).
title: madhyama-śuddhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: avara (अवर/हीन-शुद्धिः; SAT SAT-I.170): mild/less cleansing. Also called hīna-śuddhiḥ. Achievement of the mild/less degree of evacuation of doṣa during śodhana. Category: cleansing (śuddhiḥ).
title: avara hīna-śuddhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: paścāt-karma (पश्चात्-कर्म; SAT SAT-I.171): post -therapy procedures. Procedures which are adviced after major therapeutic procedure in order to make person return to normalcy. Category: five internal bio-cleansing therapies (pañcakarma).
title: paścāt-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁsarjana-kramaḥ (संसर्जन-क्रमः; SAT SAT-I.172): post therapy dietetic regimen for revival. Dietary regimn for restoration of agni after shodhana. Category: post -therapy procedures (paścāt-karma).
title: saṁsarjana-kramaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parihāra-kālaḥ (परिहार-कालः; SAT SAT-I.173): period of therapeutic restrictions. Definite period in which certain regimens are required e.g. after pañcakarma procedures some regimens are required to bring back the body constituents in normalcy. Category: post -therapy procedures (paścāt-karma).
title: parihāra-kālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: daivī-cikitsā (दैवी-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.174): divine therapy. One among four categories of medicines described in atharvaveda. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: daivī-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āṅgirasī (आङ्गिरसी; SAT SAT-I.175): treatments relating to sage Aṅgiras. One among four categories of medicines described in atharvaveda. Category: divine therapy (daivī-cikitsā).
title: āṅgirasī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ātharvaṇī (आथर्वणी; SAT SAT-I.176): treatments relating to sage Atharvan. One among four categories of medicines described in atharvaveda. Category: divine therapy (daivī-cikitsā).
title: ātharvaṇī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mānuṣī-cikitsā (मानुषी-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.177): humane therapy. One among four categories of medicines described in atharvaveda. Category: divine therapy (daivī-cikitsā).
title: mānuṣī-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: satvāvajaya-cikitsā (सत्वावजय-चिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.178): subjugation of mind/ counselling. The treatment done by psychotherapy and counseling by which the mind is made to restrain itself from wrong preoccupations. Category: disease management/ treatment (cikitsā).
title: satvāvajaya-cikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ahitebhyo-arthebhyo manonigraha (अहितेभ्योऽर्थेभ्यो मनोनिग्रह; SAT SAT-I.179): restricting the mind from desire for unwholesomeness. The main focus of satvāvajaya-cikitsā regarding restraining oneself from unwholesomeness. Category: subjugation of mind/ counselling (satvāvajaya-cikitsā).
title: ahitebhyo-arthebhyo manonigraha

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kumāratantram (कुमारतन्त्रम्/ कौमारभृत्यम्/ बाल-तन्त्रम्/ बालचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.180): pediatrics. Also called kaumārabhṛtyam, bāla-tantram and bālacikitsā. One among the eight branches of āyurveda which deals with neonatal, child care and maternal ante natal and post natal care and certain aspects of obstetrics.
title: kumāratantram kaumārabhṛtyam bāla-tantram bālacikitsā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kumārāgāram (कुमारागारम्; SAT SAT-I.181): child abode / nursery. A specially constructed abode in accord to seasonal comfort, for the child equipped with well-defined division for the water source, urinal, lavatory, bathroom, kitchen etc. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: kumārāgāram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhātrī (धात्री; SAT SAT-I.182): wet nurse. A lady who is feeding a child is called as dhātri, she may be the child’s mother or an appointed lady for that work. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: dhātrī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bālaḥ (बालः; SAT SAT-I.183): child. The term signifies child up to the age of one year or up to 16 years used in different context. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: bālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śiśuḥ (शिशुः; SAT SAT-I.184): baby. This term is used for the baby who spent most of the time in sleeping, term generally used upto 1 year of age. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: śiśuḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kṣīrādaḥ (क्षीरादः/ दुग्धाशी; SAT SAT-I.185): child dependant on breastmilk alone. Also called dugdhāśī. A child dependent on milk. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: kṣīrādaḥ dugdhāśī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dugdhānnāśī (दुग्धान्नाशी/ क्षीरान्नादः; SAT SAT-I.186): child on a diet of both breastmilk and solid food. Also called kṣīrānnādaḥ. Child who is consuming milk and food (anna). Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: dugdhānnāśī kṣīrānnādaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: annādaḥ (अन्नादः/ अन्नाशी; SAT SAT-I.187): child who takes normal diet. Also called annāśī. Child who start taking normal food. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: annādaḥ annāśī

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kumāraḥ (कुमारः; SAT SAT-I.188): child. Routinely used for child between the ages one to sixteen years and signifies immaturity of dhatu. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: kumāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sadyojātaḥ (सद्योजातः/ जातमात्रः; SAT SAT-I.189): just born baby. Also called jātamātraḥ. Neonate soon after birth. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: sadyojātaḥ jātamātraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: navajātaḥ (नवजातः; SAT SAT-I.190): neonate. Neonatal age. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: navajātaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sadyojāta-śiśu-paricaryā (सद्योजात-शिशु-परिचर्या; SAT SAT-I.191): management of the newborn. Various procedures done for the baby soon after birth. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: sadyojāta-śiśu-paricaryā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prāṇapratyāgamanam (प्राणप्रत्यागमनम्; SAT SAT-I.192): resuscitation. Measures to revive the baby soon after birth. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: prāṇapratyāgamanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: aśmanoḥ saṁghaṭaṭnaṁ karṇayormūle (अश्मनोः संघटट्नं कर्णयोर्मूले; SAT SAT-I.193): making noice by hitting of stones near ear. One among the steps in neonatal resusication where sound stimulus is provided by the sound produced by hitting of stones together near the ears of baby. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: aśmanoḥ saṁghaṭaṭnaṁ karṇayormūle

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śītodaka (शीतोदक/उष्णोदक मुखपरिषेकः; SAT SAT-I.194): sprinkling of face with cold or luke warm water. Also called uṣṇodaka mukhapariṣekaḥ. One among the steps in neonatal resusication where tactile sensation is stimulated by sprinkling of luke warm or cold water as per season. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: śītodaka uṣṇodaka mukhapariṣekaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kr̥̄ṣṇakapālikaśūrpeṇa abhiniṣpuṇanam (कृष्णकपालिकशूर्पेण अभिनिष्पुणनम्; SAT SAT-I.195): fanning by winnowing baskets made of black potsherd. One among the steps in care of newborn. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: kr̥̄ṣṇakapālikaśūrpeṇa abhiniṣpuṇanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: oṣṭha-kaṇṭha-jihvā-pramārjanam (ओष्ठ-कण्ठ-जिह्वा-प्रमार्जनम्; SAT SAT-I.196): clearing of lips, buccal cavity and throat. One among the steps in neonatal resusication where the lips, mouth and throat of the baby is cleared of mucous. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: oṣṭha-kaṇṭha-jihvā-pramārjanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhikalpana-vidhiḥ (नाभिकल्पन-विधिः; SAT SAT-I.197): techinque of cutting of umbilical cord. Standardized techinque for cutting of umbilical cord. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: nābhikalpana-vidhiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jātakarma (जातकर्म; SAT SAT-I.198): birth - rites of the newborn. Various birth rites done for a new born baby. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: jātakarma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rakṣākarma (रक्षाकर्म; SAT SAT-I.199): protective measures for the newborn. The different measures adopted to ensure the protection of new born. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: rakṣākarma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nābhināla-pātanam (नाभिनाल-पतनम्; SAT SAT-I.200): falling of umbilical cord. Falling of residual umbilical cord after 5th day or so. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: nābhināla-pātanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bāla-saṁskāraḥ (बाल-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.201): ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child. Ceremonies performed at various stages life of a child indicative of the major milestones of life. Category: pediatrics (kumāratantram).
title: bāla-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: jātakarma-saṁskāraḥ (जातकर्म-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.202): birth ceremony. One of the rituals performed just after birth, for the purpose of promotion of intellect, longevity and strength or for gut priming. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: jātakarma-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nāmakaraṇa-saṁskāraḥ (नामकरण-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.203): naming ceremony. Naming ceremony usually done after 10th day or so. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: nāmakaraṇa-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dolāśayana-saṁskāraḥ (दोलाशयन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.204): cradle ceremony. Ceremony in which child is made to lie down in a cradle for the first time. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: dolāśayana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sūryacandradarśana-saṁskāraḥ (सूर्यचन्द्रदर्शन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.205): showing of sun and moon to the child. Ceremony in which the child is exposed to the sun and moon for the first time. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: sūryacandradarśana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: niṣkrāmaṇa-saṁskāraḥ (निष्क्रामण-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.206): outing ceremony. Ritual performed in 4th month, wherein the child is taken out, first time, from the kumārāgāra (child care room). Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: niṣkrāmaṇa-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upaveśana-saṁskāraḥ (उपवेशन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.207): seating ceremony. Ritual wherein the sitting is initiated and usually done at 5th or 6th month of age. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: upaveśana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: phalaprāśana-saṁskāraḥ (फलप्राशन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.208): fruit feeding ceremony. Stage before annaprashana where the child is initiated with fruit diet before cereal based diet. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: phalaprāśana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karṇavedhana-saṁskāraḥ (कर्णवेधन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.209): ear piercing ceremony. Ritual performed in infantile period wherein the earlobes are pierced with needle. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: karṇavedhana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: annaprāśana-saṁskāraḥ (अन्नप्राशन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.210): weaning ceremony. Ritual performed in infants between six to tenth month, wherein first intake of the semisolid food is for the. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: annaprāśana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: cūḍākaraṇa-saṁskāraḥ (चूडाकरण-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.211): tonsuring ceremony. Ritual performed in the child, wherein the scalp hairs are totally shaved off, first time. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: cūḍākaraṇa-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: akṣaralekhana-saṁskāraḥ (अक्षरलेखन-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.212): writing ceremony. Ritual of making the child to write the various syllables signifying the initiation of formal education. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: akṣaralekhana-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vivāha-saṁskāraḥ (विवाह-संस्कारः; SAT SAT-I.213): marriage ceremony. Ceremony indicating beginning of family life. Category: ceremonies performed at various stages of life of the child (bāla-saṁskāraḥ).
title: vivāha-saṁskāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: dantajanmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: caturvidha-dantajanma (चतुर्विध-दन्तजन्म; SAT SAT-I.215): four types of tooth eruption. Signifying four different types of tooth eruption. Category: tooth eruption (dantajanmaḥ).
title: caturvidha-dantajanma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sāmudgaḥ (सामुद्गः; SAT SAT-I.216): dentition with early falling of teeth. An abnormal type of dentition characterised early or frequent fall. Category: tooth eruption (dantajanmaḥ).
title: sāmudgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: saṁvṛtaḥ (संवृतः; SAT SAT-I.217): type of dentition which remain dirty. An abnormal type of dentition characterised by dirty teeths. Category: tooth eruption (dantajanmaḥ).
title: saṁvṛtaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vivṛtaḥ (विवृतः; SAT SAT-I.218): type of dentition not fully covered with lips. An abnormal type of dentition characterised by excessive salivation, because these are not fully covered with lips. Category: tooth eruption (dantajanmaḥ).
title: vivṛtaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dantasampat (दन्तसम्पत्; SAT SAT-I.219): proper dentition. Proper teeth having all the characteristics of healthy teeth. Category: tooth eruption (dantajanmaḥ).
title: dantasampat

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śālākyatantram (शालाक्यतन्त्रम्/ उर्ध्वाङ्गचिकित्सा/ जत्रूर्ध्वचिकित्सा/ उत्तमाङ्गचिकित्सा; SAT SAT-I.228): branch of āyurveda dealing with disease occurring in head and neck region. Also called urdhvāṅgacikitsā, jatrūrdhvacikitsā and uttamāṅgacikitsā. One among the eight branches of āyurveda which deals with the diseases affecting the supra-clavicular region i.e. eye, ear, nose, throat, oral cavity, dentistry and various types of headaches including diseases affecting the scalp and their management (i.e. includes ophthalmology, orodentistry, ENT, and various types of scalp related conditions and generalized head related conditions such as migrain etc.).
title: śālākyatantram urdhvāṅgacikitsā jatrūrdhvacikitsā uttamāṅgacikitsā

text: śālākin (शालाकिन्/ शलाकि; SAT SAT-I.229): one who is specialized in śālākyatantra. Also called śalāki. A person who has expertise and practices śālākyatantram. Category: branch of āyurveda dealing with disease occurring in head and neck region (śālākyatantram).
title: śālākin śalāki

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: utpalabhedakaḥ (उत्पलभेदकः; SAT SAT-I.272): type of lobuloplasty. Lobuloplasty indicated when both flaps of the divided ear lobe are circular, wide and equal. Category: fifteen shapes/ methods of lobuloplasty (pañcadaśakarṇabandhākṛti).
