title: nāvanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gaṇḍūṣaḥ (गण्डूषः; SAT SAT-J.16): liquid or oil pulling/ holding of any liquid in mouth. Filling the mouth completely with any liquid such as oil, ghee, honey etc. and holding them without movement which provides strength to jaws and voice. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: gaṇḍūṣaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhūmasevanam (धूमसेवनम्; SAT SAT-J.17): inhalation of smoke. Administration of mild and soothing smoke for preventing the diseases caused due to kapha and vāta above the clavicle. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: dhūmasevanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tāmbūlasevanam (ताम्बूलसेवनम्; SAT SAT-J.18): chewing of betel. Chewing of betal leaf along with nutmeg, clove, arecanut etc which imparts good taste, cleanliness and fragrance of mouth. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: tāmbūlasevanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mūrdhnitailam (मूर्ध्नितैलम्; SAT SAT-J.19): oil application to head. Applying of various oils on the head which prevents graying of hair and also gives strength to the sense organs. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: mūrdhnitailam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: karṇatarpaṇam (कर्णतर्पणम्; SAT SAT-J.20): oil application to ears. Applying oil to the ear which prevents diseases of ear such as deafness etc. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: karṇatarpaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: abhyaṅgaḥ (अभ्यङ्गः; SAT SAT-J.21): oil application to the whole body. Application of oil to the whole body along with gentle massage. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: abhyaṅgaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāyāmaḥ (व्यायामः; SAT SAT-J.22): exercise. Movement of the body which produces lightness in the body, increase capacity to work and improves appetite and decrease body fat. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: vyāyāmaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyāyāma-śaktiḥ (व्यायाम-शक्तिः; SAT SAT-J.23): power of exercise. Stamina of the individual for doing exercise. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: vyāyāma-śaktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: udvartanam (उद्वर्तनम्; SAT SAT-J.24): whole body massage with soft powders. Gentle rubbing of the body with soft powders which reduces kapha and medas. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: udvartanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: snānam (स्नानम्; SAT SAT-J.25): taking bath. Taking bath enhances virility, longevity, strength and compactness of the body and also removes tiredness, sweat and impurities from the body. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: snānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mṛjāvarjanam (मृजावर्जनम्; SAT SAT-J.26): abstinence from cleanliness. One among the causative factors for many diseases. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: mṛjāvarjanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nirmalāmbaradhāraṇam (निर्मलाम्बरधारणम्; SAT SAT-J.27): wearing of clean cloths. It enhance the charm, fame, life and produces pleasure. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: nirmalāmbaradhāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: kaṣāya-vastram (कषाय-वस्त्रम्; SAT SAT-J.28): saffron (yellowish red) colored cloths. This kind of clothes has qualities like cold, it decreases heat and pitta dosa. It is best suited in summer season, also used by saint’s priests during ritual acts, yoga etc. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: kaṣāya-vastram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: malina-vastram (मलिन-वस्त्रम्; SAT SAT-J.29): wearing of dirty clothes. Wearing of these clothes is considered inauspicious & causes itching & other skin disorders. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: malina-vastram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: gandhaniṣevaṇam (गन्धनिषेवणम्; SAT SAT-J.30): use of fragrance. It is aphrodisiac and destroys inauspiciousness. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: gandhaniṣevaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mālyaniṣevaṇam (माल्यनिषेवणम्; SAT SAT-J.31): use of garlands. It produces good smell and calmness of mind. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: mālyaniṣevaṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ābharaṇadhāraṇam (आभरणधारणम्; SAT SAT-J.33): wearing of ornaments. It produces happiness, charm, ojas and prevents calamities. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: ābharaṇadhāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādayormalamārgāṇām abhīkṣṇaśaḥ śaucādhānam (पादयोर्मलमार्गाणाम् अभीक्ष्णशः शौचाधानम्; SAT SAT-J.34): frequent cleaning of feet and excretory orifices. It promotes intelligence, purity and longevity. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: pādayormalamārgāṇām abhīkṣṇaśaḥ śaucādhānam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: keśakalpanam (केशकल्पनम्; SAT SAT-J.35): cutting of hair. It provides cleanliness and beautification. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: keśakalpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: śmaśrukalpanam (श्मश्रुकल्पनम्; SAT SAT-J.36): proper cutting of beard and mustache. It is aphrodisiac, life promoter and provides cleanliness. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: śmaśrukalpanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: keśaprasādanam (केशप्रसादनम्; SAT SAT-J.37): combing of hairs. It is one among the daily regimen. combing is good for hairs; it removes dust, louse and dirt. maintains hygiene of head. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: keśaprasādanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādatra-dhāraṇam (पादत्र-धारणम्; SAT SAT-J.38): wearing of foot wares. It alleviates diseases of feet, promotes semen, ward off evil organisms, gives pleasure and comfort in moving and is wholesome for ojas. it prevents from abrasions of thorn, stone, gravels, dust etc. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: pādatra-dhāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: chatradhāraṇam (छत्रधारणम्; SAT SAT-J.39): holding of umbrella. It prevents from rain, wind, dust, snow etc. and wholesome for complexion, vision and ojas and has overall salutary effect. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: chatradhāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: daṇḍa-dhāraṇam (दण्ड-धारणम्; SAT SAT-J.40): holding of stick. It removes fear of dog, reptiles, ferocious beasts and horned animals. protects from falling, slipping and other defects. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: daṇḍa-dhāraṇam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vṛtti-upāyaḥ (वृत्ति-उपायः; SAT SAT-J.41): adopting of livelihood. One should make efforts to achieve means of livelihood such as- agriculture, animal husbandry, trade and commerce, government services etc. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: vṛtti-upāyaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology

title: adhyayanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: agnihotram (अग्निहोत्रम्; SAT SAT-J.44): daily ritual oblation put into the fire. Vedic ritual in which an oblation is offered particularly to agni, the god of fire. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: agnihotram

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ādhyātmika-karma (आध्यात्मिक-कर्म; SAT SAT-J.45): different spiritual practices. Various practices for spiritual upliftment such as prayer, offerings etc. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: ādhyātmika-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: tapaḥ (तपः; SAT SAT-J.46): penance. Undergoing of religious austerities, the practice of self denial and of meditation and mental concentration helpful to self-denial. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: tapaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: upavāsaḥ (उपवासः; SAT SAT-J.47): fasting. Willing abstinence or reduction from all food, thoughts etc for a period of time. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: upavāsaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sadvṛttam (सद्वृत्तम्; SAT SAT-J.48): good conduct/behavior. Right, good or moral conducts which are followed to lead healthy life. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: sadvṛttam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: prajñāparādhaḥ (प्रज्ञापराधः; SAT SAT-J.49): intellectual blasphemy. It is made out of two words pragya and aparadha. pragya refers to knowledge/intellect. aparadha means offence/ transgression/ fault. volitional transgression; erroneous deeds done on account of the impairment of intellect, wisdom and memory. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: prajñāparādhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: ācāra-rasāyanam (आचार-रसायनम्; SAT SAT-J.50): behavioural rasāyana. Customary law, codes, conducts and behavior which prevents the psychosomatic ailments. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: ācāra-rasāyanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: laukika-karma (लौकिक-कर्म; SAT SAT-J.51): worldly actions. Worldly activities such as sitting, standing, sleeping, running, throwing etc. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: laukika-karma

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rātricaryā (रात्रिचर्या; SAT SAT-J.52): night regimen. Regimens to be followed in the night. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: rātricaryā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: svapnam (स्वप्नम्; SAT SAT-J.53): dreams. Dream is known as of seven types such as - based on visual experience, auditory experience, personal experience, strong desire, imagination, future consequences and due to vitiation of doṣa. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: svapnam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vivāhaḥ (विवाहः; SAT SAT-J.54): marriage. It is one of the sixteen sanskaras (sacraments) of life. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: vivāhaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vyavāyaḥ (व्यवायः/ मैथुनम्; SAT SAT-J.55): sexual intercourse/ sexual regimen. Also called maithunam. Indulgence in sexual intercourse according to season and strength of person. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: vyavāyaḥ maithunam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dhāraṇīyavegaḥ (धारणीयवेगः; SAT SAT-J.56): suppressible urges. Urges which should be suppressed such as greed, grief, fear, anger, ego, shamelessness, jealousy, excessive attachment, desire for things possessed by others, speaking harsh words, back biting, lying, desire for other women and stealing. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: dhāraṇīyavegaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: adhāraṇīyavegaḥ (अधारणीयवेगः; SAT SAT-J.57): non- suppressible urges. Natural urges which should not be suppressed viz. urge of flatus, feces, urine, yawning, tears, eructation, vomiting, semen, hunger, thirst, dyspnoea and sleep. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: adhāraṇīyavegaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: vihāraḥ (विहारः; SAT SAT-J.58): life style. According to season, constitution, diseases etc life styles described in ayurveda. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: vihāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pravāta-sevanam (प्रवात-सेवनम्; SAT SAT-J.59): strong winds. It increases dryness and lightness. contraindicated in hemanta ṛtu (early winter). Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: pravāta-sevanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhārarasa-pākaḥ (आहाररस-पाकः; SAT SAT-J.60): complete digestion of ingested food. It is a stage indicating completion of the process of digestion. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: āhārarasa-pākaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: viṣamāśanam (विषमाशनम्; SAT SAT-J.61): unequal proportion. Consuming less or more quantity of food at improper time. due to this body will not be nourished properly and over a period of time it may lead to many disorders. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: viṣamāśanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhāravidhiviśeṣāyatanam (आहारविधिविशेषायतनम्; SAT SAT-J.62): basic factors to be considered while preparing and consuming diet. Eight in number viz: prakṛti (nature of article), karaṇa (processing), samyoga (combination), rāśi (amount), deśa (region), kāla (season and age), upayoga saṃsthā (rules for consumption) and upayoktā (consumer). Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: āhāravidhiviśeṣāyatanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhārapariṇāmakara-bhāvaḥ (आहारपरिणामकर-भावः; SAT SAT-J.63): factors responsible for proper digestion. It includes six factors- heat (ūṣmā) digests, vāyu absorbs, moisture (kleda) loosens, unctuousness (sneha) softens, time ( kāla) brings sufficiency & balanced use of all these (samayoga) which brings about proper digestion. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: āhārapariṇāmakara-bhāvaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhāramātrā (आहारमात्रा; SAT SAT-J.64): optimal digestible quantity of food optimal digestible quantity of food optimal digestible quantity of food optimal digestible quantity of food. Optimal digestible quantity of food which differs from person to person and time to time based on the digestive capacity and psychological statusoptimal digestible quantity of food which differs from person to person and time to time based on the digestive capacity and psychological statusoptimal digestible quantity of food which differs from person to person and time to time based on the digestive capacity and psychological statusoptimal digestible quantity of. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: āhāramātrā

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhāraśaktiḥ (आहारशक्तिः; SAT SAT-J.65): capacity of food intake. This is known by the quantity of food intake as well as power of digestion. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: āhāraśaktiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: āhārasampat (आहारसम्पत्; SAT SAT-J.66): excellence of diet. Food with all required nutrition in an adequate quantity which helps in preservation and promotion of health, gives strength, vitality, endurance and improves immunity. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: āhārasampat

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: dvikāla-bhojanam (द्विकाल-भोजनम्; SAT SAT-J.67): twice a day meal. Having meal twice a day is good for those having normal agni. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: dvikāla-bhojanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: parigrahaḥ (परिग्रहः; SAT SAT-J.68): accounting of the individual particular food article. It indicates the individual amount of food articles in the meal plate. it is contrast to sarvagraha. here it refers to the caloric value of individual food articles in the meal plate. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: parigrahaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: pādāṁśika-kramaḥ (पादांशिक-क्रमः; SAT SAT-J.69): alienation and adoption in quarter portion. Unwholesome food practices are to be tapered in quarter / quarter of quarters, and are substituted by pathyahara (wholesome food practice) in interval of one, two or three meal time according to condition. substitution is to be augmented in gradual, phased manner. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: pādāṁśika-kramaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: praśasta-āhārakālaḥ (प्रशस्त-आहारकालः; SAT SAT-J.70): best time part for taking food. One should eat when previous meal digested. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: praśasta-āhārakālaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: bhaktam (भक्तम्; SAT SAT-J.71): food or drinks consumed by the individual. Food taken in various forms- eaten(ashit), drunk (pita), licked (lidha) and devoured (khadita)). Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: bhaktam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mātrāvat aśanam (मात्रावत् अशनम्; SAT SAT-J.72): ingestion of sufficient quantity of food. Ingestion of sufficient quantity of food which does not cause any disturbance in the body. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: mātrāvat aśanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mātrāvat-āhāraḥ (मात्रावत्-आहारः; SAT SAT-J.73): sufficient quantity of food. Quantity of food which does not cause any disturbance in the body. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: mātrāvat-āhāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: mātrāhīnam (मात्राहीनम्; SAT SAT-J.74): less quantity of food. Those who have weak digestive power & who are sick less quantity of food is advisable. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: mātrāhīnam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rāśiḥ (राशिः; SAT SAT-J.75): quantity. Consists of sarvagraha (total account), and parigraha (individual account) which ascertain the results of the food taken in proper or improper quantity. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: rāśiḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: rukṣānnopacāraḥ (रुक्षान्नोपचारः; SAT SAT-J.76): dry food treatment. Those who have more of fat accumulation in their body, who are unctuous, those suffering from madhumeha, who have more of kapha in body should be treated with dry food. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: rukṣānnopacāraḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: samaśanam (समशनम्; SAT SAT-J.77): taking an admixture of desirable and undesirable food items. Eating green gram (wholesome) and black gram (unwholesome) at a time. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: samaśanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sarvagrahaḥ (सर्वग्रहः; SAT SAT-J.78): accounting of the quantity of the entire food in totality. Considering all the food articles together in meal plate, which may includes cooked cereals, pulses, condiments, drinkables etc. it refers to the whole caloric value of all food articles of meal plate. it is contrast to parigraha. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: sarvagrahaḥ

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sātmyam (सात्म्यम्; SAT SAT-J.79): homologation/ habituation. Daily activities and food which have become habitual to body. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: sātmyam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nātidrutam (नातिद्रुतम्; SAT SAT-J.80): not taking of food in hurry. One should not eat food in hurr, it may leads to improper mixing of food with saliva, indigestion and entry of food in wrong tract. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: nātidrutam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: nātivilambitam (नातिविलम्बितम्; SAT SAT-J.81): not taking of food too slow. One should not eat too slow by this one doesn't get satisfaction, eats more, food becomes cold and is digested irregularly. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: nātivilambitam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: auṣadhiyukta-bhojanam (औषधियुक्त-भोजनम्; SAT SAT-J.82): food mixed with medicine. Those who have aversion for medicine, it should be given mixed with food. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: auṣadhiyukta-bhojanam

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: sātmya-sampat (सात्म्य-सम्पत्; SAT SAT-J.83): excellence of suitability. Excellence or abundance of quality of suitability. Category: daily regimen (dinacaryā).
title: sātmya-sampat

source: NAMASTE portal, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India - Standardised Ayurveda Terminology
text: virudhdāhāraḥ (विरुध्दाहारः; SAT SAT-J.84): antagonistic food. Food which excites the doṣa but do-not eliminate them out of the body and thus becomes inherently antagonistic to the dhātu.
